title: Meyenburg Prize
text:
Meyenburg Prize
The Meyenburg Prize recognizes achievements in cancer research. It is awarded by the Meyenburg Foundation in support of the German Cancer Research Center in Heidelberg. Established in 1981, the annual prize carries an award of €50,000. Several recipients have also received Nobel Prizes in medicine or chemistry, including Andrew Fire, Elizabeth Blackburn, Shinya Yamanaka, Stefan Hell, and Emmanuelle Charpentier. Its first recipient was Werner W. Franke. The 2023/24 prize was awarded to Michel Sadelain of Columbia University in New York. Sadelain was recognized for contributions to cellular immunotherapy, including the development of CAR T-cell approaches to treating cancer. The German Cancer Research Center is described as Germany's largest biomedical research institution.

title: Eric Halvorson — corporate proxy biography, 2004
text:
Eric Halvorson — corporate proxy biography, 2004
Eric H. Halvorson holds a BS in accounting from Bob Jones University and a JD from Duke University School of Law. A certified public accountant, he was a partner at the Milwaukee law firm Godfrey and Kahn from 1976 to 1985. He was executive vice president and chief operating officer of Salem Communications from 1995 to 2000. From 2000 to 2003 he taught business law and accounting at Pepperdine University. He joined Computer Motion’s board in July 2002. In June 2003 he became president and CEO of the art publisher The Thomas Kinkade Company. The corporate proxy statement identifies Intuitive Surgical as the reporting company and sets out the roles of directors and senior management. Its biographical disclosures cover executives’ earlier professional appointments and educational credentials in support of shareholder voting.

title: Gemma (language model)
text:
Gemma (language model)
Gemma is a family of language models developed by Google DeepMind using technology related to Gemini, with specialized models for different uses. The first models appeared in February 2024, followed by Gemma 2 that June and Gemma 3 in March 2025. Specialized variants include the vision-language model PaliGemma and medically oriented MedGemma. Google released Gemma 3 in model sizes of 1B, 4B, 12B and 27B parameters. The 4B, 12B and 27B versions accept both image and text input, while the family supports context windows of up to 128,000 tokens. Google also reports multilingual support for more than 140 languages and provides instruction-tuned as well as pre-trained model variants.

title: Maggie Aderin-Pocock — Royal Institution biography
text:
Maggie Aderin-Pocock — Royal Institution biography
Maggie Aderin-Pocock was born and raised in London and earned a physics BSc at Imperial College London in 1990. She also completed a PhD in mechanical engineering there. From February 2014 she co-presented The Sky at Night with Chris Lintott. She became chancellor of the University of Leicester on March 1, 2023. Early in her career she developed hand-held landmine-detection instruments at the Defence Evaluation and Research Agency. She later managed observation instruments for the Aeolus satellite, which measured wind speeds. Her public-engagement work has also been recognised by the Institute of Physics, which awarded her the Lord Kelvin Medal and Prize in 2020. She served as president of the British Science Association from 2021 to 2022 and is an honorary research associate in UCL's Department of Physics and Astronomy.

title: Vanya Quiñones — Cal State Monterey Bay profile, 2022
text:
Vanya Quiñones — Cal State Monterey Bay profile, 2022
Vanya Quiñones was born in Arecibo, Puerto Rico, and grew up mainly in San Juan. She earned a bachelor’s in biology and master’s in cell biology at the University of Puerto Rico. Her PhD in neurobiology and physiology was from Rutgers University, followed by postdoctoral work at Rockefeller University. After over twenty years at Hunter College, she moved to Pace University as provost in 2018. On August 15, 2022, she began serving as Cal State Monterey Bay’s fourth president. During summers in Arecibo, she spent time on her grandparents’ farm and later described learning the value of collective work there. She initially considered art and pre-medical studies before a science professor invited her to take part in laboratory research. At Rockefeller University, she studied the effect of sex-related biological differences in neuroscience.

title: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications
text:
Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications
The Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications is a research institution in Huairou, Beijing, supported by the Beijing Municipal Government and Tsinghua University. Established on 12 June 2020 as the Beijing Yanqi Lake Institute of Applied Mathematics, it was initiated by mathematician Shing-Tung Yau, who became its first president. Its research spans mathematics, physics, and information science, with groups working on areas such as algebraic geometry, mathematical physics, machine learning, and data science. The institute hosts the International Congress of Basic Science and has more than ten research groups. It also collaborates with universities and research institutions to train doctoral students through joint programs.

title: John Clemens — UCLA faculty biography
text:
John Clemens — UCLA faculty biography
John Clemens earned a BS in biology from Stanford and an MD from Yale, followed by postdoctoral research training in clinical epidemiology at Yale. He was a research scientist at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh from 1983 to 1988. He later headed epidemiology units at the University of Maryland and the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development. He moved to UCLA in 2011 to become professor of epidemiology and founding director of its Center for Global Infectious Diseases. During his later leadership at the International Vaccine Institute, his team developed Shanchol, a killed oral cholera vaccine that was licensed in India in 2009 and received World Health Organization prequalification in September 2011. The vaccine became part of the global oral cholera vaccine stockpile supported by Gavi.

title: NASA Launch Services Program
text:
NASA Launch Services Program
NASA’s Launch Services Program purchases launch services for uncrewed missions and oversees launch integration and preparation. It was established at Kennedy Space Center in 1998 to manage the agency’s expendable launch vehicle missions. The program operates within NASA’s Space Operations Mission Directorate, with Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida and Vandenberg Space Force Base in California serving as its main launch sites. The program also manages spacecraft selected through NASA’s CubeSat Launch Initiative. CubeSats assigned to launches under that initiative are designated Educational Launch of Nanosatellites missions, commonly known as ELaNa. Those missions give students opportunities to gain experience with spacecraft development and the steps required to reach orbit.

title: Columbia — president-designate announcement in January 2026
text:
Columbia — president-designate announcement in January 2026
On January 25, 2026, Columbia University announced Jennifer L. Mnookin as its next president, effective July 1. The appointment concluded a national search by a committee of trustees and faculty that consulted the university community. At the time of her selection, Mnookin served as chancellor of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, a large public research institution. The Madison campus had more than 50,000 students in 13 schools and colleges, including a medical school and affiliated health system. The Columbia trustees’ search involved consultations with students, faculty, staff, alumni and other members of the university community. Her Wisconsin tenure included new research infrastructure and cross-campus programmes involving artificial intelligence.

title: John Ternus — university years
text:
John Ternus — university years
John Ternus graduated from Penn Engineering in 1997 and competed for the university’s varsity swimming team. A former teammate recalled his participation in backstroke and sprint freestyle races, as well as the demanding daily training schedule. A 1994 report in The Daily Pennsylvanian recorded that he won both the 50-meter freestyle and the 200-meter individual medley at a meet. Ternus joined Apple's product design team in 2001 after completing his mechanical-engineering degree. By 2025, he was Apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering and had overseen work across the iPad, iPhone, AirPods and Mac product lines. His responsibilities included Apple's transition from Intel processors to Apple silicon in Mac computers.

title: List of symphony orchestras
text:
List of symphony orchestras
African symphony orchestras include the Cairo Symphony Orchestra in Egypt and the National Symphony Orchestra Ghana. South Africa has the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra, Johannesburg Philharmonic Orchestra and KwaZulu-Natal Philharmonic Orchestra. Other ensembles include the Moroccan Philharmonic Orchestra, the Tunisian Symphony Orchestra and the Orchestre Symphonique Kimbanguiste in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The page's Pan-Asia section lists orchestras in Beijing, Guangzhou, Hangzhou, Harbin, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Xiamen, alongside the China National Symphony Orchestra and the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra. Examples from South and Central America include the Buenos Aires Philharmonic, the Argentine National Symphony and the Olavarria Symphony Orchestra.

title: Paul Thomas Anderson wins best director Oscar for One Battle After Another
text:
Paul Thomas Anderson wins best director Oscar for One Battle After Another
Paul Thomas Anderson won the directing Oscar at the 2026 Academy Awards for One Battle After Another. Earlier that evening, he had received the adapted-screenplay award, making the directing prize his second Oscar. His previous directing nominations were for There Will Be Blood, Phantom Thread and Licorice Pizza. The winning film draws loosely on Thomas Pynchon’s novel Vineland, published in 1990. Leonardo DiCaprio plays a former revolutionary, with Chase Infiniti as his teenage daughter. Anderson had already received directing prizes for the film from the Golden Globes, Baftas and Directors Guild of America. His earlier films include Boogie Nights, Magnolia, Punch-Drunk Love, The Master and Inherent Vice; the last of these was also adapted from a novel by Pynchon.

title: Penguin Random House
text:
Penguin Random House
Penguin Random House is a British-American publishing group formed on 1 July 2013 through the merger of Penguin Books and Random House. It is one of the Big Five English-language publishers. Bertelsmann became its sole owner in 2020, and the integration of its German-language publishing business brought the group to 365 imprints, including 45 from the German-language division. In 2021, the company employed approximately 10,000 people worldwide and published around 15,000 titles a year, encompassing a wide range of genres and formats. The 2013 combination was completed in a transaction valued at £2.4 billion between Bertelsmann and Pearson. The two parent companies initially held 53% and 47% of the merged business, respectively, before Bertelsmann later became its sole owner.

title: Eugene Symphony
text:
Eugene Symphony
The Eugene Symphony is an American orchestra based in Eugene, Oregon, and a resident company of the Hult Center for the Performing Arts. Its concerts take place at the center’s Silva Hall and at Cuthbert Amphitheater near Alton Baker Park. The orchestra attracts approximately 27,000 listeners to its classical and pops performances each year. Its former music directors include Marin Alsop, Miguel Harth Bedoya, Giancarlo Guerrero, Danial Rachev and Francesco Lecce-Chong. Alex Prior was named music director in 2025. The orchestra was founded in 1965 by a small group of musicians and supporters. Its founding idea emerged during a living-room rehearsal involving co-founder and oboist Caroline Boekelheide, before the ensemble developed into a resident company in Eugene.

title: Enrico Lopez-Yañez — NIH orchestra programme, December 2014
text:
Enrico Lopez-Yañez — NIH orchestra programme, December 2014
A December 2014 programme described Enrico Lopez-Yañez as completing an MM in orchestral conducting at the University of Maryland with Professor James Ross. He had earned his baccalaureate and a master’s in music at UCLA, studying trumpet with Jens Lindemann and graduating summa cum laude. He had been invited to the Castleton Festival as a conducting associate to study with Lorin Maazel. The programme also listed his assistant-conductor work with the Capital City Symphony in Washington, DC, and his music directorship of Maryland’s Repertoire Orchestra. The orchestra was founded in 1996 as an all-volunteer group bringing together NIH staff and musicians from the surrounding community. It presents two concerts each year and also performs outreach programs. Donations from its concerts support NIH-related charities, including the Children's Inn, the Clinical Center's patient emergency fund, and Special Love's camp for young people affected by cancer.

title: Memorial to Thomas R. McGetchin 1936–1979
text:
Memorial to Thomas R. McGetchin 1936–1979
Tom McGetchin was born in La Jolla, California, on 31 July 1936. His father worked as a surveyor, and McGetchin helped him as a child. He studied geology at Occidental College, where a senior paper about Mars encouraged his interest in planetary science. After a master’s degree at Brown, he earned his doctorate at Caltech in 1968, studying Utah’s Moses Rock kimberlite dike with Lee Silver and Gene Shoemaker. His childhood on the California coast left him with a lasting love of the sea and sailing. After completing his doctorate, he served from 1967 to 1969 as an assistant professor of geophysics at the Air Force Institute of Technology. He then joined MIT, where he taught from 1969 to 1974 and guided students in field and laboratory studies of volcanoes. Their methods included mapping, sample collection, seismology, high-speed photography of volcanic ejecta, and infrared imaging. He later organized a broad Geosciences Group at Los Alamos before directing the Lunar Science Institute, which he helped expand into the Lunar and Planetary Institute.

title: Simon & Schuster
text:
Simon & Schuster
Simon & Schuster is an American publishing house founded in New York City in 1924 by Richard L. Simon and M. Lincoln Schuster. It is one of the Big Five English-language publishers, alongside companies including Penguin Random House and HarperCollins. The investment firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts has owned the company since 2023. The company began after Simon's aunt asked whether a book of New York World crossword puzzles was available; finding none, Simon and Schuster decided to publish one. In 1939, the publisher backed Pocket Books, an early American paperback publisher. In 1942, it joined Western Publishing in launching the Little Golden Books series, extending its work beyond the crossword-puzzle books that had prompted its creation.

title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: Announcing our latest Gemini AI model
text:
Gemini 3.1 Pro: Announcing our latest Gemini AI model
Google announced Gemini 3.1 Pro on 19 February 2026, extending the reasoning capabilities of the Gemini 3 series. Its rollout covered developer tools, enterprise services and consumer products, including the Gemini app and NotebookLM. The model recorded a verified score of 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2, a benchmark involving unfamiliar logic patterns. Google described applications ranging from animated SVG generation to interactive design and the synthesis of complex data. For developers, the preview was made available through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini CLI, Google Antigravity and Android Studio. Enterprise access was listed through Vertex AI and Gemini Enterprise. Google said the ARC-AGI-2 result was more than twice the score reported for Gemini 3 Pro.

title: How Scrappy Cryptominer CoreWeave Transformed Into the Multibillion-Dollar Backbone of the AI Boom
text:
How Scrappy Cryptominer CoreWeave Transformed Into the Multibillion-Dollar Backbone of the AI Boom
CoreWeave’s Plano campus covers about 450,000 square feet and cost roughly $1.6 billion, according to WIRED’s May 2024 report. The Plano, Texas, facility hosts a supercomputer data center for NVIDIA. CoreWeave also operated an Oregon site serving business-chatbot company Inflection AI, while other locations supplied GPU capacity to multiple customers, including Stability AI and Anlatan. In 2016, its founders began purchasing graphics processors for cryptocurrency mining before developing a larger hardware-rental business. After cryptocurrency prices fell, the business shifted toward specialist GPU cloud services for visual-effects studios and artificial-intelligence developers. The arrival of generative AI increased demand for the GPUs, and the company later served clients including Microsoft and Stability AI.

title: Claudio Abbado
text:
Claudio Abbado
Claudio Abbado was an Italian conductor whose posts included music director of La Scala and principal conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic and London Symphony Orchestra. He founded the Lucerne Festival Orchestra and Mahler Chamber Orchestra and directed the European Union Youth Orchestra. A recipient of the Ernst von Siemens Music Prize, he was also appointed an Italian senator for life. Abbado first appeared with the Berlin Philharmonic in December 1966 and returned as a guest conductor 33 times before the orchestra selected him as principal conductor in 1989. During his tenure, he pursued a more transparent orchestral sound and organized thematic concert cycles around subjects such as Prometheus, Faust and Shakespeare. He also presented concert performances of operas by Mussorgsky, Verdi, Wagner and Alban Berg, and resigned from the principal-conductor post in 2002.

title: Longhouse, Publishers & Booksellers - Home
text:
Longhouse, Publishers & Booksellers - Home
Longhouse publishes poetry in handmade formats assembled by Bob Arnold and Susan at their home along the Green River near Brattleboro, Vermont. Its publications include American poetry and translations from languages such as Persian, Japanese, Arabic, Korean, and Chinese. Among its distinctive formats are small foldouts with colored covers and paper bands that hold them closed. Opening these chaplets reveals narrow sheets of poems, translations, or occasional essays arranged across folded panels. The press also makes postcards, bookmarks, and folded mailing sheets, many sized for an ordinary envelope. Alongside these smaller pieces, it produces full-length books once or twice a year by Bob or other poets associated with the press.

title: Kelsey Martin — UCLA profile published in 2016
text:
Kelsey Martin — UCLA profile published in 2016
Kelsey Martin majored in English and American language and literature at Harvard University. She spent two and a half years as a Peace Corps volunteer in Bibanga, Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of Congo. She later entered Yale’s MD/PhD programme and graduated in 1992. She undertook postdoctoral research with Eric Kandel at Columbia University. She joined UCLA in 1999 as an assistant professor in psychiatry and biological chemistry. In September 2015 she became interim dean of UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. In Bibanga, she wrote grants to fund measles vaccinations; the campaign was followed by a year without measles outbreaks or infant deaths in the village. The experience prompted her to move from literature toward medicine, and she later became permanent dean of the David Geffen School of Medicine in 2016.

title: Nashville Symphony — music director appointed in February 2026
text:
Nashville Symphony — music director appointed in February 2026
On February 11, 2026, the Nashville Symphony announced Leonard Slatkin as its music director for three years through the 2028/29 season. His engagement would begin in August 2026 and continue through July 2029. Slatkin had served as the orchestra’s Music Advisor from 2006 to 2009 and returned to that advisory role in 2025. The 2026–27 season was planned around the twentieth anniversary of Schermerhorn Symphony Center and the orchestra’s eightieth anniversary. He was scheduled to lead six of the fourteen Classical Series programmes during his first season in charge. His brief also included artistic direction of education and community engagement activities.

title: OptiSat
text:
OptiSat
OptiSat is a Greek technology demonstration satellite developed by Planetek Hellas. The 6U CubeSat tests laser communications and onboard data processing, using a SCOT20 laser terminal made by Germany’s TESAT. It also tests machine-learning image processing intended to identify cloud-free ground stations for optical communication. Planetek reported that the satellite launched on 30 March 2026 from Vandenberg Space Force Base aboard a Falcon 9 rocket on SpaceX's Transporter-16 mission. The mission was carried out under contract with the European Space Agency as part of Greece's National Microsatellite Programme. The company said the optical terminal is intended to support data rates of up to 1 Gbps, while processing Earth-observation data in orbit can shorten the time between image acquisition and usable information.

title: John Pyle — education and scientific career
text:
John Pyle — education and scientific career
John Adrian Pyle was born on April 4, 1951. He attended De La Salle College in Salford and earned a physics BSc at Durham University. He received his DPhil at Jesus College, Oxford, in 1978. He has been a fellow of St Catharine’s College, Cambridge. He took the 1920 Chair of Physical Chemistry at Cambridge in 2007. He received a CBE in the 2017 New Year Honours for services to atmospheric chemistry and environmental science. His research uses numerical models, often run on supercomputers, to examine processes shaping the atmosphere and its evolution. The work includes studying rapid ozone depletion in polar spring, changes in the troposphere's ability to remove pollution, and lightweight gas-chromatography instruments for measuring halocarbons from balloons and high-altitude research aircraft.

title: Hugues de Thé — degrees and earlier appointments
text:
Hugues de Thé — degrees and earlier appointments
Hugues de Thé received an MD from Paris Descartes University in 1989 and a PhD from Pierre et Marie Curie University in 1990. He had received a master's degree in biochemistry at Pierre et Marie Curie University in 1983. His medical research residency at Institut Pasteur from 1984 to 1988 was supervised by Pierre Tiollais. From 1995 to 2014 he was professor of biochemistry at Paris Diderot University. His research helped characterize PML/RARA, the fusion gene that drives acute promyelocytic leukemia. He showed that arsenic and retinoic acid act on different parts of the fusion protein and promote its degradation. Work with animal models demonstrated that combining the two agents can restore PML nuclear bodies and produce durable cures, providing a foundation for targeted treatment of this leukemia.

title: Trinity International University — presidential appointment in 2026
text:
Trinity International University — presidential appointment in 2026
On February 5, 2026, Trinity International University announced Eric Halvorson as its 18th president, an appointment effective January 27. The Board of Regents voted unanimously, and Halvorson would continue serving as dean of Trinity Law School. Halvorson had previously served as dean of Trinity Law School from 2016 to 2019 and returned to the same position in 2022. The preceding interim president, David Pao, had overseen the transfer of Trinity Evangelical Divinity School to Trinity Western University. His presidential portfolio included online programmes and a degree programme for inmates at Fox Lake Correctional Institution. The announcement also described a background in corporate law, accounting and the management of public companies.

title: Neil Ryan
text:
Neil Ryan
Neil Ryan is an English football coach and former defender, and the son of former player Jimmy Ryan. He began at Luton Town in 1991, turned professional in 1994, and moved to the United States after his Luton contract ended the following year. His American clubs included Richmond Kickers, Worcester Wildfire, Wichita Wings, and Portland Timbers. Returning to England in November 2001, he joined Altrincham and made his debut the following month. After working through Manchester United’s academy age groups, he became the club’s under-18 head coach in July 2018. He joined England’s national coaching staff in May 2022 after 19 years at Manchester United.

title: Space One
text:
Space One
Space One is a Japanese aerospace company developing the KAIROS rocket for launching small satellites. It was founded in July 2018 with investment from Canon Electronics, IHI Aerospace, Shimizu Corporation and the Development Bank of Japan. Shimizu built its Spaceport Kii launch site in Kushimoto, Wakayama, between 2019 and 2021, creating Japan’s first private-sector spaceport. KAIROS failed on its first flight in March 2024 and again on its second flight in December that year. The second mission had been intended to carry five satellites, comprising four CubeSats and one microsatellite. Space One says Spaceport Kii is in Kushimoto, Wakayama Prefecture, on the southern tip of Honshu, with a launch corridor open to the south and east. Its published service capability includes placing a 150-kilogram payload into a 500-kilometre sun-synchronous orbit. The company describes a target of completing a primary-payload launch within 12 months of contract and building toward 20 launches per year by the end of the decade.

title: Artemis program
text:
Artemis program
Artemis is NASA’s lunar exploration program, established in 2017 to return people to the Moon and develop a permanent base there. Its main systems include the Space Launch System rocket, the Orion spacecraft and a Human Landing System being developed by private contractors. SLS incorporates hardware derived from the Space Shuttle, including RS-25 engines and solid rocket boosters, while Orion originated in the canceled Constellation program. The uncrewed Artemis I mission sent Orion into lunar orbit in 2022. NASA describes Artemis as a sequence of increasingly difficult missions that use lunar exploration for scientific discovery and economic benefits while preparing for future crewed missions to Mars. Artemis I served as an integrated test of the SLS rocket, Orion spacecraft and Kennedy Space Center ground systems; it evaluated Orion without astronauts or the life-support equipment planned for later crewed missions.

title: Karen Maxwell — Toronto faculty biography
text:
Karen Maxwell — Toronto faculty biography
Karen Maxwell completed her PhD in molecular genetics at the University of Toronto, working in Marvin Gold's laboratory on the assembly of bacteriophage lambda. Her postdoctoral work at the Ontario Centre for Structural Genomics focused on phage structural genomics. She subsequently held a research associate position at the Donnelly Centre. She joined the Department of Biochemistry as an assistant professor in 2016. Her research examines the evolutionary contest between bacteriophages and the bacteria they infect. One project studies poorly characterized phage genes, sometimes called viral dark matter, in viruses that infect Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Her group also investigates bacterial anti-phage defenses and the countermeasures viruses develop, with a long-term goal of engineering phages to treat antibiotic-resistant infections. She holds a Canada Research Chair in Bacteriophage Biology and Therapeutics.

title: Álvaro Arbeloa — Liverpool playing career
text:
Álvaro Arbeloa — Liverpool playing career
Álvaro Arbeloa joined Liverpool from Deportivo La Coruna in January 2007, recruited by Rafael Benitez to challenge Steve Finnan at right-back. His debut came as a substitute against Newcastle United on February 10; his first start followed at Camp Nou against Barcelona. He made 98 appearances and scored twice for Liverpool between 2007 and 2009. He returned to Real Madrid in the summer of 2009 after Glen Johnson arrived at Liverpool. Liverpool used Arbeloa in the unfamiliar left-back position against Barcelona in the 2007 Champions League, where he helped contain Lionel Messi. He made his senior debut for Spain in March 2008 and later took part in the squad that won that year’s European Championship.

title: Kang Woo-suk
text:
Kang Woo-suk
Kang Woo-suk is a South Korean producer and director born in Gyeongsan on 10 November 1960. He initially directed comedies before the commercial success of Two Cops in 1993. His later films include Silmido and the three Public Enemy films: Public Enemy, Another Public Enemy and Public Enemy Returns. Following Two Cops, he established Cinema Service as a production and distribution company. The business grew into one of South Korea’s largest film distributors. Kang left its presidency in 2005, saying that he wanted to devote more time to his own films. The Korean Film Council notes that seven of his films released in the 2000s, beginning with Public Enemy, each attracted at least three million viewers in South Korea. Silmido was the first Korean film to reach ten million admissions, while the Public Enemy story continued through sequels. His production company began as Kang Woo-suk Production in 1993 and was renamed Cinema Service in 1995.

title: NVIDIA and CoreWeave Strengthen Collaboration to Accelerate Buildout of AI Factories
text:
NVIDIA and CoreWeave Strengthen Collaboration to Accelerate Buildout of AI Factories
NVIDIA announced on 26 January 2026 that it had invested $2 billion in CoreWeave’s Class A common stock at $87.20 per share. The companies also expanded their collaboration to support CoreWeave’s construction of more than five gigawatts of AI factories by 2030. Their plans included closer software integration and the early deployment of successive NVIDIA computing architectures, including Rubin, Vera CPUs and BlueField storage systems. NVIDIA’s financial resources would also help CoreWeave secure land, power and buildings for the facilities. The companies planned to support construction of more than five gigawatts of AI-factory capacity by 2030. Their technology collaboration included early use of NVIDIA Vera processors, Rubin computing architecture and BlueField storage systems. They also planned to test software called SUNK and CoreWeave Mission Control for possible inclusion in reference architectures.

title: Jais (language model)
text:
Jais (language model)
Jais is an open-source language model introduced in August 2023 to improve Arabic text generation. It was developed by G42, the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, and Cerebras Systems, using English as well as Arabic training data. Named after Jebel Jais, the highest mountain in the United Arab Emirates, it addresses the limited representation of Arabic in generative artificial intelligence. The initial release contained 13 billion parameters and was trained on a 395-billion-token corpus combining Arabic and English. The project partners trained the model on Condor Galaxy, a supercomputer built by G42 and Cerebras. The launch announcement said the model was intended to expand access to generative AI for more than 400 million Arabic speakers and to encourage further research on languages underrepresented in mainstream AI.

title: Rosa Rademakers — VIB conference biography
text:
Rosa Rademakers — VIB conference biography
Rosa Rademakers received a BSc in biology in 1997 and an MSc in biochemistry in 1999 at the University of Antwerp. She completed her PhD there in 2004 and continued with postdoctoral studies. In 2005 she moved to the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida. She became a Mayo neuroscience faculty member in 2007 and a full professor in 2014. Her laboratory combines genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic and proteomic analyses of patient brain tissue to investigate genetic factors associated with frontotemporal dementia. The VIB profile credits her group with identifying progranulin as the first causal gene implicated in FTD and with discovering C9ORF72 repeat expansions as a cause of ALS and FTD in 2011. She also leads international collaborations studying why symptoms and disease progression vary among people who carry known mutations. The profile records more than 400 peer-reviewed publications and awards including the 2016 Potamkin Prize.

title: Dublin Literary Award
text:
Dublin Literary Award
The Dublin Literary Award is an annual prize for a novel written in English or published in English translation, sponsored by Dublin City Council. First awarded in 1996, it was originally known as the International IMPAC Dublin Literary Award. The prize is worth €100,000; when a translated novel wins, the author receives €75,000 and the translator €25,000. Public libraries around the world nominate books, and an international judging panel selects the shortlist and winner. The first recipient was David Malouf for Remembering Babylon, an English-language novel, and the international judging panel changes from year to year. The award's judging calendar follows a defined sequence: an international panel first selects a longlist of up to 20 novels, then reduces it to a six-book shortlist. The winner is announced at a ceremony held during the International Literature Festival Dublin in May. Dublin City Libraries administer the process, while Dublin City Council has been the sole sponsor since 2015.

title: Leroy and Liam Rosenior
text:
Leroy and Liam Rosenior
Liam Rosenior is the son of former footballer Leroy Rosenior. In a November 2006 interview, Liam was playing for Fulham in the Premiership while Leroy managed Brentford in League One. Their careers had overlapped at Bristol City, where Liam joined the youth system while his father worked in coaching, and at Torquay, where Leroy signed him on loan. Both discussed the pressure that their family relationship had placed on the younger player. Liam said the three months at Torquay had taught him more than any other period of his career. Leroy recalled that his son had helped Torquay win promotion during that loan.

title: New Frontiers program
text:
New Frontiers program
NASA’s New Frontiers program funds planetary missions larger than those in its Discovery program but smaller than flagship projects. Scientists from the United States and other countries can submit proposals, with missions led by principal investigators. New Horizons launched in 2006 and reached Pluto in 2015. Juno departed in 2011 and entered orbit around Jupiter in 2016. OSIRIS-REx launched toward the asteroid Bennu in September 2016, studied it between 2018 and 2021, and returned samples to Earth in 2023. On 27 June 2019, NASA selected Dragonfly as the fourth New Frontiers mission, continuing the program’s focus on medium-scale exploration of the Solar System.

title: Albert Maguire — Helen Keller Foundation biography
text:
Albert Maguire — Helen Keller Foundation biography
Albert Maguire graduated summa cum laude with a BS in psychology from Princeton University. He earned his MD at Harvard Medical School and completed a surgery internship at Yale University School of Medicine. His ophthalmology residency was at the Wilmer Institute, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, where he became chief resident. He completed a medical and surgical retinal fellowship at William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak, Michigan. He was recruited to the University of Pennsylvania and Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia in 1992. At the University of Pennsylvania and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, his work moved from laboratory studies toward clinical testing. He served as principal investigator for the trials that supported the first United States Food and Drug Administration approval of an in vivo gene-therapy product, Luxturna, in 2017. The foundation also describes his role in trials for choroideremia and neovascular age-related macular degeneration, as well as a clinical study using CRISPR-Cas gene editing for congenital blindness. He has helped develop surgical training programmes for retinal gene-therapy procedures.

title: Developer Challenges on Large Language Models: A Study of Stack Overflow and OpenAI Developer Forum Posts
text:
Developer Challenges on Large Language Models: A Study of Stack Overflow and OpenAI Developer Forum Posts
A study of language-model developers’ discussions examined posts on Stack Overflow and the OpenAI Developer Forum using BERTopic. The researchers identified nine categories of challenges on Stack Overflow and 17 on the OpenAI forum. Stack Overflow discussions tended to seek implementation advice, whereas the OpenAI forum placed more emphasis on troubleshooting, particularly API and functionality problems. Many questions remained unresolved, including 79.03 percent of the Stack Overflow posts studied. Complex topics involving indexing, GPU use, agents and tools also attracted long response times, while mobile-development and security questions generally received quicker resolutions. The paper reports a dataset of 8,593 Stack Overflow posts and 26,474 questions from the OpenAI Developer Forum. For preprocessing, the authors used both titles and post bodies, removed quoted text, HTML, links and code snippets, and filtered common stopwords. They also manually inspected random samples of at least 30 posts per topic when assigning topic labels.

title: Development of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
text:
Development of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was developed by Sandfall Interactive. The production was built with Unreal Engine 5, and the developers used tools such as Blueprint and MetaHuman in their workflow. A March 2025 developer interview described a core team of fewer than 30 people working between Montpellier and Paris. The independent studio was founded in France in 2020 and specialises in character-driven games for personal computers and consoles. The game takes place in a fantasy setting influenced by the French Belle Époque and uses turn-based battles with real-time dodging and counterattacks. Co-founder Tom Guillermin described how engine features including Lumen and Nanite supported environments and character presentation.

title: NAS Award in Chemical Sciences
text:
NAS Award in Chemical Sciences
Benjamin F. Cravatt of Scripps Research Institute received the 2026 NAS Award in Chemical Sciences. His development of activity-based protein profiling allowed researchers to map enzyme activity in native proteomes and examine its regulation in development and disease. His research also produced chemical probes and therapeutic approaches for modifying protein function. He received the award at the Academy’s annual meeting on 26 April; it includes a medal and $15,000. The National Academy of Sciences established the award in 1978, and it was first presented in 1979 to Linus Pauling for work explaining the structural properties of molecules. Occidental Petroleum Corporation supported the award from its establishment through 1996; the Merck Company Foundation became its sponsor in 1999. The Academy presents the distinction annually with a medal and a monetary award. Its stated purpose links advances in chemical sciences with a broader contribution to understanding the natural sciences and benefiting humanity.

title: Dr Benjamin Cravatt
text:
Dr Benjamin Cravatt
Benjamin Cravatt studied at Stanford University, earning undergraduate degrees in biological sciences and history. He completed his doctorate at the Scripps Research Institute in 1996 and joined its faculty the following year. His research group develops chemical proteomic methods for protein and drug discovery, using them to investigate biochemical pathways involved in human physiology and disease. His laboratory develops chemical proteomic technologies that can be applied at a broad scale to protein and drug discovery. The Cancer Grand Challenges profile describes this work as an effort to characterize biochemical pathways involved in human physiology and disease. Cravatt completed both a BS in biological sciences and a BA in history at Stanford before earning his PhD at Scripps in 1996. The profile lists honours including the Wolf Prize in Chemistry and membership in the National Academies of Medicine and Sciences.

title: Amazon Leo
text:
Amazon Leo
Amazon Leo is an Amazon subsidiary established in 2019 to develop a satellite network for low-latency broadband. Originally called Project Kuiper, after the Kuiper belt, it received its current name in November 2025. The Federal Communications Commission authorized a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit satellites in July 2020. Service was expected to begin once an initial deployment of 578 satellites was in orbit, as part of a plan divided into five phases. Amazon's deployment plan relies on launch agreements with Arianespace, Blue Origin, SpaceX and United Launch Alliance. The network is designed around more than 3,000 low-Earth-orbit satellites linked by optical connections and a ground network of gateway stations and fiber. Customer terminals are offered in three forms: Leo Nano, Leo Pro and Leo Ultra.

title: Alex Filippenko — Chandra biography
text:
Alex Filippenko — Chandra biography
Alex Filippenko received a BA in physics from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 1979 and a PhD in astronomy from Caltech in 1984. He subsequently became a Miller Fellow at the University of California, Berkeley, joining its faculty in 1986. He has served as president of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific and as a councilor of the American Astronomical Society. He also produced introductory astronomy courses with The Teaching Company. His observational work uses facilities including the Hubble Space Telescope and the Keck 10-metre telescopes. The Chandra biography identifies exploding stars, active galaxies, black holes, gamma-ray bursts and the expansion of the universe among his main research areas. It also notes that he helped lead the High-Redshift Supernova Search Team, whose discovery of the universe's accelerated expansion was selected by Science editors as the leading scientific breakthrough of 1998. By the time of that biography, he had authored more than 430 published articles.

title: Xiaomi MiMo
text:
Xiaomi MiMo
MiMo is Xiaomi’s family of large language models, introduced in April 2025 with the seven-billion-parameter MiMo-7B. The models emphasize mathematical reasoning and code generation, with training methods that include multi-token prediction and reinforcement learning. Xiaomi provides developer access through an API and uses the family within its Human x Car x Home ecosystem. The original base model was pretrained on roughly 25 trillion tokens drawn from websites, academic papers, books and synthetic reasoning material. A subsequent version underwent supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using 130,000 mathematics and coding problems. Later versions extended the model family: MiMo-V2-Flash was released in December 2025 with 309 billion parameters, while MiMo-V2-Pro followed in March 2026 with one trillion parameters.

title: Janrain
text:
Janrain
Janrain was a customer identity and profile management software company based in Portland, Oregon. Larry Drebes founded it there in 2002, and its name referred to Portland’s wet January weather. Drebes helped develop OpenID, a decentralized authentication protocol. Janrain was a founding member of the OpenID Foundation and advocated the use of OpenID for online authentication. Akamai acquired the company in January 2019. Janrain raised US$3.25 million in December 2009 from DFJ Frontier, RPM Ventures and Anthem Venture Partners. In August 2011 it announced a US$15.5 million funding round led by Emergence Capital Partners, bringing its reported funding total at that point to US$18.7 million.

title: Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute
text:
Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute
The Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute is an independent nonprofit research institution on the University of California, Berkeley campus. Previously known as the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute, it was founded in September 1982 by Shiing-Shen Chern, Calvin Moore and Isadore Singer. Chern became its first director, Moore its deputy director and Singer the inaugural chair of its Scientific Advisory Committee. The institute moved to 17 Gauss Way in the Berkeley Hills in April 1985. It adopted its current name after receiving a $70 million gift in 2022 from James and Marilyn Simons and Henry and Marsha Laufer. Its funding sources include the National Science Foundation, private foundations, corporations, individual donors and 110 academic sponsor universities and institutions in the United States and internationally.

title: Weierstrass Institute
text:
Weierstrass Institute
The Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics conducts research in pure and applied mathematics in Berlin’s Mitte district. It belongs to the Forschungsverbund Berlin and the Leibniz Association, and has hosted the International Mathematical Union’s secretariat since February 2011. The institute was established on January 1, 1992, following a recommendation of the German Council of Science and Humanities. It developed from the former East German Academy of Sciences’ mathematics institute and is named after the mathematician Karl Weierstrass. The institute first operated as the Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics, an independent part of the Research Association Berlin. It adopted the Weierstrass Institute name in 1994 and became host of the German Mathematical Society that year.

title: Apellis Pharmaceuticals — 2017 IPO pricing
text:
Apellis Pharmaceuticals — 2017 IPO pricing
On November 8, 2017, Apellis Pharmaceuticals priced an IPO of 10,714,000 common shares at $14 each, for approximately $150 million in gross proceeds before discounts, commissions and expenses. Underwriters received a 30-day option for up to 1,607,100 additional shares. Trading was expected to begin on November 9, 2017 on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under APLS. The offering was expected to close on November 13, 2017, subject to customary conditions. Citigroup, J.P. Morgan and Evercore ISI were joint book-running managers. The SEC declared the offering registration statement effective on November 8, 2017. Apellis said it was offering all of the shares included in the IPO.

title: Okta, Inc.
text:
Okta, Inc.
Okta is an identity and access management business headquartered in San Francisco. Its cloud services handle user authentication and help developers add identity controls to applications, websites and connected devices. The company’s single-sign-on service lets users access several systems through one login, and it also sells authentication services for application programming interfaces. Todd McKinnon and Frederic Kerrest, formerly colleagues at Salesforce, founded the company as SaaSure in 2009. They changed its name to Okta the following year, borrowing a meteorological term for cloud cover. Okta’s services run on Amazon Web Services infrastructure, and the company held its initial public offering in 2017.

title: 2024–25 Premier League
text:
2024–25 Premier League
The 2024–25 Premier League was the competition’s 33rd season and the 126th season of top-flight football in England. Liverpool won the title with four matches remaining, ending Manchester City’s run of four consecutive championships and equalling Manchester United’s total of 20 English league titles. The fixture list, released on June 18, 2024, contained 33 weekend rounds, four midweek rounds and one Bank Holiday matchweek. It was the final season with Nike as the league’s match-ball supplier, before Puma took over for 2025–26. By the final day, the league had recorded 1,091 goals, the second-highest total in any 38-game Premier League season at that point. Mohamed Salah had scored 28 goals and registered 46 goal involvements after 37 matches.

title: United Launch Alliance
text:
United Launch Alliance
United Launch Alliance is an American rocket-launch company established in December 2006 by Lockheed Martin Space and Boeing Defense, Space & Security. It inherited the Atlas V and Delta rocket families from its parent companies. ULA began developing their replacement, Vulcan Centaur, in 2014; its first flight took place in January 2024. The company serves NASA, the Department of Defense and commercial customers. ULA offers Vulcan in four standard configurations with zero, two, four or six solid rocket boosters. The Centaur V upper stage is designed for long-duration operation and complex orbital insertions, allowing the vehicle to serve national-security, civil and commercial missions.

title: Jean Bennett — Yale honorary degree biography
text:
Jean Bennett — Yale honorary degree biography
Jean Bennett was born and raised in New Haven. She graduated from Yale College in 1976 with an honours BS in biology, studying with cell biologist Joseph Gall. She earned a PhD in zoology and cell and developmental biology at the University of California, Berkeley in 1980. She received her MD from Harvard Medical School in 1986. Her postdoctoral fellowships were at UC San Francisco, Yale’s Department of Human Genetics and Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. In 1992 she joined the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania. With her husband and colleagues, Bennett developed a gene therapy for Leber congenital amaurosis, a hereditary condition that causes early-onset and progressive vision loss. The treatment became the first gene therapy approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in 2017, after earlier testing in puppies with inherited blindness restored their sight.

title: Mikel Arteta
text:
Mikel Arteta
Mikel Arteta Amatriain, born on 26 March 1982, is a Spanish football manager and former midfielder. He began his senior career at Barcelona in 1999, then moved to Paris Saint-Germain on loan after finding first-team opportunities limited. He joined Rangers in 2002 and won the Scottish league and league cup in his first season. Following a spell at Real Sociedad, he moved to Everton in 2005 and twice became the club’s Player of the Season. Arteta joined Arsenal in 2011, won two FA Cups and retired in 2016. He represented Spain at youth level but never played for its senior national team.

title: Sophie Adenot
text:
Sophie Adenot
Sophie Adenot was born on July 5, 1982, in Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire, Burgundy, France. Her early interest in aviation drew on her grandfather’s work as an aircraft mechanic and on watching astronaut Claudie Haigneré’s 1996 launch to the Mir space station. Adenot studied engineering at ISAE-SUPAERO, specializing in the flight dynamics of aircraft and spacecraft, and received her degree in 2004. That year she also earned a master’s degree in human factors engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, studying adaptation to artificial gravity. She joined the French Air Force in 2005 for military and initial flying training, then qualified as a helicopter test pilot in 2018 at the Empire Test Pilots’ School in Boscombe Down. The European Space Agency reports that she has logged 3,000 flight hours across 22 helicopter types.

title: List of NASA missions
text:
List of NASA missions
NASA’s missions include crewed spaceflight programs and robotic exploration, with a history extending from the agency’s establishment in 1958. Mercury was the first United States program to send people into space, followed by Gemini, which developed rendezvous and spacewalking techniques. Apollo landed the first humans on the Moon, while Skylab became the first American space station. The Apollo–Soyuz Test Project was a joint mission with the Soviet Union in 1975. The Space Shuttle program launched 135 crewed missions between its first flight in 1981 and its retirement in 2011. Apollo 1 never reached launch: a preflight cabin fire in January 1967 killed astronauts Virgil Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee. The Space Shuttle Columbia was lost during re-entry on 1 February 2003 after a 16-day mission that carried more than 80 international research experiments.

title: Leonard Slatkin — Pittsburgh Symphony biography for 2017–18
text:
Leonard Slatkin — Pittsburgh Symphony biography for 2017–18
Leonard Slatkin was born in Los Angeles to violinist-conductor Felix Slatkin and cellist Eleanor Aller, founders of the Hollywood String Quartet. He began on the violin, studying conducting with his father, Walter Susskind at Aspen, and Jean Morel at Juilliard. His 2017–18 biography named his wife as composer Cindy McTee and his home as Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. It described his second book, Leading Tones: Reflections on Music, Musicians, and the Music Industry. As principal guest conductor of the Minnesota Orchestra, he founded its annual Sommerfest in Minneapolis. Slatkin led the Detroit Symphony Orchestra for a decade and later held an honorary music-director position with the Orchestre National de Lyon. His recorded output includes complete symphony cycles by Beethoven, Brahms and Tchaikovsky with Detroit. He has received several Grammy awards and the National Medal of Arts.

title: Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics
text:
Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics
Roman Bezrukavnikov of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology received the 2026 Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics. His work in geometric representation theory and algebraic geometry developed new tools and resolved questions about modular representations of semisimple Lie algebras. The prize recognises contributions by a mathematician in mid-career and carries a $20,000 award, given every two years. Bezrukavnikov accepted it on 26 April at the 163rd annual meeting of the National Academy of Sciences. The National Academy of Sciences renamed the prize in honour of Maryam Mirzakhani, the Stanford mathematician who became the first woman to receive the Fields Medal. The prize was originally established in 1988 by the American Mathematical Society to mark its centennial. Funding from the Simons Foundation and other benefactors supports the biennial award. The Academy describes it as a distinction for exceptional contributions to the mathematical sciences by a mid-career mathematician, rather than a prize restricted to one mathematical specialty.

title: Sven-Göran Eriksson
text:
Sven-Göran Eriksson
Sven-Göran Eriksson was a Swedish football player and manager who lived from 1948 to 2024. He played at right-back before moving into coaching. Between 1977 and 2001, his club sides in Sweden, Portugal and Italy won eighteen trophies. His European honors included the 1982 UEFA Cup and the final UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup in 1999, when he also won the UEFA Super Cup. He later managed England, Mexico, the Philippines and Ivory Coast, as well as Manchester City and Leicester City. Born in Sunne, he grew up in Torsby, both in Värmland, Sweden. UEFA records that he became the first foreign manager of England's national team in 2001. England reached the quarter-finals at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups and at EURO 2004 during his tenure. His earlier club achievements included the 1990 European Cup final with Benfica and the 2000 Serie A title with Lazio.

title: Robert Eggers
text:
Robert Eggers
Robert Eggers is an American filmmaker born in New York City on July 7, 1983. He wrote and directed The Witch, The Lighthouse, The Northman and Nosferatu, films that combine historical settings with gothic horror, folklore or mythology. His family moved to Lee, New Hampshire, in 1990 after his stepfather became a provost at the University of New Hampshire. Eggers returned to New York in 2001 to attend the American Musical and Dramatic Academy, where he developed his interests in theatre and filmmaking. Before making features, Eggers worked in experimental and street theatre in New York. His early short films included the silent, black-and-white Hansel and Gretel (2007) and a 2008 adaptation of The Tell-Tale Heart that used puppetry. For The Witch, he favored practical, in-camera effects and period-specific language over contemporary visual-effects conventions.

title: List of football clubs in Spain
text:
List of football clubs in Spain
Spain’s men’s football clubs compete in a league system overseen by the Royal Spanish Football Federation, founded in 1909 and affiliated with FIFA and UEFA. La Liga is the highest division, above the Segunda División and Primera Federación. Madrid clubs include Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid and Rayo Vallecano, while Barcelona is home to Barcelona and Espanyol. Athletic Bilbao plays at San Mamés, Celta Vigo at Balaídos, and Real Sociedad at Anoeta in San Sebastián. Other clubs listed in the top division include Sevilla and Real Betis in Seville, Valencia in Valencia, and Villarreal in Villarreal. Real Madrid was founded in 1902 and Barcelona in 1899.

title: Netflix — InterPositive acquisition and advisory appointment
text:
Netflix — InterPositive acquisition and advisory appointment
On March 5, 2026, Netflix announced that filmmaker Ben Affleck would join it as a senior adviser as part of its acquisition of InterPositive. Affleck founded InterPositive to develop AI tools for filmmakers and the production process. The acquisition would bring the company's entire team into Netflix. The announcement described an approach intended to preserve creative choice, with technology supporting the judgment of the people making films rather than replacing it. The acquisition brought InterPositive’s whole team to Netflix and gave its founder a new senior-advisory role. InterPositive’s AI tools were developed using controlled soundstage footage to reproduce practical production conditions. The project aimed to give cinematographers and directors more detailed control over technical aspects of their workflows.

title: Fantastic Fest
text:
Fantastic Fest
Fantastic Fest is an annual film festival in Austin, Texas, devoted to fantasy, horror, science fiction, action and cult cinema. Alamo Drafthouse founder Tim League established it in 2005. The festival takes place in September at the Alamo Drafthouse South Lamar, occupying eight screens for eight days. Its program includes secret screenings whose titles are withheld until viewers are seated, along with themed parties and film-related meals. Writers, directors and actors attend, including both established filmmakers and newcomers. Festival organizers describe its mission as supporting challenging genre cinema and bringing attention to filmmakers and film regions that receive less exposure. The event also collaborates with archives, cinematheques and other festivals. Past editions have hosted world premieres of titles including Smile, John Wick and Zombieland, alongside discussions and events featuring filmmakers and performers.

title: Pocket Opera
text:
Pocket Opera
Pocket Opera is a chamber opera company in San Francisco that performs in English with its orchestra, the Pocket Philharmonic. Founded in 1978, it stages familiar operas alongside less frequently performed works. Its repertoire has grown to more than ninety operas, and its March-to-July season usually comprises four or five productions. Founder Donald Pippin began translating opera librettos into English in the 1960s. His translations form the basis of the company’s productions, and the performance scores are archived at Stanford University. Pocket Opera's own profile describes its performances as fully staged and accompanied by the Pocket Philharmonic, a chamber ensemble of five to twelve players. It also performs at the Hillside Club in Berkeley and at the Gunn Theater in San Francisco's Legion of Honor. The company identifies outreach and education, alongside performance, as part of its mission.

title: Fan Chung
text:
Fan Chung
Fan Chung is a Taiwanese-American mathematician whose research includes spectral graph theory, extremal graph theory and random graphs. She was born in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, on October 9, 1949, and studied mathematics at National Taiwan University before moving to the University of Pennsylvania for graduate study. There she earned a doctorate in 1974 under Herbert Wilf, working on Ramsey theory. After nineteen years at Bell Laboratories and Bellcore, Chung became the first woman to hold a tenured mathematics professorship at the University of Pennsylvania. In 1998 she became the Paul Erdős Professor in Combinatorics at the University of California, San Diego.

title: Lilly — Ventyx acquisition agreement, January 2026
text:
Lilly — Ventyx acquisition agreement, January 2026
On January 7, 2026, Lilly announced a definitive agreement to acquire Ventyx Biosciences. Both boards approved the transaction, which remained subject to stockholder approval, regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. The proposed purchase included Ventyx’s clinical-stage pipeline of oral medicines targeting chronic inflammatory conditions. The programme included NLRP3 inhibitors being studied across neuroinflammatory and cardiometabolic diseases. Lilly said the planned acquisition complemented work in cardiometabolic health, neuroscience and autoimmune disorders. The company’s chief executive, Raju Mohan, described a portfolio intended to address residual inflammation associated with chronic illnesses. The acquisition announcement described Ventyx as a San Diego-based clinical-stage biotechnology firm developing oral small-molecule treatments.

title: 2026 Canada Gairdner Awards announcement
text:
2026 Canada Gairdner Awards announcement
The Gairdner Foundation announced its 2026 laureates on March 31, 2026. International Awards went to cryo-electron tomography researcher Wolfgang Baumeister, affiliated with ShanghaiTech, and drug-discovery researcher Jeffery Kelly of Scripps Research. Proteomics researchers John Yates III at Scripps, Ruedi Aebersold at ETH Zurich and Matthias Mann at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry also received International Awards. The Global Health Award was shared by John Clemens, an International Vaccine Institute adviser in Seoul, and Jan Holmgren of Gothenburg. Momentum Awards went to Karen Maxwell of Toronto and Aaron Phillips of Calgary. The Gairdner Foundation selected nine biomedical and global-health researchers for its 2026 honours. Baumeister’s cryo-electron tomography methods reveal the three-dimensional organization of molecular complexes inside intact cells. His work combined cryogenic sample thinning, automated microscopy and computational methods for identifying protein structures.

title: TCL Electronics Holdings Limited — corporate information
text:
TCL Electronics Holdings Limited — corporate information
Shares of TCL Electronics Holdings Limited trade on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under the code 1070. The company was listed on November 26, 1999 and is incorporated in the Cayman Islands. Its principal place of business is at Hong Kong Science Park in Shatin, in the New Territories. Its financial year ends on December 31. The corporation’s registered address is in the Cayman Islands, while its main place of business is in Hong Kong Science Park in Sha Tin. Its Hong Kong listing dates from November 26, 1999, and its reporting financial year ends on December 31. The listed board includes chairperson Du Juan and chief executive Zhang Shaoyong.

title: Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize
text:
Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize
The Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize is an Indian literary award established in 1989 for translations of creative and critical writing. It covers 24 languages recognized by the Sahitya Akademi, including English and Rajasthani. The award consists of a plaque and ₹50,000. Both the original author and the translator must be Indian nationals. Translations made directly from the original language are preferred, although translations through an intermediate language and joint translations can also qualify. The Akademi's published award history records how the cash component changed over time: it began at Rs.10,000 in 1989, rose to Rs.15,000 in 2001 and Rs.20,000 in 2003, before reaching Rs.50,000 in 2009.

title: Samuel Wesley Stratton Award
text:
Samuel Wesley Stratton Award
The Samuel Wesley Stratton Award is an annual research honor established in 1962 by what is now the National Institute of Standards and Technology. It recognizes scientific or engineering work that earns wider scientific recognition while advancing the institute’s mission. Named for the organization’s first director, it is NIST’s highest award for fundamental research. Past recipients include John L. Hall in 1971, Marilyn E. Jacox in 1973 and William Daniel Phillips in 1987. NIST's early award record shows that the first Stratton Awards were presented in 1962 to James R. Wait, Peter L. Bender and Raymond L. Driscoll. The joint citation recognized precision electromagnetic measurement, while Wait was honored for work on electromagnetic radiation and radio-wave propagation.

title: Charlie Marsh — EuroRust 2024 speaker profile
text:
Charlie Marsh — EuroRust 2024 speaker profile
Charlie Marsh founded Astral, a company that builds performance-focused tools for Python developers. He wrote Ruff, a Python linter and formatter, as well as uv, a package manager, both implemented in Rust. Before Astral, he worked at Khan Academy and later led a hybrid Rust-Python machine-learning and data platform as a staff engineer at Spring Discovery. He received a Bachelor of Science in computer science from Princeton. The EuroRust session description explains that the talk would examine the architecture and design choices behind uv, including allocators, concurrency and zero-copy techniques. It framed Python packaging as a mature problem space shaped by specifications and tools developed over several decades, and asked how a new implementation could remain compatible while improving performance. The event page reported that uv had passed ten million downloads per month after its February release. Marsh's profile also connects his developer-tool work with earlier experience on mobile and web platforms at Khan Academy.

title: Michael Carrick — playing career and autobiography
text:
Michael Carrick — playing career and autobiography
Michael Carrick began his career at West Ham United and won the FA Youth Cup there in 1999. After loan spells at Swindon Town and Birmingham City, he established himself in West Ham's first team during the 2000–2001 season. He moved to Tottenham Hotspur in 2004 and Manchester United in 2006, later serving as United's captain. His autobiography, Michael Carrick: Between the Lines, was published in 2018. Carrick moved to Tottenham Hotspur in 2004, making seventy-five appearances across two seasons before joining Manchester United. He represented England at the 2006 and 2010 FIFA World Cups and accumulated more than thirty senior international caps. His foundation supports educational activities and access to football for disadvantaged young people.

title: Cimulate — Sierra Ventures investment profile, 2024
text:
Cimulate — Sierra Ventures investment profile, 2024
John Andrews and Vivek Farias founded Cimulate in 2023 after working together in retail technology. Sierra Ventures led its $5 million seed round in fall 2023. In a December 18, 2024 investment profile, Sierra reported a $28 million Series A led by Spark Capital. The profile described Cimulate's Commerce Experience Server as powered by CustomerGPT, its LLM-based operating system. Farias was an MIT professor specializing in reinforcement learning and applied probability, while Andrews had worked at Endeca and Oracle. Its founders previously built Celect, a retail inventory-optimisation business that was subsequently sold to Nike. Sierra Ventures led Cimulate’s $5 million seed financing in the autumn of 2023. Spark Capital later led a $28 million Series A funding round, announced in December 2024. Co-founder Vivek Farias is a professor at MIT whose research includes reinforcement learning and applied probability.

title: Okta acquires Axiom Security to enhance privileged access management
text:
Okta acquires Axiom Security to enhance privileged access management
Okta signed an agreement to buy Axiom Security, an Israeli startup developing technology for privileged access management. Founded in 2021, Axiom offers temporary access to critical infrastructure, permission-request and approval processes, and reviews of user access. Okta planned to add these capabilities to its own privileged-access product over the months following the transaction. The companies did not disclose financial terms, and Okta said it expected to complete the purchase in September, strengthening a platform intended to reduce unnecessary standing permissions. The product announcement describes several specific controls: just-in-time access, automated request and approval workflows, and user access reviews. Okta's chief technology officer said the acquisition would add connectors for infrastructure resources such as databases and Kubernetes. The planned integration was intended to extend privileged-access controls to resources both on premises and in cloud environments. The report noted that the financial terms were not disclosed and that Okta expected the transaction to complete in September.

title: Hans Rademacher
text:
Hans Rademacher
Hans Adolph Rademacher was a German-born American mathematician who worked in analysis and number theory. He completed his doctorate at Göttingen in 1916 under Constantin Carathéodory. After teaching in Berlin and Hamburg, he lost his Breslau position in 1933 because of his public support for the Weimar Republic. He left Europe in 1934 and joined the University of Pennsylvania, remaining there until retirement in 1962. His research included Dedekind sums and a convergent series for the integer partition function, which he discovered in 1937. Rademacher was invited to address the American Mathematical Society in 1938 on Fourier expansions of modular forms and partition problems. A later lecture in 1941 reviewed developments in analytic number theory and emphasized the close interaction between analysis and arithmetic.

title: CrowdStrike to Acquire SGNL to Transform Identity Security for the AI Era
text:
CrowdStrike to Acquire SGNL to Transform Identity Security for the AI Era
CrowdStrike announced an agreement to acquire SGNL on 8 January 2026. The acquisition was intended to extend its Falcon security platform with controls that grant or revoke access according to changing risk. Those controls cover human users, other non-human identities and AI agents, with dynamic authorization extending across software-as-a-service applications and hyperscaler cloud environments. The transaction formed part of CrowdStrike’s Next-Gen Identity Security strategy. The proposed deal was expected to close during the first quarter of CrowdStrike’s fiscal year 2027, subject to regulatory clearance. SGNL’s technology was designed to re-evaluate access to cloud services and other applications as identity and device risks change.

title: PEN Translation Prize
text:
PEN Translation Prize
The PEN Translation Prize is an annual PEN America award for a book translated into English and published in the United States. Established in 1963 with the Book of the Month Club, it was the first American award expressly for literary translators. The distinction carries a $3,000 cash prize. Eligible works are book-length English translations published in the United States during the relevant year, regardless of the translator's or original author's nationality. The prize is separate from PEN America's Award for Poetry in Translation and forms part of the organization's wider literary awards programme. A 1999 New York Times profile compared its standing to a major literary award, reflecting its prominence among established translators.

title: Europe’s Starlink competitor is go
text:
Europe’s Starlink competitor is go
The European Union signed a €10.6 billion public-private agreement for the IRIS² satellite network in December 2024, with service expected by 2030. The project is intended to provide secure connections for governments, businesses, and European residents, including areas without reliable broadband. Its interconnected satellites are planned for both low and medium Earth orbits to maintain secure connections. SpaceRISE, a consortium led by SES, Eutelsat, and Hispasat, received a 12-year concession to develop, deploy, and operate the system, with support from companies including Airbus and Deutsche Telekom. The planned constellation comprises 264 satellites in low Earth orbit and 18 in medium Earth orbit. IRIS² is short for Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite. The concession covers development, deployment and operation of the network, rather than construction alone.

title: Rover (space exploration)
text:
Rover (space exploration)
A planetary rover is a mobile exploration vehicle designed to travel across the surface of a planet, moon or other celestial body. Some carry astronauts, while others operate as partially or fully autonomous robots, examining terrain and collecting samples of soil, rock or other material. Rovers must withstand acceleration, extreme temperatures, dust and radiation without routine repairs. Communication delays prevent real-time control of vehicles on Mars, so they perform some navigation and data collection independently, while ground controllers choose targets and help plan their movements. A radio signal travelling between Mars and Earth can take roughly three to 21 minutes to arrive, so remote operators cannot steer a rover in real time. Onboard systems therefore handle parts of navigation and data collection, while ground teams select distant targets and plan routes that preserve access to solar energy.

title: Nicholas Michael Smith
text:
Nicholas Michael Smith
Nicholas Michael Smith is a British conductor, composer, and music educator born in 1967. He has lived and worked in China since 1994. In 2011, he received an OBE for his musical work and contributions to relations between the United Kingdom and China, where his work has featured on television and radio. After moving to Beijing, Smith founded the Peking Sinfonietta in 1997 and the Beijing International Festival Chorus in 2002. He later conducted Chinese music programmes at Cadogan Hall in London in 2016 and 2018, including performances that combined traditional material with improvisation by Canadian composer David Braid. He has also translated several children's books by Hong Ying into English.

title: Yoon Je-kyoon
text:
Yoon Je-kyoon
Yoon Je-kyoon is a South Korean director, screenwriter and producer born in Busan in 1969. He graduated in economics from Korea University in 1996 and worked for the advertising agency LG Ad. His first film as director was My Boss, My Hero in 2001, followed by Sex Is Zero in 2002. Tidal Wave, his 2009 disaster film, attracted more than ten million viewers, a milestone also reached by Ode to My Father in 2014. Yoon became chief executive of the production company JK Film, previously called Dusabu Film. Tidal Wave was promoted as South Korea's first disaster film and reportedly had a production budget of US$16 million. It received nominations in several categories at the 2009 Black Dragon Awards and won the award for Best Special Effects.

title: Cal Poly Pomona — president appointed in March 2026
text:
Cal Poly Pomona — president appointed in March 2026
On March 11, 2026, Cal Poly Pomona reported the appointment of Vanya Quiñones as its next president by the CSU Board of Trustees. She would take office on July 1, 2026, becoming the institution’s eighth president and first Latina president. Her previous administration at Monterey Bay had introduced a mentoring programme for undergraduate students and expanded hands-on learning. The university also reported improvements in research funding and philanthropic giving during her tenure. The Cal Poly Pomona announcement cited enrollment growth of nearly thirty percent during Quiñones’s prior presidency. Before leading Monterey Bay, she was provost and executive vice president for academic affairs at Pace University in New York.

title: Aaron Naber
text:
Aaron Naber
Aaron Naber is an American mathematician born in 1982. He earned a mathematics bachelor’s degree at Pennsylvania State University in 2005 and a doctorate at Princeton in 2009, supervised by Gang Tian. After appointments at MIT, he joined Northwestern University as an associate professor in 2013 and became its Kenneth F. Burgess Professor of Mathematics in 2015. In 2024, he joined the Institute for Advanced Study as a permanent faculty member. His research includes geometric analysis, differential geometry and nonlinear harmonic maps. In his doctoral work, Naber extended the study of Ricci solitons from three dimensions to manifolds of four or more dimensions under bounded non-negative curvature. With Tobias Colding, he later investigated limits of manifolds with lower Ricci-curvature bounds and the geometric structure of the resulting spaces.

title: €100,000 Dublin literary award won by Romanian author Mircea Cărtărescu
text:
€100,000 Dublin literary award won by Romanian author Mircea Cărtărescu
Mircea Cărtărescu’s novel Solenoid won the 2024 Dublin literary award in an English translation by Sean Cotter. The €100,000 prize was divided between the Romanian author, who received €75,000, and his American translator, who received €25,000. Set in communist Bucharest during the late 1970s and early 1980s, the novel follows a schoolteacher whose reflections develop into a surreal journey through different dimensions. It was the first winner translated from Romanian since the award began in 1996. The Dublin city council sponsors the award, and public libraries nominate books for the competition; Solenoid was nominated by the Octavian Goga library in Cluj-Napoca, Romania.

title: Huawei PanGu
text:
Huawei PanGu
PanGu is a family of large language models developed by Huawei, named after the primordial figure in Chinese creation mythology. Huawei introduced PanGu 3.0 in July 2023 for industries including finance, manufacturing, mining and meteorology. The system was designed for enterprise tasks and could be adapted using customers’ own data. PanGu-Σ was described as a trillion-parameter model trained for more than 100 days on a cluster of 512 Ascend 910 AI accelerators. The training processed 329 billion tokens across more than 40 natural and programming languages. Its Random Routed Experts design and Transformer decoder allow task-specific submodels for conversation, translation and code generation.

title: King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Award for Translation
text:
King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Award for Translation
The King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz International Award for Translation is a Saudi literary award for works translated into or out of Arabic. Based at the King Abdul Aziz Public Library in Riyadh, it was established on October 31, 2006, following approval by the library’s council.
