Its first awards were presented in 2008 for works published in 2007, with the stated aim of encouraging cultural exchange and intellectual interaction between civilizations. The award distributes prizes across four translation categories covering the humanities, religion, literature and natural sciences, with works translated into or out of Arabic. A separate fifth category recognizes institutions that promote translation, while each of the four main category prizes has been listed at US$200,000.

title: Peter Steinberger — document-software startup interview
text:
Peter Steinberger — document-software startup interview
Peter Steinberger described himself in a pre-WWDC19 interview as the founder and CEO of PSPDFKit, based in Vienna, Austria. His background was in iOS development, and the document software began as an iOS product before expanding to Android, the web and other platforms. PSPDFKit supplied document-viewing and interaction software as an SDK to other companies. He said that arranging a visa for an early job in San Francisco had taken nine months. In the interview, Steinberger explained that PSPDFKit supplies the document interface inside other apps, allowing users to open files, search their contents and select text. He cited Dropbox as an example, along with software used in Lufthansa aircraft and by IBM. The SDK is licensed to companies that embed document features in their own products rather than being sold only as a consumer app.

title: James Burton
text:
James Burton
James Burton was born in London and began his musical training in Westminster Abbey’s choir, where he became head chorister. His subsequent studies took him to St John’s College at the University of Cambridge, where he held a choral scholarship. He earned a master’s degree in orchestral conducting at the Peabody Conservatory, studying with Frederik Prausnitz and Gustav Meier. In February 2017, he was appointed conductor of the Tanglewood Festival Chorus and choral director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra. Burton later studied at St John’s College, Cambridge, and earned a master’s degree in orchestral conducting from the Peabody Conservatory. He directed the Hallé Choir between 2002 and 2009 and founded the Hallé Youth Choir, later receiving a Gramophone choral award.

title: Masashi Yanagisawa — professional CV
text:
Masashi Yanagisawa — professional CV
Masashi Yanagisawa was born in Tokyo in 1960. He earned an MD, summa cum laude, at the University of Tsukuba in 1985 and a PhD in medical sciences there in 1988. In 1991 he became an associate professor of molecular genetics at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas. He held the Patrick E. Haggerty Distinguished Chair in Basic Biomedical Science at UTSW from 1998 to 2014. His honours include election to the National Academy of Sciences in 2003 and Japan’s Medal with Purple Ribbon in 2016. From 2001 to 2007, he directed the Yanagisawa Orphan Receptor Project, a programme of Japan's Science and Technology Agency. Since 2012, he has directed the International Institute for Integrative Sleep Medicine at the University of Tsukuba. During his UTSW appointment, he also served as an investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.

title: Paolo Bortolameolli — LA Phil artist profile
text:
Paolo Bortolameolli — LA Phil artist profile
Paolo Bortolameolli earned a Master of Music at Yale School of Music in 2013 and a Graduate Performance Diploma at the Peabody Institute in 2015. He also holds a piano performance diploma from Universidad Católica de Chile and a conducting diploma from Universidad de Chile. His music education project Ponle Pausa uses short videos and concerts to reach social network users. In 2020 he published his first book, RUBATO: Procesos musicales y una playlist personal. Bortolameolli has also held conducting positions with Mexico’s Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional Esperanza Azteca and Chile’s Filarmónica de Santiago. He directed a production of Meredith Monk’s opera ATLAS at Walt Disney Concert Hall in 2019. The Los Angeles Philharmonic biography lists concert work with ensembles in North America, Europe and Asia.

title: EDGX
text:
EDGX
EDGX is a Belgian space technology company based in Ghent and founded in 2023. It develops computers for use in orbit and took its first systems from concept to space within two years. Its product range includes the Sterna and Morus computers and SpaceFeather software. Co-founders Nick Destrycker and Wouter Benoot lead the company as chief executive and chief technology and operating officer respectively. The team includes specialists in embedded software, electronics, radiation effects and mechanical engineering. The company develops computing equipment for use in orbit and provides engineering support for production and system integration. Its website identifies Nick Destrycker as co-founder and chief executive and Wouter Benoot as co-founder and technical and operating lead. The team reported having more than fifteen members and described a move from initial development to computers operating in space.

title: Lee Isaac Chung
text:
Lee Isaac Chung
Lee Isaac Chung is an American filmmaker born in 1978. His first feature, Munyurangabo, screened at Cannes in 2007 and was the first narrative feature made in Kinyarwanda. His later film Minari won the Golden Globe for foreign-language film and earned him Oscar nominations for directing and original screenplay. He also directed an episode of The Mandalorian in 2023 and the disaster film Twisters in 2024. The film follows two boys whose friendship develops in the aftermath of the Rwandan genocide. Chung later earned an MFA in film studies at the University of Utah, following his undergraduate studies in biology.

title: Bryan Traynor — education and clinical training
text:
Bryan Traynor — education and clinical training
Bryan Traynor was born in Dublin, Ireland in 1969. At University College Dublin he earned his MB, BCh and BAO degrees in 1993, an MD in 2000 and a PhD in 2012. He also earned an MMSc in drug development and clinical trial design through the Harvard–MIT Health Sciences and Technology program. His neurology residency and fellowship training were at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital. At the National Institutes of Health, Traynor's group studies the genetic, molecular and biomarker basis of ALS and FTD. It combines large-scale human genetics, proteomics, clinical cohorts and functional studies to examine disease mechanisms. The laboratory also identified familial ALS-associated mutations in genes including VCP, MATR3, CHCHD10, KIF5A, HTT and SPTLC1.

title: Paris-Saclay University
text:
Paris-Saclay University
Paris-Saclay University is a public research university and technological research institute in Orsay, France. It was established in its collegiate form in 2019, combining technical grandes écoles, engineering schools, technological institutes, and research facilities. Its laboratories investigate fields including particle physics, astrophysics, electronics, nanotechnology, nuclear physics, and condensed matter physics. The university forms part of the wider Paris-Saclay academic and business cluster. Its campuses include an urban site on the plateau around Orsay, Gif-sur-Yvette, and Palaiseau, and a historic valley campus centered on the Château de Launay. Within this research network, the Institute of Light Sciences lists major facilities such as Synchrotron SOLEIL, a free-electron laser, an attosecond X-UV laser platform and the Centre for Nanosciences and Nanotechnology. These resources support work in spectroscopy, imaging, photonics, materials and quantum technologies.

title: Explorers Program
text:
Explorers Program
NASA’s Explorers Program provides spaceflight opportunities for investigations in physics, geophysics, heliophysics and astrophysics. Explorer 1, launched in 1958, became the first United States spacecraft to reach orbit. NASA has operated the program since Explorer 6, working with other institutions and international partners across a series of more than 90 missions. NASA describes the program as a source of frequent, focused investigations that complement larger observatories. Its missions are generally small to medium in scale and designed to move from development through testing and launch in a shorter period than major observatories. The program office at Goddard Space Flight Center manages the portfolio.

title: Cimulate — company origins and technology
text:
Cimulate — company origins and technology
John Andrews and Vivek Farias began Cimulate in 2023 to move retail search beyond keywords and toward shopper intent. The company developed CommerceGPT, a model grounded in domain-specific behavioral data, along with an intent-aware context engine. By simulating millions of shopping journeys, it reported revenue-per-user improvements of up to 14 percent for partners. The approach aimed to explain not only what people bought but why. Before Cimulate, its founders had worked together on Celect, an inventory-optimisation company that was later acquired by Nike. Sierra Ventures described Vivek Farias as a professor at MIT whose work in reinforcement learning and applied probability informed the company's technology. It described John Andrews as a retail-technology executive whose earlier experience included Endeca and Oracle. These complementary backgrounds shaped the founders' focus on applying language-model methods to retail search.

title: Ex Cathedra announces James Burton as next Artistic Director succeeding founder Jeffrey Skidmore after 57 years
text:
Ex Cathedra announces James Burton as next Artistic Director succeeding founder Jeffrey Skidmore after 57 years
Ex Cathedra announced on 27 January 2026 that James Burton would succeed Jeffrey Skidmore as artistic director. He was due to join as artistic director designate that spring, before Jeffrey Skidmore’s retirement in autumn 2027 after 57 years. Skidmore would then become founder and conductor emeritus. Burton had spent eight seasons leading the Tanglewood Festival Chorus and serving as choral director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra. He also directed Schola Cantorum of Oxford for 15 years and founded the Hallé Youth Choir and Boston Symphony Children’s Choir. The artistic-director search involved interviews, workshops, rehearsals and performances with musicians, trustees and staff. The choir planned to celebrate Skidmore’s final season with concerts including a French Baroque programme in February 2026.

title: Ruedi Aebersold — ETH career profile
text:
Ruedi Aebersold — ETH career profile
Rudolf Aebersold, also known as Ruedi Aebersold, was born in Switzerland in 1954 and completed a doctorate in cell biology in Basel. His career took him to an assistant professorship in biochemistry at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver and a professorship at the University of Washington in Seattle. He cofounded the Institute for Systems Biology, which opened in Seattle in 2000. In 2003 he took a dual professorship at ETH Zurich and the University of Zurich. At ETH Zurich, Aebersold's work helped establish quantitative proteomics as a way to measure both the identity and abundance of proteins in a biological sample. The ETH account explains that his mass-spectrometry-based methods made it possible to observe changes in the proteome systematically, rather than simply listing which proteins were present. After becoming professor emeritus, he continued to lead an ETH tumour-profiling project that combined molecular measurements to help identify treatments suited to individual cancer patients. The project was scheduled to continue through 2023.

title: Liam Rosenior appointed Chelsea head coach
text:
Liam Rosenior appointed Chelsea head coach
Chelsea announced Liam Rosenior as head coach of its men’s team on 6 January 2026, on a contract running to 2032. He joined from RC Strasbourg after taking the French club into European competition in his first season, ending a 19-year absence. His earlier coaching roles in England included Hull City and Derby County. Rosenior described teamwork and unity as central to his approach and said he wanted to build strong relationships with players and staff, both on and off the pitch. On accepting the job, he said he wanted the team to reflect Chelsea’s identity and its tradition of winning trophies.

title: G. D. Birla Award for Scientific Research
text:
G. D. Birla Award for Scientific Research
The K. K. Birla Foundation established the G. D. Birla Award for Scientific Research in 1991 to commemorate philanthropist Ghanshyam Das Birla. It recognizes research by Indian scientists under fifty who live and work in India, with emphasis on work from the preceding five years. The annual award covers basic, applied and medical sciences and carries a prize of five lakh rupees. Narayan Pradhan received the award for contributions to materials science. Other recipients include Suman Chakraborty for engineering research supporting affordable healthcare and Rajeev Kumar Varshney for agricultural research. The 2023 recipient was quantum-information researcher Aditi Sen De. A later example is the 2025 award, announced in January 2026, which went to Bushra Ateeq of IIT Kanpur for work in biological sciences. The institute describes the selection as a highly selective process overseen by a board chaired by the president of the Indian National Science Academy.

title: Camillo De Lellis — Institute for Advanced Study biography
text:
Camillo De Lellis — Institute for Advanced Study biography
Camillo De Lellis was born in San Benedetto del Tronto, Italy, in 1976. He completed an undergraduate degree in mathematics at the University of Pisa in 1999. His 2002 doctorate at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa was supervised by Luigi Ambrosio. He joined the University of Zurich as an assistant professor in 2004 and became a full professor in 2005. He moved to the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton in 2018. His research spans geometric analysis and partial differential equations, including conservation laws, transport equations, Hamilton–Jacobi equations and fluid equations such as Euler and Navier–Stokes. He has also studied minimal surfaces in Riemannian manifolds and the formation of singularities in these settings.

title: Salesforce announces Cimulate acquisition agreement
text:
Salesforce announces Cimulate acquisition agreement
On February 10, 2026, Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cimulate, a company developing AI-powered product discovery for retailers. The acquisition was intended to improve search and discovery in Agentforce Commerce. The company's technology combined real and simulated shopping journeys to interpret what customers wanted. Salesforce said the team would add expertise in contextual search for e-commerce and retail. Cimulate’s software combines observed and simulated shopping journeys to infer customer intent and improve retail search. Salesforce planned to integrate the technology into Agentforce Commerce for more contextual and conversational product discovery. The company said the integration could help merchants respond to changing shopper preferences during the purchasing journey.

title: Ingmar Bergman
text:
Ingmar Bergman
Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish filmmaker and theatre director whose works include The Seventh Seal, Wild Strawberries, Persona and Fanny and Alexander. He directed more than 60 films and documentaries for cinema and television, writing most of them himself. Many of his films made from 1961 onward were shot on the island of Fårö, and he worked closely with cinematographers Gunnar Fischer and Sven Nykvist. His theatre career included leading positions at Stockholm’s Royal Dramatic Theatre and Munich’s Residenztheater. The foundation's biography notes that Bergman wrote or directed more than 170 theatrical productions and authored over 100 books and articles. It identifies Shakespeare, Molière, Ibsen and Strindberg as major influences on his stage work and broader artistic practice.

title: Joseph Colaneri — career biography current in December 2020
text:
Joseph Colaneri — career biography current in December 2020
Joseph Colaneri graduated from New York University and received a Master of Music from Westminster Choir College, which gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1994. He conducted at New York City Opera in 1987–1998, directed its touring National Company in 1991–1998, and was acting music director in 1995–1996. His NYCO conducting debut was South Pacific in 1987. His Metropolitan Opera company debut was La bohème in 2000. He became Glimmerglass music director in 2013 and initiated fully staged Mannes productions in 2004. He was West Australian Opera’s artistic director in 2012–2014. At Glimmerglass, Colaneri has conducted works ranging from Janáček's The Cunning Little Vixen and Donizetti's L'assedio di Calais to Bernstein's Candide and John Corigliano's The Ghosts of Versailles. His professional profile also describes guest work with opera companies in Europe and North America.

title: MediaTek’s Founding Chairman and CEO Bestowed GSA’s Highest Honor
text:
MediaTek’s Founding Chairman and CEO Bestowed GSA’s Highest Honor
MediaTek chairman and chief executive Ming-Kai Tsai received the Global Semiconductor Alliance’s 2015 Dr. Morris Chang Exemplary Leadership Award. The award presentation was scheduled for 10 December at the Santa Clara Convention Center in California. The association created the distinction in 1999, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation chairman Morris Chang as its first recipient. Tsai established MediaTek in Hsinchu, Taiwan, in 1997. He earned an electrical engineering bachelor’s degree at National Taiwan University and a master’s degree at the University of Cincinnati. Under Tsai's leadership, MediaTek became one of the world's three largest fabless semiconductor companies and the only top-listed company of that type headquartered outside the United States. The company also became a major supplier of optical-storage products, optical-disc players and digital-television chipsets.

title: PARK Chan-kyong Comes Back with MANSHIN: TEN THOUSANDS SPIRITS
text:
PARK Chan-kyong Comes Back with MANSHIN: TEN THOUSANDS SPIRITS
Park Chan-kyong, the younger brother of filmmaker Park Chan-wook, works in film and in installation art using photographs and video. The brothers collaborated under the name PARKingCHANce, co-directing the short films Night Fishing and Day Trip. Chan-kyong’s Mansin: Ten Thousand Spirits combines documentary with fantasy. Anyang, Paradise City received the JJ-STAR Prize at the Jeonju International Film Festival. The short film Night Fishing won the Golden Bear for short films at the Berlin International Film Festival in 2011. Mansin features Kim Sae-ron, Ryu Hyun-kyung and Moon So-ri portraying the shaman Kim Geum-hwa at different stages of her life. A crowdfunding campaign was organised in 2013 to support post-production on Mansin: Ten Thousand Spirits before its planned release.

title: MaXware
text:
MaXware
MaXware was a Norwegian supplier of identity management, virtual directory and federation software, headquartered in Trondheim. Its principal products were the Directory Synchronisation Engine and Virtual Directory Server, the latter designed for complex, high-volume environments. The virtual directory brought identity information from separate applications and data stores into customized views for authentication and authorization. The company had offices in the United States and United Kingdom, and SAP acquired it in May 2007. MaXware's product history began in two Norwegian software businesses. Former Norsk Data employees founded NOTIS AS after office-software development ended, while Televerket spun off its email and directory work into MaXware. The firms merged in 1996, and the Virtual Directory Server originated in a 1995 project for Swedish Post's X.500 directory service.

title: IDEMIA
text:
IDEMIA
Idemia is a French technology company headquartered in Courbevoie that supplies identity-security services, facial recognition systems and other biometric products to businesses and governments. It was formed through the combination of Oberthur Technologies and Safran Identity & Security, also known as Morpho, following a transaction completed on May 31, 2017. The combined identity and security business initially used the name OT-Morpho before adopting Idemia on September 28. Morpho’s origins reach back to Morpho Systèmes, founded in 1982 and absorbed by Sagem in 1993; the business subsequently operated under several names before becoming Safran Identity & Security in 2016. Its portfolio also includes automated fingerprint identification systems, iris and finger-vein recognition, biometric terminals, electronic gates, identity cards, ePassports, payment cards and SIM cards.

title: Sophos
text:
Sophos
Sophos is a British cybersecurity company that develops security software, hardware, and managed services. Its offerings include endpoint protection, incident response, and managed detection and response. Jan Hruska and Peter Lammer founded the company, which began making antivirus and encryption products in 1985. During the late 1990s, Sophos concentrated on antivirus software and expanded internationally. The business was listed on the London Stock Exchange before private equity firm Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in March 2020. In 2010, a majority interest in Sophos was sold to Apax Partners. The company announced plans for a US$100 million London Stock Exchange flotation in June 2015 and completed its listing later that year.

title: Cloudflare
text:
Cloudflare
Cloudflare is an American internet-services company headquartered in San Francisco, California. Founded in 2009 by Matthew Prince, Lee Holloway and Michelle Zatlyn, it provides content delivery, cybersecurity, protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks and domain registration. Its services commonly act as a reverse proxy between visitors and a website’s hosting provider. The company began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019 under the symbol NET, and its products include the Workers computing platform, the 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver and WARP. Cloudflare Workers supports front-end and back-end applications, serverless AI inference, scheduled jobs and durable workflows. The company's network is interconnected with more than 13,000 service providers, cloud providers and enterprise networks.

title: Christine Holt — NAS biographical sketch
text:
Christine Holt — NAS biographical sketch
Christine Holt was born and grew up in Wylam, Northumberland. She graduated in biological sciences from Sussex and earned her PhD in zoology at King’s College, London University, in 1982. She was a postdoctoral fellow at Oxford and the University of California, San Diego, joining the latter’s faculty in 1992. She moved to Cambridge in 1997 and became a fellow of Gonville and Caius College. She shared the Rosenstiel Award in 2022 and the Brain Prize in 2023. She was elected an international NAS member in 2020 and appointed CBE for services to neuroscience in 2024. Her laboratory focuses on retinal ganglion cell axons and the molecular mechanisms that guide them from the eye through the optic chiasm to appropriate targets in the brain. The group uses molecular techniques and live imaging to study how local protein synthesis helps growing axons respond to guidance cues.

title: HiVE
text:
HiVE
HiVE, short for High-precision Versatile Ecosphere, is an Earth-observation satellite constellation developed by the German company constellr. It uses infrared imaging to measure land-surface temperatures at high resolution for applications including agriculture, urban planning and infrastructure management. The European Space Agency’s InCubed programme provides support and partial funding, and the constellation contributes to the European Union’s Copernicus programme. Its first two satellites, SkyBee-1 and SkyBee-2, were launched on separate Falcon 9 flights on January 14 and June 23, 2025. Both spacecraft operate in sun-synchronous orbit: SkyBee-1 launched on Transporter-12 and SkyBee-2 on Transporter-14. A third satellite is planned to extend the constellation's thermal-imaging coverage.

title: Zhijian James Chen — Buffalo alumni career profile
text:
Zhijian James Chen — Buffalo alumni career profile
Zhijian James Chen received an undergraduate degree in biology from Fujian Normal University in 1985 and became a US citizen in 2004. After completing his doctorate, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Salk Institute. He subsequently worked for Baxter Healthcare Corporation and then as a senior scientist at ProScript before joining the faculty at UT Southwestern. Chen has been an investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute since 2005 and holds the George L. MacGregor Distinguished Chair in Biomedical Sciences at UT Southwestern. His work on protein degradation and biochemical pathways in cancer and immunity earned him the National Academy of Sciences Award in Molecular Biology in 2012.

title: Aaron Phillips — UBC postdoctoral profile
text:
Aaron Phillips — UBC postdoctoral profile
Aaron Phillips is a native of Grimsby, Ontario, and began a postdoctoral fellowship at UBC in 2013. He worked in physical medicine and rehabilitation with the International Collaboration on Repair Discoveries and the Centre for Heart, Lung and Vascular Health. His mentors included Andrei Krassioukov and Philip Ainslie. Phillips described Ainslie as an important mentor during his PhD and a reason for choosing UBC. His research examines cerebrovascular and cognitive complications after spinal cord injury. He reported that injury can trigger pro-fibrotic remodeling of brain blood vessels, while severe hypotension can impair both vascular and cognitive function. His work combines preclinical models, imaging and hemodynamic measurements with studies designed to test therapies in clinical practice.

title: Jennifer Mnookin — UCLA faculty career profile
text:
Jennifer Mnookin — UCLA faculty career profile
Jennifer L. Mnookin earned an AB at Harvard, a JD at Yale and a PhD in History and Social Study of Science and Technology at MIT. She joined UCLA Law’s faculty in 2005 and served as dean from August 2015 to June 2022. Before UCLA, she was a professor at the University of Virginia. She cofounded PULSE, the Program on Understanding Law, Science & Evidence. Her vice-dean terms covered faculty and research in 2007–2009 and faculty recruitment and intellectual life in 2012–2013. She was elected to the American Law Institute in 2011 and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2020.

title: Semyon Bychkov: Conductor of the Year
text:
Semyon Bychkov: Conductor of the Year
Semyon Bychkov first performed in public at six, playing Grieg’s March of the Trolls on the piano. He entered the Glinka School two years later and became interested in conducting. At seventeen and a half, he won a place in Ilya Musin’s orchestral conducting course at the Leningrad Conservatory, having competed with seventy-seven other applicants. Born in St Petersburg in 1952, Bychkov spent twenty-two years in the Soviet Union before emigrating to the United States. His conducting repertoire has ranged from Russian composers including Tchaikovsky and Mussorgsky to Debussy, Ravel, Wagner and Mahler. He has discussed the detailed preparation behind his recording of Mahler’s Fourth Symphony and the interpretation of its opening theme.

title: GLM-130B: An Open Bilingual Pre-trained Model
text:
GLM-130B: An Open Bilingual Pre-trained Model
GLM-130B is a language model with 130 billion parameters trained to work in both Chinese and English. Its developers describe the training design, engineering decisions and methods used to address instability. They also report four-bit quantization with little performance loss, allowing inference on four RTX 3090 graphics cards. The paper reports that GLM-130B outperformed GPT-3 175B on several English benchmarks and ERNIE TITAN 3.0 260B on Chinese benchmarks. The authors also describe training challenges involving loss spikes and divergence, along with the engineering choices used to stabilize pretraining. The model weights, code and training logs were made publicly available.

title: Herbert von Karajan
text:
Herbert von Karajan
Herbert von Karajan was an Austrian conductor who lived from 1908 to 1989 and led the Berlin Philharmonic for 34 years. He conducted the Berlin State Opera during the Second World War and became a dominant, though controversial, figure in European classical music after the mid-1950s. His extensive recording career contributed to that prominence, with one estimate putting his record sales at 200 million. His family had Greek ancestry. The official Karajan archive documents more than 2,000 audio recordings and around 200 video productions made between the late 1930s and late 1980s. His catalogue covers the works of more than 150 composers and draws chiefly on recordings with the Philharmonia Orchestra, the Berlin Philharmonic and the Vienna Philharmonic. Karajan also revisited some works over several decades, recording them with different orchestras, soloists, venues and technologies.

title: John Rubenstein — NAS biography
text:
John Rubenstein — NAS biography
John Rubenstein studied chemistry as a Stanford undergraduate from 1973 to 1977. He earned a doctorate in biophysics there in 1982, working with Harden McConnell and James Rothman on membranes and plasma membrane proteins. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the Pasteur Institute from 1984 to 1986, working with François Jacob, J. F. Nicolas and Josh Sanes. He then trained in child psychiatry at Stanford with Roland Ciaranello before joining the UCSF faculty. Rubenstein is recognized for developmental genetics research on how forebrain regions and cell types are formed. His work has examined the origin and tangential migration of cortical inhibitory neurons, as well as the transcriptional and cell-signaling mechanisms that regulate their specification, migration and synapse formation. With colleagues, he provided evidence that transplanting immature interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence can ameliorate epilepsy in mice.

title: Gilead — Arcellx acquisition agreement, February 2026
text:
Gilead — Arcellx acquisition agreement, February 2026
On February 23, 2026, Gilead announced a definitive agreement to acquire Arcellx. Both boards had approved the transaction, which was expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions. The agreed consideration included $115 in cash per share and a contingent value right worth up to another $5 per share. Gilead placed the transaction’s implied equity value at approximately $7.8 billion payable at closing. Its Kite unit had collaborated with Arcellx since 2022 on an investigational CAR T-cell treatment known as anito-cel. The therapy targeted BCMA in multiple myeloma and had received FDA acceptance of its biologics licence application.

title: The Canadian Opera Company appoints Ian Derrer as next General Director
text:
The Canadian Opera Company appoints Ian Derrer as next General Director
The Canadian Opera Company announced Ian Derrer as its next General Director on 10 February 2026, with his term beginning in the 2026–27 season. The appointment followed a national and international search lasting more than a year. At the time of the announcement, Derrer had spent eight years as General Director and CEO of The Dallas Opera. The search committee worked with executive recruitment firm Isaacson Miller and consulted staff and stakeholders from the opera sector. At Dallas Opera, a matching-gift fundraising campaign exceeded its new-donation target by $4.5 million and brought the full campaign total to $54.5 million. The company also reported increased attendance among visitors aged 18 to 45 during his leadership.

title: Manchester United — January 2026 head-coach appointment
text:
Manchester United — January 2026 head-coach appointment
On January 13, 2026, Manchester United appointed Michael Carrick head coach of the men's first team until the end of the 2025–2026 season. He had previously coached the club after retiring as a player and had also managed Middlesbrough. His support staff included Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans and Craig Mawson. Darren Fletcher was to remain lead coach of the Under-18s. Carrick represented Manchester United in 464 matches and won five Premier League championships during his playing career there. After retiring in 2018, he worked on the first-team coaching staff under José Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

title: Centessa Pharmaceuticals — 2024 annual report
text:
Centessa Pharmaceuticals — 2024 annual report
Centessa Pharmaceuticals reported 77 full-time employees at March 1, 2025; 36% held MD or PhD degrees. Of that workforce, 49 worked in research and development and 28 in business development, finance, legal, general management and administration. Its IPO registration statement became effective on May 27, 2021. The June 2021 IPO involved 16,500,000 American Depositary Shares priced at $20 per ADS. Each ADS represented one ordinary share, with a nominal value of £0.002 per ordinary share. The 2024 annual report describes ORX750 as Centessa's most advanced OX2R agonist candidate and reports that its Phase 1 study produced positive data during the year. By late 2024, the company had advanced ORX750 into the Phase 2a CRYSTAL-1 study for narcolepsy types 1 and 2 and idiopathic hypersomnia. ORX142 and ORX489 remained follow-up OX2R agonists in IND-enabling studies for neurological, neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Ken Dugdale
text:
Ken Dugdale
Ken Dugdale is an English football coach and former player, born in Liverpool on December 7, 1950. His early clubs included Kirkby Town, Aston Villa and Wolverhampton Wanderers, followed by non-league spells with Wigan Athletic, New Brighton and Burscough. He managed New Zealand’s national team from 1998 to 2002 and led it at the 1999 FIFA Confederations Cup. He also coached Football Kingz and Vollen UL in Norway. His uncle Jimmy Dugdale and brother Alan were footballers. New Zealand's official football history records that the 1999 Confederations Cup in Mexico was the national team's first appearance at that competition. Under Dugdale, the team faced the United States, Germany and Brazil, losing by narrow margins of 1–2, 0–2 and 0–2 respectively. After his tenure, the national association separated the head-coach and director-of-football roles, assigning the latter responsibility for coach education and player development.

title: Emmanuel Candès — MacArthur Fellow biography
text:
Emmanuel Candès — MacArthur Fellow biography
Emmanuel Candès received a BE from École Polytechnique in 1993, an MSc from Université de Paris VI in 1994 and a PhD from Stanford University in 1998. He taught at Stanford from 1998 to 2000 and at the California Institute of Technology from 2000 to 2009. He then returned to Stanford as the Barnum-Simons Chair in Mathematics and Statistics, with a courtesy appointment in electrical engineering. His research is especially associated with compressed sensing, a framework for reconstructing signals from relatively small sets of measurements. Applications described in the MacArthur profile include high-resolution image reconstruction, recovery of missing entries in large data tables, MRI, radar imaging and wireless communications. He also developed statistical methods for low-rank matrix completion and worked on phase retrieval problems relevant to crystallography and astronomical instrumentation.

title: Mung Chiang — Princeton faculty biography
text:
Mung Chiang — Princeton faculty biography
Mung Chiang received his bachelor’s, master’s and PhD degrees from Stanford in 1999, 2000 and 2003. He was an assistant professor at Princeton in 2003–2008, a tenured associate professor in 2008–2011, and a professor in 2011–2013. He received the Alan T. Waterman Award in 2013, IEEE Kiyo Tomiyasu Award in 2012, and Guggenheim Fellowship in 2014. He founded the Princeton EDGE Lab in 2009 and became Keller Center director in 2014. His undergraduate textbook Networked Life: 20 Questions and Answers received the 2012 PROSE Award in Engineering and Technology. Chiang's research spans Internet and wireless networks, broadband access, content distribution, network economics and online social networks. His work includes network optimization, smart data pricing, fog networking and social learning networks. The EDGE Lab combines mathematical analysis with prototypes and technology transfer; its research has been adopted in products used by millions of smartphones.

title: List of Premier League clubs
text:
List of Premier League clubs
The Premier League was formed in 1992, and 51 clubs have appeared in the competition. Two of those clubs, Cardiff City and Swansea City, are based in Wales but compete in the English league system. Preston North End are the only former champions of the top-flight First Division who have never played in the Premier League. Conversely, Barnsley, Bournemouth, Hull City, Reading, Swindon Town and Wigan Athletic reached the Premier League without previously having played in the old First Division, which preceded it. The Premier League operates with 20 clubs, each playing every other club twice, once at home and once away, for a total of 380 matches in a season. Teams receive three points for a win and one for a draw, with goal difference used to separate clubs level on points. The bottom three clubs are relegated to the Championship and replaced by three promoted sides, two automatic and one determined through the promotion play-offs.

title: Warwick Prize for Women in Translation
text:
Warwick Prize for Women in Translation
The Warwick Prize for Women in Translation was established in 2017 to improve the representation of women in translated literature available to British and Irish readers. Funded and administered by the University of Warwick, it recognizes books written by women and translated into English. Eligible genres include fiction, poetry, literary nonfiction and writing for children or young adults; the translator may be of any gender. The £1,000 award is shared equally between the author and translator or translators, with the full amount going to the translators when the author has died. In the 2026 competition, the prize received 164 submissions representing 37 languages, the largest number and language range in its ten-year history. The judging panel comprised Arifa Akbar, Véronique Tadjo and Boyd Tonkin, and the six-book shortlist included works translated from Arabic, Hungarian, Norwegian, French, Japanese and Russian. The University of Warwick publishes eligible-entry lists to support translators, publishers, bookshops and researchers as well as to promote women's writing in translation.

title: Cannes Film Festival
text:
Cannes Film Festival
The Cannes Film Festival is an invitation-only film festival held annually in Cannes, France, usually in May. Established in 1946, it screens new films across genres, including documentaries, at the Palais des Festivals et des Congrès. The International Federation of Film Producers Associations formally accredited the festival in 1951. Cannes is grouped with Venice and Berlin as one of Europe’s three principal film festivals, and with Toronto and Sundance in the wider group commonly called the Big Five. The festival's top award did not originally carry its current name: until 1954, the jury presented a Grand Prix for Best Director together with a work by a contemporary artist. A palm-shaped trophy was designed in 1954 as a tribute to the coat of arms of the city, and the first Palme d'Or was awarded in 1955 to Delbert Mann for Marty. The prize was reintroduced in 1975 and has since become the enduring award for the best feature film in the Official Competition.

title: Introducing Sonnet 4.6
text:
Introducing Sonnet 4.6
Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4.6 on 17 February 2026, making it available through Claude plans, Cowork, Claude Code, its API and major cloud platforms. The release included updates to coding, computer use, long-context reasoning, planning and design, alongside a one-million-token context window in beta. Sonnet 4.6 became the default model for Free and Pro users in Claude and Cowork. Published pricing matched Sonnet 4.5, starting at $3/$15 per million tokens. Anthropic also added file creation, connectors, skills and conversation compaction to its free tier. On the Claude Platform, Sonnet 4.6 supports both adaptive thinking and extended thinking, while context compaction is available in beta to summarize older conversation context. On the API, the web search and fetch tools can write and execute code to filter results before placing relevant material in context. Code execution, memory, programmatic tool calling and tool search were also made generally available with the release.

title: Karen Heywood — EGU interview, April 2022
text:
Karen Heywood — EGU interview, April 2022
In an April 2022 interview, Karen Heywood was described as professor of physical oceanography at the University of East Anglia. She had been president of the European Geosciences Union’s Ocean Sciences division from 2016 to 2021. She had first studied physics in the early 1980s before undertaking a PhD in physical oceanography. After postdoctoral work, she moved to UEA for a lectureship in 1989. Her research at the time used ocean gliders and other autonomous platforms to study the Antarctic, including the waters around ice shelves. In the planned Amundsen Sea campaign, the team intended to send two autonomous underwater vehicles beneath a floating ice shelf, tag seals, deploy gliders and collect ship-based measurements. The measurements were designed to clarify how ocean processes contribute to ice loss at Thwaites Glacier.

title: GSK — RAPT acquisition agreement, January 2026
text:
GSK — RAPT acquisition agreement, January 2026
On January 20, 2026, GSK announced a definitive agreement to acquire RAPT Therapeutics. The terms provided for $58 per share at closing, with an estimated aggregate equity value of $2.2 billion. The purchase would bring GSK ozureprubart, a long-acting antibody targeting immunoglobulin E in development for prevention of food-allergy reactions. At the time of the announcement, ozureprubart was in a phase IIb trial and investigators expected results during 2027. GSK described a possible twelve-week injection interval, compared with the two-to-four-week schedule of existing anti-IgE treatment. The asset was intended to strengthen the group’s Respiratory, Immunology and Inflammation research pipeline. The company estimated that approximately seventeen million people in the United States were living with food allergies.

title: Toronto International Film Festival
text:
Toronto International Film Festival
The Toronto International Film Festival was founded in 1976 and takes place each September in downtown Toronto. Originally called the Toronto Festival of Festivals, it presented a selection of films from other international festivals. The inaugural event showed 127 films from 30 countries to about 35,000 viewers. Its People’s Choice Award is decided by audience voting and has been won by films including Slumdog Millionaire, The King’s Speech and Nomadland. TIFF also operates the Lightbox, a year-round venue for film screenings and other programming. TIFF's year-round initiatives extend beyond the September festival: its Canada’s Top Ten event, established in 2001, highlights outstanding contemporary Canadian cinema. Its Film Circuit also works with more than 180 local groups in 160 communities to bring Canadian and international independent films to audiences across the country.

title: David Gross — Kavli Institute biography
text:
David Gross — Kavli Institute biography
David Gross earned his bachelor’s degree at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1962 and a physics PhD at UC Berkeley in 1966. He then spent three years as a junior fellow at Harvard. He became a professor at Princeton in 1973 and its Eugene Higgins Professor of Physics in 1986. He directed the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics from 1997 to 2012. He shared the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physics with David Politzer and Frank Wilczek. In 1973, Gross and Frank Wilczek discovered asymptotic freedom in non-Abelian gauge theories, leading to quantum chromodynamics, the theory of the strong nuclear force. He also helped originate heterotic string theory, an approach that seeks to place gravity within a unified quantum framework.

title: Lin King - National Book Foundation
text:
Lin King - National Book Foundation
Lin King is a writer and translator from Taipei, Taiwan, whose work includes translations from Mandarin and Japanese into English. She earned a BA at Princeton University and an MFA at Columbia University, where she also taught undergraduate writing. Her translations include Yang Shuang-Zi’s Taiwan Travelogue and Yu Pei-Yun’s graphic novel series The Boy from Clearwater, illustrated by Zhou Jian-Xin. Her fiction has appeared in One Story, Boston Review and Joyland and received the PEN/Robert J. Dau Short Story Prize for Emerging Writers. Taiwan Travelogue won the 2024 National Book Award for Translated Literature. The novel is framed as a rediscovered text: its fictional writer travels through Taiwan under Japanese rule in 1938, accompanied by a local interpreter. The National Book Foundation's judges described the book as a metafictional account that uses food, customs and intimate relationships to reveal colonial power dynamics.

title: European Football Clubs
text:
European Football Clubs
European Football Clubs is an organization recognized by UEFA and FIFA as the independent representative body for European football clubs, representing their interests at European level. Previously called the European Club Association, it was formed in January 2008 through the merger of G-14 and UEFA’s European Club Forum. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge served as acting chairman before members formally elected him in July 2008. The association adopted the name European Football Clubs on 7 October 2025. UEFA describes EFC as the sole body representing the interests of European clubs, with more than 800 member clubs. The association works with UEFA on governance, representation, regulatory, financial and sporting matters affecting both men's and women's clubs.

title: Momentum — early branding and launch case study
text:
Momentum — early branding and launch case study
Momentum launched in spring 2020 as a sales workflow tool built on Slack to help teams coordinate work and close deals. It was funded by Basis Set Ventures and South Park Commons. Product marketing agency Olivine worked on its positioning, messaging, brand and launch from the company's beginnings. Olivine developed the brand and website with design partner Elipse and continued to run Momentum's marketing. The product's deal rooms were Slack channels built around a Salesforce opportunity, giving a sales team a shared space to coordinate an individual deal. The early product sheet kept its feature list short and illustrated the workflow as a three-step sequence, while the front page emphasized benefits for account executives and sales managers.

title: One Identity spins out as independent company, relocates global HQ to Ireland
text:
One Identity spins out as independent company, relocates global HQ to Ireland
One Identity announced that it would separate from Quest Software and establish its global headquarters at its Cork office in Ireland. Quest had been acquired by Clearlake Capital in 2021. The identity-security company said independence would support investment in identity governance and privileged access management as customers faced growing numbers of human and machine identities. More than 80 percent of its engineering staff were already in Europe, along with several senior leaders, and the transition was expected to continue throughout 2026. The company reports that its services are used by more than 6,000 enterprise customers and manage over 500 million identities. It says that 80 of the Fortune 100 are customers and that its global partner network exceeds 1,000 organizations.

title: Stuart Orkin — Gruber career biography
text:
Stuart Orkin — Gruber career biography
Stuart Orkin grew up in New York City, where his father practised as a urologist. He entered MIT in 1963 and later joined John Littlefield’s laboratory at Massachusetts General Hospital. His postdoctoral work was in Philip Leder’s laboratory on the NIH campus in Bethesda, Maryland. He subsequently trained in hematology and oncology in a program overseen by David Nathan. In 1978 he became an assistant professor at Harvard Medical School. Orkin's research helped define the GATA family of hematopoietic transcription factors and their roles in blood-cell development. His work on BCL11A showed that reducing this repressor can reactivate fetal hemoglobin, a finding that led to gene-editing strategies for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

title: Jeffery W. Kelly — NAS biography
text:
Jeffery W. Kelly — NAS biography
Jeffery W. Kelly received a BS in chemistry from SUNY Fredonia in 1982 and a PhD in organic chemistry from the University of North Carolina in 1986. He completed postdoctoral training at Rockefeller University from 1986 to 1989. His Scripps posts have included dean of the graduate program, vice president of academic affairs and chairman of molecular medicine. His research on protein folding and aggregation has been recognized by several scientific societies. His laboratory uses chemical, biophysical and biological methods to study how proteins misfold and aggregate in diseases such as Alzheimer's and transthyretin amyloidosis. This work led to tafamidis, a small-molecule stabilizer of transthyretin that became an approved treatment for familial amyloid polyneuropathy and transthyretin cardiomyopathy.

title: Rackspace Technology
text:
Rackspace Technology
Rackspace Technology is a cloud computing company based in San Antonio, Texas, with offices and data centers in several countries. Richard Yoo, Dirk Elmendorf and Patrick Condon founded the business in 1996. It grew out of Cymitar Technology Group, which Yoo started in a garage after leaving Trinity University to sell internet access to former classmates. Graham Weston and Morris Miller supplied seed capital and began managing the company two years later, when it adopted the Rackspace name. Weston became chief executive in 1998. In 2008, Rackspace moved its headquarters into the previously vacant Windsor Park Mall in Windcrest, Texas.

title: Kenneth Harris — Academy of Europe CV
text:
Kenneth Harris — Academy of Europe CV
Kenneth Harris studied mathematics at Cambridge, receiving a first-class honours BA and then a Certificate of Advanced Study. His PhD in neural computation at University College London was supervised by Michael Recce and titled Memory and Spatial Function in Animals and Robots. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Rutgers University from 1999 to 2003. He became a reader in neurotechnology at Imperial College London in 2009. In 2012 he became professor of quantitative neuroscience at UCL. His honours include an Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship in 2005. His recent research includes brainwide organization of neuronal activity, learning-related changes in neural population codes and transcriptomic analysis of brain cells in Alzheimer's disease models. He has also been part of the International Brain Laboratory, a multi-institution collaboration studying brain activity during behavior.

title: Jude Vaclavik — composer biography, September 2021
text:
Jude Vaclavik — composer biography, September 2021
Jude Vaclavik, a native of Houston, Texas, earned his bachelor’s, master’s and Doctor of Musical Arts in music composition at Juilliard, studying with Christopher Rouse and John Corigliano. He began his publishing career at Boosey & Hawkes. By September 2021 he was director of US Classical Publishing and Promotion at G. Ricordi & Co., New York. He had held posts at Houston Grand Opera, Juilliard, and Utah State University. His commissioners included the New York Philharmonic, Lubbock Symphony Orchestra, and New York Youth Symphony. His work had been recognised by the American Academy of Arts and Letters and ASCAP. His compositions include works for orchestra and chamber ensembles.

title: Allan MacDonald — Wolf Foundation biography
text:
Allan MacDonald — Wolf Foundation biography
Allan MacDonald received his BSc from St. Francis Xavier University in 1973. His MSc and PhD in physics came from the University of Toronto in 1974 and 1978, respectively. He worked on the research staff of the National Research Council of Canada from 1978 to 1987. He taught at Indiana University from 1987 to 2000, then moved to the University of Texas at Austin in 2000. The Wolf Foundation biography identifies him as the holder of the Sid W. Richardson Chair in Physics. The Wolf Foundation describes the work as showing that the electronic properties of graphene interfaces can be controlled by rotating one layer relative to the other. In 2011, MacDonald and Rafi Bistritzer calculated that electron tunnelling velocity in twisted bilayer graphene could vanish at a misfit angle of about 1.1 degrees, a value later associated with the material's so-called magic angle. The foundation notes that this theoretical result was initially overlooked before later experiments drew renewed attention to the system.

title: Katherine High — education and early career
text:
Katherine High — education and early career
Katherine High was born in High Point, North Carolina. She received an AB in chemistry at Harvard in 1972 and an MD at the University of North Carolina in 1978. After an internal medicine residency, she became a hematology fellow at Yale under Edward J. Benz Jr. She was a faculty member at UNC-Chapel Hill for seven years. She later cofounded Spark Therapeutics, serving as president and chief scientific officer. At the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, High led bench-to-bedside studies of gene therapy for hemophilia, including early clinical trials using adeno-associated viral vectors in human muscle and liver. Her research also examined how the human immune system responds to AAV delivery and helped develop approaches intended to improve the safety and effectiveness of treatment. In 2013 she cofounded Spark Therapeutics, where the team advanced Luxturna, the first gene therapy approved in the United States for an inherited disease.

title: FilmQuest
text:
FilmQuest
FilmQuest is an annual international festival in Provo, Utah, devoted to fantasy, science fiction, horror, and related genre films, with programs that include premieres and awards. Filmmaker Jonathan Martin founded it in 2014 and has served as its director. The festival screens feature-length and short films, bringing together filmmakers, performers, industry representatives, and audiences. Screenings take place at the Velour Live Music Gallery, with question-and-answer sessions and events for attending filmmakers. An international jury awards prizes in multiple categories, including Best Feature Film and the Grand Prize Best Short Film, which was introduced in 2023. The festival's organizers describe FilmQuest as a filmmaker-founded event intended to support emerging artists and help established filmmakers advance their careers. Its first edition ran from June 30 to July 5, 2014, in Salt Lake City, after FilmQuest began as the genre-film branch of the newly formed FantasyCon. The festival's official history records that its program grew to include feature films, short films, student work, animation, music videos and screenplay competitions.

title: Anjali Goswami — government biography
text:
Anjali Goswami — government biography
Anjali Goswami received a BSc from the University of Michigan in 1998 and a PhD from the University of Chicago in 2005. A US National Science Foundation fellowship took her to the Natural History Museum. She subsequently held a junior research fellowship at King’s College, Cambridge, and a lectureship in Earth Sciences at Cambridge. Her principal fossil fieldwork has been based in South India. On July 1, 2025, she became Chief Scientific Adviser at Defra and Director General for Science, Data and Analysis. Her research group develops methods for measuring the complex three-dimensional shapes of organisms and uses those measurements to reconstruct patterns of biodiversity through evolutionary time. Although her work spans insects and dinosaurs, her principal scientific interest is the evolution of mammals. Her field research has included fossil searches from Svalbard to Madagascar, with much of her primary fieldwork carried out in South India. She was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2024 and has received medals from the Linnean Society and the Zoological Society of London.

title: List of launch service providers
text:
List of launch service providers
A launch service provider delivers payloads such as satellites, spacecraft, cargo or astronauts into space. Its responsibilities can include obtaining the rocket, preparing facilities, integrating the payload and conducting the launch. These companies do not necessarily manufacture every vehicle or component themselves, and may subcontract parts of the work. An Interface Control Document sets out the integration and mission responsibilities of the provider and its customer. The European Space Agency's Flight Ticket Initiative co-funds launch opportunities for European organisations seeking to demonstrate or validate new satellite technologies in orbit. The first providers contracted through the scheme were Arianespace, Isar Aerospace, PLD Space, Orbex and Rocket Factory Augsburg. Those companies compete for specific launch work orders, while the initiative restricts supported missions to European-manufactured launchers funded through Horizon Europe and ESA's Boost! programme.

title: Appointment of Semyon Bychkov as Music Director of the Opéra national de Paris
text:
Appointment of Semyon Bychkov as Music Director of the Opéra national de Paris
The Paris Opera announced Semyon Bychkov’s appointment as Music Director on 6 January 2026. His four-season term would begin on 1 August 2028. Before that, he would work with its musical ensembles as Appointed Music Director from 1 August 2026. In the appointed-director role he would oversee artistic quality across the orchestra, chorus and vocal coaches, and help plan programmes and musician auditions. His later duties as Music Director would include conducting two opera productions and six symphonic concert programmes in each season. Previous Paris Opera projects with Bychkov included Un ballo in maschera in 2007, Tristan und Isolde in 2008 and Elektra in 2022.

title: VMware
text:
VMware
VMware is a cloud computing and virtualization company based in Palo Alto, California. It developed commercially successful virtualization for the x86 computer architecture. Its desktop products run on Windows, Linux and macOS, while its ESXi hypervisor runs directly on server hardware. Broadcom acquired VMware on 22 November 2023 in a transaction valued at $69 billion. VMware’s End-User Computing division was subsequently sold to KKR and renamed Omnissa. VMware's software portfolio has included products for cloud computing, application modernization, networking, security and digital workspaces. The company states that its software supports infrastructure used by organisations of different sizes and operates across cloud environments. After Broadcom completed its acquisition in November, VMware, Inc. became VMware by Broadcom, also referred to as VMware LLC in company materials.

title: Lauren Collins Learns to Love in French
text:
Lauren Collins Learns to Love in French
Lauren Collins moved to Geneva after her husband Olivier relocated there for work. They had met and established their relationship in London, speaking English, while her limited French made everyday tasks in Switzerland difficult. Olivier had studied English for many years, including during a teenage stay with a family in New York State. He later studied mathematics in England and pursued a doctorate in California, gradually becoming a fluent English speaker after initially struggling to communicate in both countries. The article recounts that Olivier had studied English for more than a decade before moving to England, yet his first university roommate told him after six weeks that he had initially been unable to speak the language. After England, he moved to California for doctoral study and struggled at first while teaching a freshman calculus course. In 2007, he took an English-language assessment to obtain an amateur pilot licence; the examiner rated his spoken English at the highest level, describing it as fluent and stylistically flexible. Olivier also spoke Spanish, learned through the language of his maternal grandparents.

title: Ziff Davis — 2024 annual report
text:
Ziff Davis — 2024 annual report
Ziff Davis, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware in 2014 through a holding-company structure, as j2 Global, Inc., with the stock ticker JCOM. Its October 7, 2021 cloud fax separation accompanied the adoption of the Ziff Davis name and a change of ticker to ZD. The 2024 annual report located its principal executive offices at 360 Park Avenue S, New York, New York 10010. Common stock had a par value of $0.01 per share. At December 31, 2024, the company had approximately 3,800 employees. The 2024 filing groups the company into five reportable segments: Technology and Shopping; Gaming and Entertainment; Health and Wellness; Connectivity; and Cybersecurity and Martech. The filing describes the first segment as earning revenue from advertising, commerce sites and specialized technology content, while Gaming and Entertainment includes editorial coverage and storefront sales for games, books and software. Health and Wellness combines consumer tools and applications with professional education and information services. Connectivity supplies data and services related to broadband access and network performance, while Cybersecurity and Martech provides cloud software for communication, security, privacy and customer engagement.

title: Max Planck Institute for Coal Research
text:
Max Planck Institute for Coal Research
The Max Planck Institute for Coal Research is a chemical research institute in Mülheim an der Ruhr, Germany. It was founded in 1912 as the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Coal Research and became an independent Max Planck Institute in 1949. Its research covers organic and organometallic chemistry, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, and theoretical chemistry, with an emphasis on selective, environmentally benign methods of making compounds and materials. Franz Fischer and Hans Tropsch developed the Fischer–Tropsch process there in 1925, and Karl Ziegler later worked at the institute. The institute's original programme sought better ways to convert coal into liquid fuels and to use its energy more efficiently, including research into direct conversion of coal energy into electricity. After Karl Ziegler became director in 1943, he shifted the institute away from mainly application-oriented work toward basic research in general synthetic chemistry. That change placed catalysis at the centre of the institute's scientific programme. In 1953, researchers filed an early patent for low-pressure polyethylene synthesis, an important development in polymer chemistry.

title: Paul Bates — hydrology education and career
text:
Paul Bates — hydrology education and career
Paul Bates graduated in geography at the University of Southampton in 1989 and completed his PhD at Bristol in 1993. He cofounded the water-risk intelligence company Fathom. He directed Bristol’s Cabot Institute from 2011 to 2013 and headed its School of Geographical Sciences from 2013 to 2017. He is noted for developing the LISFLOOD-FP hydrodynamic model. His honours include a CBE in 2019, election to the Royal Society in 2021 and the John Dalton Medal in 2024. His research combines numerical modelling with satellite observations to investigate flood inundation. His work addresses the prediction of flood extent and water depth across large geographical areas. He has also studied uncertainty in flood-risk assessment.

title: Singapore Symphony Orchestra
text:
Singapore Symphony Orchestra
The Singapore Symphony Orchestra was established in 1979, with Choo Hoey as its music director and resident conductor. Its main concert venue is the Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay, although it also performs at the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall. The orchestra gives more than 60 concerts a year and forms part of the Singapore Symphony Group, which also manages youth ensembles and music competitions. The orchestra gave its inaugural concert on 24 January 1979 at the Singapore Conference Hall. Its repertoire combines the Western symphonic tradition with works by Singaporean and other Asian composers. The orchestra has made numerous commercial recordings for the Swedish record label BIS.

title: Jan Holmgren — research and career profile
text:
Jan Holmgren — research and career profile
Jan Holmgren trained in medicine and research at the University of Gothenburg, earning an MD and a Doctor of Medical Sciences. He worked as a scientist for the Swedish Medical Research Council from 1970 to 1980, then became professor of medical microbiology and head of Gothenburg's Department of Microbiology and Immunology. His research led to Dukoral, the first oral cholera vaccine to be internationally licensed and WHO-prequalified. His scientific honors include the Sabin Gold Medal and Prince Mahidol Award in Public Health. Holmgren's research has also addressed mucosal immunity, particularly how immune responses at intestinal surfaces can be stimulated by vaccination. He collaborated with Ann-Mari Svennerholm on the development of oral vaccines against cholera and enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli.

title: Pablo Jarillo-Herrero — MIT biographical sketch
text:
Pablo Jarillo-Herrero — MIT biographical sketch
Pablo Jarillo-Herrero received his physics licenciatura from the University of Valencia in 1999 and an MSc at the University of California, San Diego. He earned his PhD at Delft University of Technology in 2005 and stayed for a one-year postdoc. He then worked at Columbia University as a NanoResearch Initiative Fellow. He joined MIT as an assistant professor in January 2008, received tenure in 2015, and became a full professor in 2018. He was elected to the US National Academy of Sciences in 2022. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero is the Cecil and Ida Green Professor of Physics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

title: Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2025
text:
Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2025
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 won the Game of the Year award at The Game Awards 2025. The 2025 ceremony took place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles and was hosted by Geoff Keighley. The winning game led the nominations with 13 and received nine awards during the event. Its other wins included awards for narrative, art direction, score and music, and role-playing game design. The annual event was the twelfth edition of the awards and included newly announced games alongside presentations of trophies. Organizers reported more than 171 million worldwide livestreams of the 2025 presentation. The show also presented a Game Changer honour to Girls Make Games, an organisation supporting young women entering game development.

title: RAPT Therapeutics — 2024 annual report
text:
RAPT Therapeutics — 2024 annual report
RAPT Therapeutics was incorporated in Delaware in March 2015 under the name FLX Bio, Inc. It adopted the RAPT Therapeutics name in May 2019. Its 2024 annual report located the principal offices at 561 Eccles Avenue, South San Francisco, California 94080. At December 31, 2024, it had 68 employees: 46 in research and development and 22 in general and administrative functions. Twenty-three full-time employees had a PhD or another advanced science or medical degree. The company’s 2024 Form 10-K describes research programmes intended to develop antibodies for inflammatory and allergic conditions. The report also includes information on clinical studies, regulatory risks and the cost of developing candidate therapies. Its securities traded publicly on Nasdaq, and the filing details operating results for the financial year ended December 31, 2024.

title: HackerOne
text:
HackerOne
HackerOne is a cybersecurity company whose business centers on bug bounties and coordinated vulnerability disclosure, using outside researchers to find weaknesses in websites, applications and servers. Jobert Abma and Michiel Prins began examining the security of 100 technology companies in 2011 and reported the flaws they found. Their contact with Facebook’s security team brought them together with Alex Rice, and the three founded HackerOne with Merijn Terheggen in 2012. By December 2022, its network had distributed more than $230 million in bounties. Customers have included the United States departments of State and Defense, as well as GitHub, Google, Microsoft and PayPal.

title: VIREON
text:
VIREON
VIREON is an Earth observation satellite constellation developed by AAC Clyde Space in Glasgow with support from the UK and European space agencies. It is intended to provide near-real-time images of crops, forests and water resources for agricultural and land management applications. The first two satellites, both 16U CubeSats, reached low Earth orbit in March 2026 aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-16 mission. VIREON is a British satellite constellation. The launch vehicle used for the first two satellites was SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket. The constellation's monitoring is intended to increase productivity in agriculture, forestry and land management. It is also intended to reduce the environmental impact of those activities.

title: Clear Secure
text:
Clear Secure
Clear Secure is a biometrics technology company headquartered in New York City that operates identity and travel-document checks at airports and stadiums. Founded in 2003, the company closed after entering bankruptcy in 2009. Caryn Seidman-Becker and Ken Cornick bought the business in 2010 and relaunched it in 2012. It went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021 as Clear Secure, using the ticker YOU. Clear operates with the permission of partner airports, which receive commissions when customers sign up for new memberships. Steven Brill and Ajay Amlani were Clear's original owners. Clear received certification under the SAFETY Act from the United States Department of Homeland Security in June 2012. Los Angeles International Airport receives 12.5% of Clear's revenue generated at the airport.

title: Wolfgang Baumeister — Max Planck CV
text:
Wolfgang Baumeister — Max Planck CV
Wolfgang Baumeister was born in Wesseling near Cologne in 1946. He studied biology at the universities of Münster and Bonn and completed his doctorate at Düsseldorf in 1973. He obtained his habilitation in biophysics at Düsseldorf in 1978 and held a Heisenberg scholarship in Cambridge. He became a director and scientific member at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry in 1988. He completed doctoral studies at Düsseldorf University in 1973 and a habilitation in biophysics there in 1978. He later held a Heisenberg scholarship at Cambridge and joined the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry as a research-group leader in 1981. His honours have included the Otto Warburg Medal and the Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine. He also received the Shaw Prize in 2025 for contributions to biological research.

title: Tottenham Hotspur — March 2026 head-coach appointment
text:
Tottenham Hotspur — March 2026 head-coach appointment
On March 31, 2026, Tottenham Hotspur announced Roberto De Zerbi as men's head coach on a long-term contract, subject to a work permit. Sporting director Johan Lange said he had been the club's first choice for the summer and welcomed his earlier arrival. De Zerbi said the immediate priority was to climb the Premier League table. His most recent club, Marseille, had finished second in the French league in 2024–2025. The club’s sporting director Johan Lange said its coaching search had initially targeted a summer appointment. De Zerbi previously led Sassuolo and Shakhtar Donetsk and won the Ukrainian Super Cup while managing the latter. At Brighton he achieved the club’s then-highest Premier League finish and qualified for European competition.

title: Chris Grassie
text:
Chris Grassie
Chris Grassie is an English football coach who became head coach of Marshall University’s men’s soccer team in January 2017. He played at Alderson Broaddus, where he captained the team and studied political science and history. His coaching career began there before assistant roles at Marshall and the University of Michigan. He then spent six seasons leading the University of Charleston, winning six conference tournaments and five regular-season titles. His Charleston teams reached three NCAA Division II Final Fours and twice finished runners-up. At Marshall, Grassie led the Thundering Herd to the 2020 NCAA national championship and received the United Soccer Coaches college coaching award.

title: Apple — Q.ai acquisition
text:
Apple — Q.ai acquisition
On January 29, 2026, Apple announced it had bought Israeli audio AI startup Q.ai. The acquired team included CEO Aviad Maizels among a total of one hundred employees. Apple did not release a purchase price, although a person familiar with the transaction put the startup’s valuation at approximately $1.6 billion. Q.ai worked on machine-learning techniques for understanding whispered speech and improving audio in noisy settings. A patent application also described detecting subtle facial-skin movements to identify mouthed words and estimate physiological indicators. The company had received backing from Matter Venture Partners, Kleiner Perkins, Spark Capital, Exor and GV. The transaction was announced without any stated plan for integrating the acquired technology into a particular Apple product. The startup’s staff included co-founders Yonatan Wexler and Avi Barliya, both of whom were expected to join Apple.

title: SentinelOne
text:
SentinelOne
SentinelOne is an American cybersecurity company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 2013 by Tomer Weingarten, Almog Cohen and Ehud Shamir. Its software uses machine learning to monitor computers, connected devices and cloud workloads. The company completed its New York Stock Exchange flotation in June 2021, raising $1.2 billion and trading under the symbol S. It acquired the data analytics platform Scalyr in 2021 and the identity detection and response company Attivo Networks in 2022. Tomer Weingarten serves as the company's CEO. The company has approximately 2,800 employees and offices in Mountain View, Boston, Prague, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv. In June 2019, SentinelOne received $120 million in a Series D funding round led by Insight Partners. Since 2021, SentinelOne has been the official cybersecurity sponsor of the Aston Martin Cognizant F1 Team.

title: Symphony
text:
Symphony
A symphony is an extended composition in Western classical music, usually written for orchestra. By the late eighteenth century, the term generally described a work in several movements, often three or four, with the opening movement in sonata form. A typical symphony uses strings, woodwind, brass, and percussion. The complete score contains every instrumental part, while individual musicians read music written for their own instruments. Some symphonies also include singers, as in Beethoven’s Ninth and Mahler’s Second, although vocal writing is not a requirement of the form. The word symphony derives from the Greek symphōnía, meaning "agreement or concord of sound". In late Greek and medieval theory, the word was used for consonance. The Italian overture is often considered the direct forerunner of the orchestral symphony. The terms "overture", "symphony" and "sinfonia" were widely regarded as interchangeable for much of the eighteenth century.

title: Introducing GPT-5.4
text:
Introducing GPT-5.4
OpenAI released GPT-5.4 on 5 March 2026 in ChatGPT, the API and Codex. The ChatGPT version was called GPT-5.4 Thinking, and a Pro version was also made available in ChatGPT and the API. The release combined reasoning, coding and tool use for professional tasks involving documents, presentations and spreadsheets. In Codex and the API, it supported computer use and a context window of up to one million tokens. GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer. A context window specifies the amount of text a model can consider within a single interaction. An application programming interface allows developers to integrate model capabilities into their own software.

title: Manfred Honeck
text:
Manfred Honeck
Manfred Honeck was born in Austria and completed his musical training at the University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna. Before becoming a conductor, he played viola with the Vienna Philharmonic and the Vienna State Opera Orchestra. He began conducting as an assistant to Claudio Abbado and as director of the Vienna Jeunesse Orchestra. A subsequent engagement at Zurich Opera House brought him the European Conducting Prize in 1993. In 2023, the Bamberg Symphony Orchestra appointed him honorary conductor after many years of collaboration. Honeck became music director of the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra in 2008. He served as music director of the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra from 2000 to 2006.

title: Academy Award for Best Director
text:
Academy Award for Best Director
The Academy Award for Best Director is presented each year by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences to recognize achievement in film direction. At the first ceremony in 1929, directing was divided into dramatic and comedy categories, won respectively by Frank Borzage for 7th Heaven and Lewis Milestone for Two Arabian Knights. The categories were combined for subsequent ceremonies. Nominees are chosen by the Academy’s directors branch using the single transferable vote, while eligible members across the Academy select the winner through a plurality vote. The award is officially known as the Academy Award of Merit for Directing. John Ford has received the most awards in this category, with four. William Wyler holds the record for the most nominations, with 12. Lina Wertmüller was the first woman nominated in the category, for Seven Beauties (1976). Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the award, for The Hurt Locker (2009).

title: Brendan Rodgers
text:
Brendan Rodgers
Brendan Rodgers is a Northern Irish football manager and former defender who began his playing career at Ballymena United. He moved to Reading at 18, but a genetic knee condition ended his professional playing career two years later. After coaching at Reading, he joined Chelsea’s youth setup in 2004 and became reserve-team manager in 2006. He subsequently managed Watford and Reading before taking Swansea City into the Premier League in 2011. Rodgers joined Liverpool in 2012 and led the club to second place in the 2013–14 league season, won domestic trebles with Celtic and later guided Leicester City to the 2021 FA Cup.
