title: Holberg and Nils Klim Prizes — 2026 announcement
text:
Holberg and Nils Klim Prizes — 2026 announcement
On March 17, 2026, the Holberg Prize named historian Lyndal Roper its 2026 laureate. The award carried NOK 6 million and was due to be presented at the University of Bergen on June 4. The same announcement named Danish psychologist Majse Lind the recipient of the Nils Klim Prize. Lind was recognized for interdisciplinary research on mental health, including work with young people and older adults. Roper’s scholarship has examined early modern European witch trials, the Reformation and the German Peasants’ War. Her 2004 book Witch Craze drew on trial archives from southern Germany to study beliefs about gender, ageing and witchcraft.

title: List of football clubs in Argentina
text:
List of football clubs in Argentina
Argentina’s football clubs compete in national divisions and in lower leagues organized around different forms of affiliation with the Argentine Football Association. The two national divisions are the Primera Division and Primera B Nacional. Below them, directly affiliated clubs are mainly located in Greater Buenos Aires, with others in Buenos Aires and Santa Fe provinces. Clubs in the rest of the country are affiliated indirectly through their local leagues, forming a separate branch of the league structure below the national divisions. Directly affiliated clubs below Primera B Nacional play in Primera B Metropolitana, Primera C and Primera D. Indirectly affiliated clubs below that level play in Argentino A, Argentino B and Argentino C. These leagues make up the first five tiers of Argentine football. Below the fifth tier, indirectly affiliated clubs compete in various regional leagues.

title: Roberto De Zerbi — playing career and first coaching posts
text:
Roberto De Zerbi — playing career and first coaching posts
Roberto De Zerbi began his playing career at AC Milan and later made his Serie A debut with Napoli. He played for CFR Cluj in Romania before returning to Italy in 2013 for a final playing spell at Trento. His coaching career began with Darfo Boario in Serie D before he moved to Foggia in Serie C. He later coached Palermo, Benevento and Sassuolo before moving to Shakhtar Donetsk in 2021. De Zerbi started in youth and lower-division football before later managing Foggia, Palermo, Benevento and Sassuolo. At Benevento his team gained attention for an attacking approach, including an unlikely draw with AC Milan after a stoppage-time goalkeeper goal. He spent three seasons at Sassuolo and led the team to successive eighth-place finishes in Serie A.

title: Ravi Bellamkonda — Emory career biography, 2021
text:
Ravi Bellamkonda — Emory career biography, 2021
Ravi Bellamkonda earned a PhD in medical science at Brown, with a dissertation on nerve regeneration. His MIT postdoctoral appointment was as a Markey Fellow in Brain and Cognitive Sciences. He began his academic career at Case Western Reserve before joining Emory and Georgia Tech in 2003. He chaired their biomedical engineering department from 2013 to 2016, then spent five years as dean of Duke’s Pratt School of Engineering. Emory named him provost in 2021. His wife is Lalita Kaligotla, and their goldendoodle was named CJ. Before returning to Emory in 2021, Bellamkonda served for five years as dean of Duke University’s Pratt School of Engineering. At Duke he helped expand experiential learning and team-based design projects in the first-year engineering curriculum. He also earlier held a joint faculty appointment at Emory and Georgia Tech and chaired their biomedical engineering department.

title: Vasily Belokurov — Cambridge curriculum vitae
text:
Vasily Belokurov — Cambridge curriculum vitae
Vasily Belokurov completed a combined bachelor’s and master’s degree in astronomy at Moscow State University’s Sternberg Astronomical Institute in 1999. His Cambridge CV lists a 2004 PhD in theoretical physics from Oxford. He was a Cambridge research associate in 2003–2006, an STFC postdoctoral fellow in 2006–2008, and a Royal Society University Research Fellow in 2008–2013. He became a university lecturer in 2011 and professor of astronomy in 2019. He visited the Flatiron Institute’s Center for Computational Astrophysics in 2017–2018 and 2021–2022, and received the Aaronson Prize in 2015 and RAS Fowler Prize in 2011. He uses large astronomical surveys to reconstruct the history of the Milky Way through Galactic Archaeology. He was Reader in Astrophysics at Cambridge’s Institute of Astronomy from 2014 to 2018. He was principal investigator for the European Research Council’s “Streams” Starting Grant from 2013 to 2018.

title: Esa-Pekka Salonen — musical background
text:
Esa-Pekka Salonen — musical background
Esa-Pekka Salonen was born in Helsinki, Finland, on June 30, 1958. He began studying French horn with Holger Fransman at age 11 and later trained at the Sibelius Academy, earning degrees in horn and conducting. In 1980 he helped found the experimental music ensemble Toimii with fellow Finnish musicians and composers. His Finnish conducting debut was with the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra in 1979. His 1983 London debut with the Philharmonia Orchestra came as a last-minute replacement for Michael Tilson Thomas. Salonen received the 2024 Polar Music Prize at a ceremony in Stockholm attended by other laureates and guest performers. One performance featured Stravinsky’s Octet for Wind Instruments with musicians drawn from Swedish orchestras. The prize foundation traces his international conducting breakthrough to a 1983 performance of Mahler’s Third Symphony. He also writes orchestral music and explores technological tools to make classical performances more accessible.

title: Jo Jin-kyu
text:
Jo Jin-kyu
Jo Jin-kyu is a South Korean film director born in 1960. Before directing features, he worked as a script editor on Agada in 1984 and as an assistant director on Good Morning, Ms. President in 1989. His directorial debut was the gangster comedy My Wife Is a Gangster in 2001, and he returned to the series for its third film in 2006. He directed and executive-produced Man on the Edge in 2013. In 2016, he directed Sweet Sixteen, a Korean-Chinese production starring Joo Won. His television work includes Bolder By the Day. He directed Who's Got the Tape? in 2004. Bolder By the Day aired on MBN from 2011 to 2012.

title: Arcellx — 2024 annual report
text:
Arcellx — 2024 annual report
Arcellx was incorporated in Delaware in December 2014 as Encarta Therapeutics, Inc. Its 2024 annual report placed the principal executive offices in Redwood City, California. Its common stock traded as ACLX on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, with a par value of $0.001 per share. At December 31, 2024, it had 163 full-time employees, including 112 engaged in research and development. The filing describes a biotechnology business focused on immune-cell therapies and the development of candidates for serious diseases. It discusses research, regulatory milestones, collaboration agreements and the uncertainty of clinical development. The annual report covers the 2024 financial year and includes risk factors and audited financial statements.

title: Stanford Woosley — education and early appointments
text:
Stanford Woosley — education and early appointments
Stanford Woosley earned a BS in physics at Rice University in 1966 and a PhD in astrophysics there in 1971. He was a research associate at Rice from 1971 to 1973, then a research fellow at the California Institute of Technology's Kellogg Radiation Laboratory from 1973 to 1975. He became an assistant professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz in 1975, an associate professor in 1978 and a professor in 1983. His CV gives his birthplace as Texarkana, Texas. He began serving as a consultant to Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in 1974. He chaired the astronomy department at the University of California, Santa Cruz from 1983 to 1987 and from 1989 to 1991. From 1996 to 1998, he was an A. V. Humboldt Professor at the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Garching, Germany.

title: Lyndal Roper — Australian women’s history encyclopedia
text:
Lyndal Roper — Australian women’s history encyclopedia
Lyndal Roper graduated from the University of Melbourne in 1977 with an honours degree in history with philosophy. Historian Charles Zika encouraged her to pursue postgraduate research. Her doctoral work at King's College, University of London, was supervised by Bob Scribner. Her first book, The Holy Household: Women and Morals in Reformation Augsburg, appeared in 1989. Roper graduated with honours in history and philosophy in 1977 after studying the German Reformation. Her undergraduate research explored the preacher Andreas Osiander and questions of religious authority in early modern Nuremberg. A scholarship from the German Academic Exchange Service then supported archival research at Tübingen and other German cities. The early research examined women’s lives and household relationships through town and criminal records.

title: Daniel Harding — Mahler Foundation biography
text:
Daniel Harding — Mahler Foundation biography
Daniel Harding studied trumpet at Chetham's School of Music and joined the National Youth Orchestra at thirteen. After hearing a recording of his conducting, Simon Rattle hired him as an assistant at the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra for 1993–1994. He then spent a year at Cambridge before becoming Claudio Abbado's assistant with the Berlin Philharmonic. Away from music, he is a fan of Manchester United. From 1998 to 2003, Harding was Principal Guest Conductor of the Mahler Chamber Orchestra. He became the orchestra's Music Director in 2003. In 2007, he assumed the position of Principal Conductor. He has been the orchestra's Conductor Laureate since 2011.

title: Fiona Wood — Australian Academy of Science interview
text:
Fiona Wood — Australian Academy of Science interview
Fiona Wood was born in Yorkshire, England, in 1958. She graduated from St Thomas’ Hospital Medical School in London in 1981 and immigrated to Australia in 1987. She took a plastic-surgery registrar position at Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital in Perth and became a consultant in 1991. She co-developed Cellspray in 1995. In 1999 she founded Clinical Cell Culture with Marie Stoner. Wood completed her internship and residency at several hospitals in London before immigrating to Australia. She began working with medical scientist Marie Stoner in 1993 on burns treatment at Royal Perth and Princess Margaret hospitals. Cellspray is a spray-on solution of skin cells. Her expertise in burns treatment gained international recognition after the 2002 Bali bombings. She was interviewed by Dr Norman Swan in 2008.

title: Relativity Space Closes $140 Million Series C Funding Round Led by Bond and Tribe Capital
text:
Relativity Space Closes $140 Million Series C Funding Round Led by Bond and Tribe Capital
Tim Ellis and Jordan Noone founded Relativity Space in 2015 to develop an automated rocket factory and launch services for satellite constellations. Its factory combines robotics with autonomous 3D manufacturing to produce the Terran 1 rocket. The company described a design with one hundredth as many parts as conventional rockets and a production process intended to take less than 60 days from raw material to flight. Its investors included Bond, Tribe Capital, Playground Global, Y Combinator, Social Capital and Mark Cuban. Terran 1 had a payload capacity of up to 1250 kg. Both the Stargate factory and Terran 1 were completely designed, built, and operated in the United States.

title: Park Chan-wook, President of the Jury of the 79th Festival de Cannes
text:
Park Chan-wook, President of the Jury of the 79th Festival de Cannes
On 26 February 2026, the Festival de Cannes announced that South Korean filmmaker Park Chan-wook would chair the competition jury at its 79th edition. He became the first Korean filmmaker chosen for the role. His jury was scheduled to present the Palme d’Or at the Grand Théâtre Lumière on 23 May. Park’s association with Cannes included the 2004 Grand Prix for Old Boy. The announcement credited him with twelve feature films and described his work as a director, screenwriter and producer. The festival stated that his appointment would be the first time a Korean film-maker had presided over its feature-film competition jury. His earlier Cannes recognitions included the Grand Prix for Oldboy in 2004 and a Jury Prize for Thirst in 2009. Decision to Leave later received the festival’s Best Director award in 2022.

title: Janet Thornton — EMBL-EBI career retrospective
text:
Janet Thornton — EMBL-EBI career retrospective
Janet Thornton directed EMBL’s European Bioinformatics Institute from 2001 to 2015 and retired in summer 2023. With Roman Laskowski, she developed ProCheck software to assess the quality of protein structures. With Christine Orengo, she introduced the CATH classification of protein structures. She led the establishment of ELIXIR, an intergovernmental organisation connecting European life-science data resources. The Janet Thornton Fellowship funds researchers returning after a career break. She was appointed a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire in the 2012 Birthday Honours for services to bioinformatics. During her directorship, the institute grew from 160 to over 600 people. She began her career by trying to predict protein structures from sequence. Her work at EMBL spanned structural biology, bioinformatics, biological chemistry and chemoinformatics.

title: Real Madrid — January 2026 first-team coach announcement
text:
Real Madrid — January 2026 first-team coach announcement
Real Madrid announced Álvaro Arbeloa as its new first-team coach on January 12, 2026. He had coached Castilla since June 2025 and had worked in the club's youth academy since 2020. His youth-team assignments included the Under-14s, Under-16s and Under-19s. With the Under-19s he won the league, Copa del Rey and Champions Cup in the 2022–2023 season. Arbeloa had coached Real Madrid Castilla since June 2025 after working with several youth teams from 2020 onward. He led the under-nineteens to a domestic treble in the 2022–23 season and another league title in 2024–25. As a Real Madrid player he made 238 official appearances between 2009 and 2016 and won two European Cups.

title: Phoenix Symphony names its next music director in 2026
text:
Phoenix Symphony names its next music director in 2026
On March 10, 2026, the Phoenix Symphony named Paolo Bortolameolli its next Virginia G. Piper Music Director. He was to serve as music director designate in 2026–2027 and assume the music directorship in 2027–2028. The board approved the appointment unanimously following a three-year international search involving the musicians. During the designate season he was scheduled to lead four programs and open the season. The board unanimously approved the selection after a three-year international search conducted with the orchestra’s players. The conductor was scheduled to lead four programmes during his designate season and open the orchestra’s 2026–27 concert season. The appointment made him the twelfth music director in the orchestra’s nearly eighty-year history.

title: Gilles Brassard — education and scientific collaboration
text:
Gilles Brassard — education and scientific collaboration
Gilles Brassard earned his bachelor's and master's degrees at the University of Montreal. At age 24, he completed a PhD in theoretical computer science at Cornell, working with John Hopcroft. In 1979 he met IBM physicist Charles Bennett while both were swimming off the coast of Puerto Rico. Brassard was taking a break from a theoretical computing conference, where he was presenting his graduate research on the mathematical foundations of cryptography. Brassard is a Canadian computer scientist and a faculty member at the University of Montreal. He received the 2025 Turing Award jointly with Charles Bennett for founding quantum information science and developing new encryption technology for secure communication and computing. Their BB84 system used particles of light to create encryption keys for locking and unlocking digital data.

title: Klaus Tennstedt
text:
Klaus Tennstedt
Klaus Tennstedt was a German conductor born in Merseburg in 1926. He studied violin and piano at the Leipzig Conservatory and became concertmaster of the Halle Municipal Theater orchestra in 1948. A finger injury ended his violin career, after which he worked as a voice coach and turned to conducting. He became music director of the Dresden Opera in 1958 and of the Schwerin State Orchestra and Theatre in 1962. After leaving East Germany in 1971, he obtained asylum in Sweden and conducted in Gothenburg and Stockholm. From 1983 to 1987, he was principal conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra, with which he recorded Mahler’s symphonies.

title: Donald Leo — Buffalo alumni profile, September 2024
text:
Donald Leo — Buffalo alumni profile, September 2024
Donald Leo earned his bachelor’s degree at Illinois Urbana-Champaign and his master’s and PhD at Buffalo, completing the latter degrees in 1992 and 1995. Before Georgia, he was a mechanical engineering professor and associate research dean at Virginia Tech. He was also a DARPA program manager, overseeing a $50 million interdisciplinary research portfolio. His research focused on smart materials, and he had been principal investigator on over 50 grants and contracts, with around $12 million in external funding. He served on Buffalo’s Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering advisory board. Leo was appointed executive vice president and provost of Ohio University. He previously served as the first dean of the College of Engineering at the University of Georgia. During his time at Georgia, he grew enrollment to over 2,700 students.

title: List of football clubs in England
text:
List of football clubs in England
The English men’s football league system includes clubs from England and clubs based elsewhere that compete in its leagues. The Premier League occupies level one, followed by the Championship, League One and League Two at levels two to four. The National League is level five, with its North and South divisions at level six. Below them, the Isthmian, Northern Premier and Southern leagues have premier divisions at level seven and further divisions at level eight. The list covers clubs down to Level 10 (Step 6). Regional Feeder Leagues start at Level 11, and the increasingly local leagues below extend down to Level 20.

title: Disney — chief executive succession announced in February 2026
text:
Disney — chief executive succession announced in February 2026
On February 3, 2026, Disney announced that its board had chosen Josh D'Amaro as the company's next chief executive, succeeding Robert Iger. The change would take effect at the annual shareholders' meeting on March 18. D'Amaro led Disney Experiences, which generated $36 billion in revenue in the 2025 financial year and employed 185,000 people. Disney also named Dana Walden as president and chief creative officer, with her appointment taking effect on the same date. Disney’s board selected D’Amaro by unanimous vote, with the leadership change set for its March 2026 annual meeting. At the time he led Disney Experiences, a division reporting approximately $36 billion in annual revenue and employing 185,000 people in fiscal 2025.

title: Swee Lay Thein — NIH career biography
text:
Swee Lay Thein — NIH career biography
Swee Lay Thein was educated in Malaysia and the United Kingdom and trained in hematology at the Royal Postgraduate Medical School and Royal Free Hospital in London. She joined the MRC Molecular Hematology Unit in Oxford in 1982. In 2000 she became professor of molecular hematology at King’s College London and clinical director of the Red Cell Centre. She joined the NHLBI in spring 2015. Since 2006 she has directed and hosted the Sickle Cell in Focus Conference. She became a fellow of the UK Academy of Medical Sciences in 2003. Her group conducts research on the pathophysiology of sickle cell disease, applying insights from genotype-phenotype observations to translate basic discoveries into therapeutic applications. In a 2007 genome-wide association study, her group identified BCL11A as a key repressor of the gamma-globin gene.

title: Michael Haynie — University of Delaware alumni profile
text:
Michael Haynie — University of Delaware alumni profile
J. Michael Haynie earned a political science BA from the University of Delaware in 1992. He received an MBA at the University of Oregon and a PhD in entrepreneurship and business strategy at the University of Colorado Boulder. Before his academic career, he served for 14 years as a commissioned officer in the United States Air Force. He was named a university professor at Syracuse in 2018 and received its Chancellor’s Medal in 2021. Haynie’s research has focused on entrepreneurship, business strategy and innovation, including programmes intended to help veterans and their families. His professional advisory work has involved the United States departments of Labor and Veterans Affairs, as well as the White House.

title: Phi (language model)
text:
Phi (language model)
Phi is Microsoft’s family of open-weight language models designed to run locally, including on consumer devices. Microsoft introduced the first model, Phi-1, on 21 June 2023 with 1.3 billion parameters. Phi-3-mini followed in April 2024, using 3.8 billion parameters and offering deployment through Azure as well as operation on a phone. Reviewers compared Phi-3-mini’s performance with that of GPT-3.5. Microsoft released the 15-billion-parameter vision-language model Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B in March 2026. That model can choose whether to produce a reasoning process before answering a prompt or respond without that additional step. The New York Times characterized Phi-3-mini as Microsoft's push into smaller language models.

title: Ohio State — presidential appointment in March 2026
text:
Ohio State — presidential appointment in March 2026
On March 12, 2026, Ohio State’s Board of Trustees appointed Ravi V. Bellamkonda the university’s 18th president, effective immediately. He had joined Ohio State the previous year as executive vice president and provost. As provost, Bellamkonda had helped prepare Ohio State’s strategic plan and guide the early stages of its implementation. Board chair John W. Zeiger announced the decision in a message addressed to students, faculty and staff. The university said it would provide further information about filling the provost position in the coming weeks. Bellamkonda’s wife, Lalita Kaligotla, was also described as a leader in Ohio State’s College of Nursing.

title: Fields Institute
text:
Fields Institute
The Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences is an independent nonprofit research centre with ties to 20 universities in Ontario. Founded in 1992, it was initially based at the University of Waterloo before moving to the University of Toronto in 1995, where it occupies a purpose-built building on the St. George campus. The institute is named after the Canadian mathematician John Charles Fields, whose name is also attached to the Fields Medal. It brings together mathematicians from Canada and abroad and encourages collaboration with researchers in statistics, computer science, engineering, medicine, economics and other fields, alongside monthly meetings on mathematics education.

title: Tatia Granger — William & Mary faculty CV
text:
Tatia Granger — William & Mary faculty CV
Tatia Granger earned a BA in French in 1989, an MEd in Social Foundations of Education in 1993, and a PhD in 1999, all at the University of Virginia. She received a Leadership Coaching Certificate from Georgetown in 2015 and a College Teaching Certificate from William & Mary in 2017. At William & Mary, she was university ombuds in 2008–2016 and an adjunct business professor in 2013–2017. Her earlier positions included Bennett College vice president for enrollment services in 2003–2005, Duke chief of staff to the CFO in 2000–2003, and James Madison multicultural student services director in 1994–1997. She served as assistant dean for undergraduate admission at the University of Virginia from 1990 to 1994. She became a clinical associate professor in organizational behavior at William & Mary's Raymond A. Mason School of Business in 2017. She has also served as adjunct faculty in leadership coaching at Georgetown University's Institute for Transformational Leadership since 2019.

title: Alan G. Hinnebusch — NAS biography
text:
Alan G. Hinnebusch — NAS biography
Alan Hinnebusch was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 1954 and grew up in Monroeville and Canton, Ohio. He graduated in biology from the University of Dayton in 1975 and earned a PhD in biochemistry and molecular biology at Harvard in 1980. He studied yeast genetics as a postdoctoral fellow with Gerald R. Fink, first at Cornell and later at MIT. In 1983 he became an independent investigator at the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development in Bethesda, Maryland. His research in the Section on Nutrient Control of Gene Expression investigates fundamental molecular mechanisms of eukaryotic gene regulation. The section uses Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a model organism to combine genetics, biochemistry, and structural biology in studying gene transcription and mRNA translation.

title: English National Opera
text:
English National Opera
English National Opera is a London opera company based at the London Coliseum in St Martin’s Lane. Its productions are performed in English. The company developed from theatrical and operatic performances organized at the Old Vic by Emma Cons and later her niece Lilian Baylis. It became a permanent ensemble at Sadler’s Wells during the 1930s and toured during the Second World War. In 1968 it moved to the Coliseum, adopting the name English National Opera in 1974. The company's repertoire has ranged from early operas by Monteverdi to new commissions, operetta and Broadway shows. Directors who have staged productions for the company include David Pountney, Jonathan Miller, Nicholas Hytner, Phyllida Lloyd and Calixto Bieito.

title: Space Missions
text:
Space Missions
The Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory has helped design, build, operate or lead more than seventy spacecraft missions. Its Dragonfly project will send a rotorcraft to Titan to investigate chemistry and habitability. Another planned mission, Lunar Vertex, will examine a lunar magnetic anomaly, its associated surface swirl and its small magnetosphere. The laboratory built and operates New Horizons, which conducted the first close flyby of Pluto in July 2015. It also built Parker Solar Probe, a NASA spacecraft launched in 2018 to study the Sun's outer atmosphere. Its NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft became the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid when it entered orbit around Eros in February 2000. The laboratory developed and operated the Double Asteroid Redirection Test, which struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos in September 2022 to demonstrate kinetic impact as a planetary defense technique.

title: Ian Derrer to lead The Dallas Opera
text:
Ian Derrer to lead The Dallas Opera
Ian Derrer was born in Rockport, Illinois, and moved with his family to the Charlotte area of North Carolina when he was six months old. Both parents sang in the Charlotte Opera chorus, and he began attending their rehearsals as a child. He remembered seeing The Magic Flute at about five and later singing Gherardino in Gianni Schicchi. His father’s record collection introduced him to singers including George London, whose performances of Boris Godunov and Duparc songs became favourites. A scholarship subsequently brought him to Southern Methodist University to study voice. His early voice lessons led him to train as a bass-baritone, influenced partly by recordings of George London and Norman Treigle. He later worked as an artistic administrator at Dallas Opera between 2014 and 2016, drawing on previous professional experience in Santa Fe and Chicago.

title: Shizuo Akira — Gairdner biography
text:
Shizuo Akira — Gairdner biography
Shizuo Akira received his MD from Osaka University in 1977 and completed a PhD there in 1984 after clinical training. From 1985 to 1987 he was a postdoctoral fellow in microbiology and immunology at the University of California, Berkeley. He then worked at Osaka University's Institute for Molecular and Cellular Biology in Tadamitsu Kishimoto's laboratory. He became a professor at Hyogo College of Medicine in 1996 and at Osaka's Research Institute for Microbial Diseases in 1999. In Kishimoto's laboratory, he cloned the transcription factors NF-IL6(C/EBPbeta) and STAT3. He became director of Osaka University's WPI Immunology Frontier Research Center in 2007. He won the 2011 Canada Gairdner International Award for discovering Toll like receptors and the microbial compounds they recognize to provide innate resistance to infection. He is a member of the National Academy of Sciences and the European Molecular Biology Organization. His other awards include the Robert Koch Prize, the William B. Coley Award, and the Keio International Medical Science Prize.

title: Joseph Henrich Curriculum Vitae
text:
Joseph Henrich Curriculum Vitae
Joseph Henrich graduated from the University of Notre Dame in 1991 with bachelor’s degrees in aerospace engineering and anthropology, both with high honours. He subsequently studied anthropology at the University of California, Los Angeles, receiving a master’s degree in 1995 and a doctorate in 1999. His July 2019 curriculum vitae listed him as professor and chair of Harvard University’s Department of Human Evolutionary Biology. His book The Secret of Our Success received a Canadian Institute for Advanced Research award in 2016. Henrich’s research examines cultural evolution and the relationship between culture and human psychology. With Steven J. Heine and Ara Norenzayan, he coauthored the 2010 article “The weirdest people in the world?”, which questioned the representativeness of populations commonly studied in behavioral science. His 2020 book The WEIRDest People in the World explores the historical development of psychological differences associated with Western societies.

title: Anthony Parnther — San Bernardino Symphony profile
text:
Anthony Parnther — San Bernardino Symphony profile
Anthony Parnther's hometown is Norfolk, Virginia, and his education includes Yale University and Northwestern University. He began conducting the San Bernardino Symphony in 2019 and serves as its music director. His performances champion works by Black, Latino and women composers, including Margaret Bonds, Florence Price and William Grant Still. Los Angeles television station KCET/TV profiled him as a Local Hero for that work. He led the Gateways Music Festival Orchestra's sold-out Carnegie Hall debut, featuring the world premiere of Jon Batiste's I Can. He led recording sessions for the Oscar-winning score for Oppenheimer. He also led scoring sessions for Encanto, The Mandalorian and Avatar: The Way of Water.

title: Citrix Systems
text:
Citrix Systems
Citrix Systems is an American technology company whose products include desktop and application virtualization, networking, cloud computing, and software services. Ed Iacobucci founded the business in Richardson, Texas, in 1989 and remained its chairman until 2000. Its early products enabled remote access to Microsoft operating systems, using source code licensed from Microsoft. Citrix subsequently developed thin-client technology that allowed dedicated devices to use applications and resources on remote servers. The company made its initial public offering in 1995, before expanding into further markets through acquisitions. A partnership with Microsoft continued throughout its history. Citrix acquired Sequoia Software Corp. in 2001. In 2003, Citrix acquired ExpertCity, a provider of remote desktop products. In 2021, Citrix generated $3.2 billion in revenue. The company had 9,700 employees in 2021.

title: Mei-Ann Chen — New England Conservatory interview
text:
Mei-Ann Chen — New England Conservatory interview
Mei-Ann Chen earned simultaneous master's degrees in violin and conducting at New England Conservatory before pursuing doctoral studies at the University of Michigan. Her first music director position was with the Portland Youth Philharmonic in Oregon. She recalled that Marylou Speaker Churchill taught her violin, English and aspects of American life while she lived with Churchill and her husband Mark. Her teachers also included Frank Battisti and Eric Rosenblith. Chen was born in Taiwan. She holds an undergraduate degree in violin performance from New England Conservatory. She holds a Doctor of Musical Arts degree in conducting from the University of Michigan. She served as music director of the Memphis Symphony from 2010 to 2016. She was artistic director of the National Taiwan Symphony Orchestra Summer Festival from 2016 to 2022. Since 2014, she has mentored young conductors through Chicago Sinfonietta’s Freeman Conducting Fellowship program. She has been a mentor for the Taki Alsop Fellowship since 2022.

title: Ketan Patel — early life and research career
text:
Ketan Patel — early life and research career
Ketan Jayakrishna Patel was born in Nairobi, Kenya, and left Kenya in 1976 to attend Marlborough College in Wiltshire. He qualified in medicine at the Royal Free Hospital and University of London in 1985, then trained as a gastroenterologist. His Cambridge PhD was supervised by Michael Neuberger. After his doctorate he worked with Ashok Venkitaraman from 1995 to 1998. He became a tenure-track group leader at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology in 1999 and a tenured principal investigator in 2007. In 2020 he became director of the MRC Weatherall Institute of Molecular Medicine and Molecular Haematology Unit at Oxford.

title: Sony — proposed home entertainment joint venture
text:
Sony — proposed home entertainment joint venture
In a January 20, 2026 announcement, Sony and TCL Electronics Holdings Limited outlined a proposed joint venture in which TCL would hold 51 percent of the shares. Sony would retain the remaining 49 percent. The new business would cover televisions and home audio equipment, including product development, manufacturing, sales and customer service. The partners aimed to sign binding agreements by the end of March, with operations expected to begin in April 2027 subject to approvals and other conditions. The parties planned to negotiate binding agreements by the end of March 2026 and anticipated a possible business launch in April 2027. Sony’s picture and audio technology would be combined with TCL’s display manufacturing and international supply-chain capacity.

title: Salesforce — Momentum acquisition agreement
text:
Salesforce — Momentum acquisition agreement
On February 18, 2026, Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Momentum, a conversational-insights and revenue-orchestration platform. Its technology was intended to help Agentforce 360 and Slackbot ingest unstructured conversations from third-party video applications such as Zoom and Google Meet. Salesforce said those conversations would provide context for automated workflows. An editor's update records that the acquisition closed on March 2, 2026. Santiago Suarez Ordoñez is Momentum's CEO and co-founder. Steve Fisher is Salesforce's President and Chief Product Officer. According to Suarez Ordoñez, joining Salesforce would help GTM teams transform static meeting audio into structured intelligence with immediate revenue impact.

title: HarperCollins
text:
HarperCollins
HarperCollins is a British-American publishing group owned by News Corp, with headquarters in London and New York City. It belongs to the group commonly called the Big Five English-language publishers. Its name joins two publishing traditions: Harper & Brothers, founded in New York in 1817, and William Collins, Sons, founded in Glasgow in 1819. Harper & Brothers later became Harper & Row through a merger with Row, Peterson & Company. The HarperCollins emblem combines the flame of the Harper torch with water from the Collins fountain. HarperCollins operates publishing groups in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, India, and China. Brian Murray has been the company's president and chief executive since 2008. In 2014, HarperCollins acquired Canadian romance publisher Harlequin Enterprises for C$455 million.

title: Steve Goldstein — UC Irvine appointment biography, 2018
text:
Steve Goldstein — UC Irvine appointment biography, 2018
Steve Goldstein earned an MD and immunology PhD at Harvard and became dean and chief diversity officer of Loyola Chicago’s Stritch School of Medicine. He had been provost and senior vice president for academic affairs at Brandeis. At Chicago he was chair of pediatrics and founding physician-in-chief of Comer Children’s Hospital. He was a Yale professor and founder of its Section of Developmental Biology and Biophysics. He received the E. Mead Johnson Award in 2001 from the Society for Pediatric Research. He advised NIH on nanomedicine and vice-chaired the NSF Biological Sciences Advisory Committee. In December 2018, UC Irvine announced his appointment as its next vice chancellor for health affairs. His research interests include ion channels and their function in disease and health. He is an alumnus of Brandeis University. He was also the founding director of two biomedical research institutes at the University of Chicago. He is a fellow of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

title: Building Europe's first space-based Quantum Key Distribution system -- The German Aerospace Center's role in the EAGLE-1 mission
text:
Building Europe's first space-based Quantum Key Distribution system -- The German Aerospace Center's role in the EAGLE-1 mission
EAGLE-1 is a European project to establish a sovereign satellite-based system for quantum key distribution. ESA and SES lead the mission with national space agencies and commercial partners. Its planned infrastructure combines a low-Earth-orbit satellite payload, optical receiving stations, operational networks and key management. The German Aerospace Center’s communications institute is developing the quantum transmitter and adapting its Oberpfaffenhofen ground station for in-orbit testing. That station will assess the payload and optical connection, using upgraded adaptive optics to reduce atmospheric distortion. DLR-IKN is also responsible for developing the transmitter’s software and firmware. The transmitter generates quantum states for a QKD protocol using an optical signal transmitted to the ground. The upgraded adaptive optics will also optimize coupling of incoming light into a single mode optical fiber.

title: ForgeRock
text:
ForgeRock
ForgeRock was an identity and access management software company headquartered in San Francisco. Former Sun Microsystems employees founded it in Norway in February 2010 after Oracle acquired Sun. They continued developing software that was otherwise due to be phased out in favor of Oracle products. The company went public in September 2021, trading on the New York Stock Exchange as FORG. Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition of ForgeRock for approximately $2.3 billion in August 2023, after which ForgeRock merged into Ping Identity. Its platform included access management, identity management, directory services, and a gateway for web traffic and APIs, with components based on open-source projects including OpenAM and OpenIDM.

title: Nutanix
text:
Nutanix
Nutanix is an American cloud computing company that develops software for data centers and hybrid multicloud systems. Its products cover virtualization, Kubernetes, database services, networking, security, and storage. Dheeraj Pandey, Mohit Aron, and Ajeet Singh founded the company on 23 September 2009. Aron left in early 2013 to establish the data-storage company Cohesity. Nutanix reached a valuation of $1 billion in 2013 and raised a further $140 million in a 2014 financing round that valued it at approximately $2 billion. It is based in San Jose, California. Venture capital firms invested $312.2 million in Nutanix over five rounds of funding. Nutanix's initial public offering on September 30, 2016, raised about $230 million through the sale of 14.87 million shares at $16 each. In 2021, the company transitioned from making hardware appliances to focusing on subscription software.

title: GPT-5.2
text:
GPT-5.2
GPT-5.2 is an OpenAI language-model family released on December 11, 2025, as the successor to GPT-5.1. It has three modes: Instant, Thinking and Pro, with the latter two designed for reasoning. Thinking offers standard and extended options, while Pro uses more reasoning time and computing resources than Thinking. OpenAI also released a version specialized for programming, GPT-5.2-Codex. The family forms part of the GPT series and provides different options for tasks that call for quick responses or more extensive reasoning. GPT-5.2 was released approximately three weeks after Google's Gemini 3 Pro. Aaron Levie, CEO of Box, reported that GPT-5.2 scored 7 points better than GPT-5.1 on the company's tests for real-world knowledge work.

title: Tuttle Publishing
text:
Tuttle Publishing
Tuttle Publishing was founded by Charles E. Tuttle in Tokyo in 1948. Originally called the Charles E. Tuttle Company, it publishes books about Asian languages, cooking, travel, martial arts, design, and culture. Its publishing businesses include Tuttle, Periplus Editions, and Journey Editions, with a strong focus on Asia. It was the 31st corporation approved by the occupying Allied administration. In its first year of operation, the company imported and distributed U.S. paperback publications to the occupying forces. In 1996, the company changed its name to Tuttle Publishing. Tuttle Publishing is part of Periplus Publishing Group and has around 60 staff members across offices in North Clarendon, Vermont, Singapore and Tokyo. It is the official publisher of the Bruce Lee Library, with permission from his estate.

title: Deborah Warner
text:
Deborah Warner
Deborah Warner is a British theatre and opera director whose work includes productions of classical drama, opera, poetry and oratorio. Her honours include an honorary doctorate from Bath Spa University and an honorary fellowship of the Central School of Speech and Drama. She became a CBE in 2006 and has also received the French distinction Commandeur de l’Ordre des Arts et des lettres. An Associate Artist at the Barbican Theatre, she held the Cameron Mackintosh Visiting Professorship of Contemporary Theatre at the University of Oxford in 2019. She also directed the Ustinov Studio in Bath, programming chamber music, dance and plays by Shakespeare and Pinter.

title: School of Film/Video
text:
School of Film/Video
The CalArts School of Film/Video offers undergraduate programs in character animation, experimental animation, and film and video. Its graduate programs cover experimental animation, film and video, and film directing. Students work in live action, animation, documentary, installation, and other moving-image forms. The school provides theaters, laboratories, studios, and production spaces for individual work and collaborative projects involving both conventional filmmaking and experimental approaches. All of the school's faculty are working artists, filmmakers, and technicians. The school has an 8:1 student-faculty ratio. Its BFA programs emphasize small class sizes, dedicated mentorship, and an open-ended, experience-based approach. Graduate programs emphasize rigorous critique, dynamic discourse, and cross-genre collaboration.

title: Seamfix
text:
Seamfix
Seamfix is a Nigerian technology company specializing in identity management, digital verification and software development. Chimezie Emewulu and Chibuzor Onwurah founded it in October 2007, initially building custom software for local businesses. The company later supplied SIM registration systems to telecommunications operators including Airtel, MTN Nigeria and Starcomms. It also developed mobile enrollment platforms for Nigeria’s National Identity Management Commission and the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System. Seamfix expanded into other African markets and established offices in the United Kingdom and United Arab Emirates. In 2024, it raised $4.5 million from Alitheia IDF to expand its infrastructure and digital identity services.

title: Asha Sharma — Carlson School alumni profile
text:
Asha Sharma — Carlson School alumni profile
Asha Sharma graduated from the Carlson School in 2011, having majored in marketing. During her studies she completed seven internships and worked on a Cargill project in Poland and Hungary. She began her career as an associate product manager at Microsoft. As a student at Carlson, Sharma completed seven internships and took part in its consulting enterprise programme. In her senior year she helped create the A-List, a Brooklyn Park centre supporting teenagers seeking employment and professional experience. Her marketing and advertising work at home-improvement startup Porch earned her a place on Forbes’s 2015 list of emerging leaders under thirty. The school described her work establishing a partnership between Porch and home-improvement retailer Lowe’s.

title: Esa-Pekka Salonen lands new Boston Symphony Orchestra role
text:
Esa-Pekka Salonen lands new Boston Symphony Orchestra role
On February 2, 2026, the Boston Symphony Orchestra named Esa-Pekka Salonen to direct that summer’s Tanglewood Festival of Contemporary Music. He was to curate five programs running from July 23 to 27, combining music by younger composers with memorial works for recently deceased figures. The closing concert was planned around Nordic music, including Salonen’s Cello Concerto and works by Hans Abrahamsen, Anders Hillborg and Magnus Lindberg. Salonen had left the San Francisco Symphony in 2025 after disagreements over finances and artistic policy. His subsequent appointments included creative director of the Los Angeles Philharmonic and principal conductor of the Orchestre de Paris.

title: Ben Affleck — feature directing career
text:
Ben Affleck — feature directing career
Ben Affleck made his feature film directing debut in 2007 with Gone Baby Gone. The thriller was adapted from a novel by Dennis Lehane. He subsequently directed and acted in The Town in 2010 and Argo in 2012, both made for Warner Bros. Argo, in which he played intelligence agent Tony Mendez during the Iran hostage crisis, won the Academy Award for Best Picture, while Affleck received the Golden Globe and BAFTA awards for directing. Affleck co-wrote and acted in Good Will Hunting, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay alongside Matt Damon. Argo received the Academy Award for Best Picture, while Affleck received director honours at the Golden Globes and BAFTAs.

title: List of football clubs in the Czech Republic
text:
List of football clubs in the Czech Republic
Czech football clubs compete in a league system headed by the Czech First League. Its 2026–27 membership includes Sparta Prague, Slavia Prague, Viktoria Plzeň, Baník Ostrava and Slovan Liberec. The Czech National Football League forms the second tier, with clubs including Karviná, Dukla Prague, Opava and Vysočina Jihlava. At the third level, teams compete in the Bohemian Football League or the Moravian-Silesian Football League. The Bohemian competition has two groups, and the fourth division is organized into groups as well. The list places SK Dynamo České Budějovice in Group A of the Bohemian Football League. It places MFK Chrudim in Group B of the same competition.

title: Seraphic Security secures $29 million Series A to transform any browser into a secure
text:
Seraphic Security secures $29 million Series A to transform any browser into a secure
Seraphic Security was founded in 2020 by chief executive Ilan Yeshua and chief technology officer Avihay Cohen. Yeshua had previously served for many years as chief executive of the news website Walla. The company’s browser-security platform protects access to SaaS and private web applications on both managed and personal devices. It works across browsers and also supports desktop applications such as Teams, Slack, Discord and WhatsApp. At the time of its Series A funding announcement, Seraphic employed more than fifty people. A January 2025 funding round provided $29 million in Series A investment led by GreatPoint Ventures, with participation from several existing backers. The browser-security company reported more than 50 employees and a threefold year-on-year increase in annual recurring revenue. Its software also covered SaaS applications and desktop services such as Teams and Slack without requiring a virtual desktop infrastructure.

title: Bruce Lee Rothschild
text:
Bruce Lee Rothschild
Bruce Lee Rothschild is an American mathematician whose work includes combinatorics, Ramsey theory and extremal set theory. Born in Los Angeles on August 26, 1941, he earned a mathematics degree at the California Institute of Technology in 1963 and a doctorate at Yale University in 1967, supervised by Øystein Ore. He taught at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1967 to 1969 and worked as a consultant for Bell Labs, collaborating with Ronald Graham. Rothschild joined the University of California, Los Angeles in 1971, became a full professor in 1977 and later held emeritus status there. Together with Ronald Graham, Rothschild formulated the Graham–Rothschild theorem. He was promoted to associate professor at UCLA in 1973. He received a Sloan Research Fellowship for 1973–1975.

title: Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics
text:
Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics
The Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics is a Chinese Academy of Sciences research center in Dalian, Liaoning. Its work spans physical and biophysical chemistry, chemical physics, chemical engineering and materials science. The institute developed from the research department of the South Manchuria Railway and received its present name in 1961. It moved to its current site in 1995. Its facilities include a national laboratory, two state key laboratories and five national engineering research centers. The Dalian National Laboratory for Clean Energy links research groups inside and outside the institute, studying fossil-fuel conversion, cleaner energy technologies and the use of solar energy and biomass.

title: William Procter Prize for Scientific Achievement
text:
William Procter Prize for Scientific Achievement
Sigma Xi awards the William Procter Prize for Scientific Achievement each year to a researcher who combines scientific accomplishment with communication across disciplines. Recipients receive a glass sculpture and $5,000, and nominate a younger scholar for a further $5,000 research grant. The winner traditionally gives an address at the society’s annual meeting. The award was endowed in 1950 by William Procter, an heir to a Procter and Gamble founder who was active in Sigma Xi and the Research Society of America. The prize's glass sculpture is a Steuben sculpture. The younger scholar designated by a recipient usually works in the same field. The Research Society of America was affiliated with Sigma Xi.

title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Seraphic, Turning Any Browser into a Secure Enterprise Browser
text:
CrowdStrike to Acquire Seraphic, Turning Any Browser into a Secure Enterprise Browser
CrowdStrike announced on 13 January 2026 that it had signed an agreement to acquire browser-security company Seraphic Security. The company planned to combine Seraphic’s browser protection with endpoint data and threat intelligence from its Falcon platform, alongside SGNL’s continuous authorization technology. The proposed combination was intended to provide a unified security system covering each stage of work, from the endpoint through browser sessions and into cloud services. Chief executive George Kurtz said the approach would allow employees to keep using their preferred browsers while applying enterprise security controls, without requiring a change of browser or slowing their work. Its security technology operates within Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox, including on unmanaged devices, without requiring a separate enterprise browser. The planned integration would combine active browser-session telemetry with Falcon endpoint intelligence.

title: Oswald Steward — UCI career profile, 2020
text:
Oswald Steward — UCI career profile, 2020
Oswald Steward earned a BA in psychology at the University of Colorado in 1970 and a PhD in psychobiology at UC Irvine in 1974. From 1974 to 1986, he held professorial positions in neurosurgery and physiology at the University of Virginia. He became founding chair of Virginia’s Department of Neuroscience, holding the Harrison Foundation professorship until 1999. In 1999 he returned to UC Irvine as founding director of the Reeve-Irvine Research Center. He served as senior associate dean for research in UCI’s School of Medicine from 2012 to 2017. His research focuses on cellular and molecular mechanisms of repair following central nervous system injury. His work has established fundamental principles regarding local protein synthesis at synaptic sites on dendrites. He received the NINDS Landis Award for Outstanding Mentorship in 2020. He was elected Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 2008.

title: Chennai Mathematical Institute
text:
Chennai Mathematical Institute
Chennai Mathematical Institute is a teaching and research institution in Chennai, India, founded by the SPIC Science Foundation in 1989. It offers degrees in mathematics, physics and computer science. The institute moved to Siruseri in 2005 and gained deemed-university status under the University Grants Commission Act in December 2006. The institute is noted for research in algebraic geometry, particularly moduli of bundles. Its first premises were in an office complex in T. Nagar, Chennai. In 1996, the School of Mathematics became an independent institution named SPIC Mathematical Institute. It was renamed Chennai Mathematical Institute in 1998. In 2010, the institute launched a summer fellowship programme inviting about 30 students from across India to work on research projects under its faculty.

title: Orchestra
text:
Orchestra
An orchestra brings together instrumentalists from several families, usually strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion. Modern orchestras may also include a harp or keyboard instruments, while some compositions call for guitars or electronic instruments. A symphony orchestra can have more than a hundred musicians; a chamber orchestra generally has no more than about fifty. Orchestras are usually led by a conductor who directs performances with movements of the hands and arms. The conductor sets the tempo and shapes the ensemble's sound. The conductor also leads rehearsals before public concerts. The principal player of the first violin section is commonly called the concertmaster. The term orchestra derives from the Greek name for the area in front of a stage reserved for the chorus in ancient Greek theatre.

title: ACM Turing Award — March 2026 announcement
text:
ACM Turing Award — March 2026 announcement
On March 18, 2026, ACM announced that Charles H. Bennett and Gilles Brassard would share the 2025 ACM AM Turing Award. Bennett was an American physicist at IBM Research, while Brassard was a Canadian computer scientist on the faculty of the Université de Montréal. The award recognized their foundational contributions to quantum information science and secure communication. It carried a $1 million prize supported by Google. Their 1984 BB84 protocol demonstrated how quantum-mechanical effects could be used to distribute cryptographic keys securely. The announcement described their work as helping establish quantum information science at the intersection of physics and computing.

title: ServiceNow to acquire Veza in major identity security play
text:
ServiceNow to acquire Veza in major identity security play
ServiceNow announced plans to buy identity security company Veza and incorporate its access-management technology into the AI Control Tower. Veza’s Access Graph maps permissions across people, machines and AI systems, allowing security teams to identify excessive access to company data and applications. The proposed integration would combine those relationships with ServiceNow’s workflow and knowledge-graph tools to manage what AI agents can reach inside an organization. Veza had about 230 employees and nearly 150 enterprise customers across industries including banking and hospitality. The companies did not disclose the price, and the transaction remained dependent on regulatory clearance and other customary closing requirements.

title: SGNL
text:
SGNL
SGNL was founded in 2021 by product and engineering specialists whose previous employers included Google, Okta and Microsoft. The company develops identity and access controls for enterprises, helping them manage access to sensitive information and reduce the proliferation of roles across human users and non-human identities. Founders Scott Kriz and Erik Gustavson previously built Bitium, which Google acquired in 2017. They subsequently shifted their focus from authentication to controlling access to customer data, software code and cloud infrastructure using business context. SGNL’s policies are designed to reduce the administrative burden of access management and address gaps in older privileged-access and identity-governance systems.

title: John Yates III — laboratory biography
text:
John Yates III — laboratory biography
John R. Yates III received a BA in zoology from the University of Maine in 1980, followed by an MS in chemistry there in 1983. He completed a chemistry PhD at the University of Virginia in 1987. His laboratory develops methods for proteomics, and he has held the Ernest W. Hahn professorship at Scripps Research. His honors include HUPO awards in proteomics in 2005 and discovery in 2017. He has been a professor of Chemistry and Molecular Medicine at Scripps Research Institute since 2007. His awards include the Michael Gross Lecture from the University of Nebraska in 2022. He has lectured for the California Institute of Technology.

title: Roman Bezrukavnikov - Curriculum Vitae
text:
Roman Bezrukavnikov - Curriculum Vitae
Roman Bezrukavnikov was born in Moscow in 1973 and became a mathematics professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in September 2005. Before joining MIT, he held a tenure-track assistant professorship at Northwestern University from September 2002 to August 2005, including a year on leave at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. He was a long-term prize fellow at the Clay Mathematical Institute in 2001–2002 and a Dickson Instructor at the University of Chicago from 1999 to 2001. His education included a master’s degree from Brandeis in 1994 and a doctorate at Tel Aviv University in 1998, supervised by Joseph Bernstein.

title: Steve Cooper (football manager)
text:
Steve Cooper (football manager)
Steve Cooper is a Welsh football manager and former defender who began coaching in Wrexham’s academy while still playing in the Welsh leagues. He moved to Liverpool in 2008 and became academy manager there in 2011. After joining England’s youth coaching staff in 2014, he led the under-17 team to the 2017 World Cup title. Cooper later managed Swansea City and Nottingham Forest. He was born in Pontypridd on December 10, 1979, grew up in nearby Hopkinstown and is the son of former referee Keith Cooper. At the age of 27, Cooper obtained his UEFA Pro Licence, becoming one of the youngest coaches to achieve the qualification. On 29 May 2022, Cooper led Nottingham Forest to promotion to the Premier League after a 1–0 win over Huddersfield Town in the Championship play-off final at Wembley Stadium.

title: Pep Guardiola
text:
Pep Guardiola
Pep Guardiola is a Spanish football manager and former midfielder from the Catalan region born on 18 January 1971. As a Barcelona player, he belonged to Johan Cruyff’s side that won the 1992 European Cup and four consecutive Spanish league titles. He later managed Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Manchester City. He captained Barcelona from 1997 until his departure in 2001. He was capped 47 times for Spain and appeared at the 1994 FIFA World Cup and UEFA Euro 2000. Guardiola managed Barcelona B and won the Tercera División title before taking charge of the first team in 2008. He was named the FIFA World Coach of the Year in 2011.

title: Japan Prize — 2026 laureate announcement
text:
Japan Prize — 2026 laureate announcement
The Japan Prize Foundation announced its 2026 laureates on January 21, 2026. Cynthia Dwork of the United States received the Electronics, Information, and Communication prize for research on differential privacy and fairness. The Life Sciences prize was shared by Japan's Shizuo Akira and the US-based Zhijian James Chen for discovering how the innate immune system senses nucleic acids. The foundation selected the laureates from 292 nominees across the two fields. The foundation considered 292 nominations across the two prize fields for the year, including 107 in electronics and communications. The life-sciences awards went to Shizuo Akira and Zhijian Chen for work on innate immune detection of nucleic acids. The information-science award highlighted differential privacy and fairness in digital society.

title: Nashville Symphony
text:
Nashville Symphony
The Nashville Symphony is an American orchestra based at the Schermerhorn Symphony Center in Nashville, Tennessee. It was founded in 1946 after Walter Sharp, a Nashville native returning from service in World War II, enlisted local support for a new symphony orchestra. Sharp appointed William Strickland as its first music director and conductor. The orchestra gave its first concert at Nashville’s War Memorial Auditorium in the autumn of 1946, and Strickland remained in charge for its first five seasons. During Michael Charry's tenure, the orchestra moved its subscription series from War Memorial Auditorium to Jackson Hall in the Tennessee Performing Arts Center. In September 2006, the symphony opened Schermerhorn Symphony Center, a $123.5 million project that includes Laura Turner Concert Hall. In 2008, its recording of Joan Tower's Made in America won three Grammy Awards, including Best Orchestral Performance and Best Classical Album.

title: Dutch National Opera
text:
Dutch National Opera
Dutch National Opera is based in Amsterdam and shares the Stopera building with Dutch National Ballet. The building was designed by Cees Dam and Wilhelm Holzbauer and opened in 1986. The company began after the Second World War as a repertory ensemble and toured from Amsterdam’s Stadsschouwburg. In 1964, it became De Nederlandse Operastichting and began engaging different singers and creative teams for individual productions. It moved to the Stopera in 1986, later adopting the Dutch name De Nationale Opera in 2014. The company won the International Opera Awards’ Opera Company of the Year award in 2016. The company has its own choir of sixty singers. It has a technical staff of 260. The company produces an average of eleven productions per year. It has also performed at the Carré Theatre and on the Westergasfabriek industrial site in Amsterdam.

title: John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science
text:
John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science
Harvard University’s Joseph Henrich received the 2026 John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science. His research examines how cultural evolution shapes human behaviour and psychology, combining ethnographic evidence with experiments drawn from anthropology, economics and psychology. His work includes studies of prestige, religion, kinship and the influence of social norms on cooperation. He accepted the award at the National Academy of Sciences’ 163rd annual meeting on 26 April; the honour carries a medal and a $25,000 prize. The award was established in 1932 through a gift from the American Telephone and Telegraph Company. It is named for John J. Carty, an American electrical engineer known for his contributions to the development of telephone communication.

title: About Cerebras
text:
About Cerebras
Andrew Feldman, Gary Lauterbach, Michael James, Sean Lie and Jean-Philippe Fricker founded Cerebras in 2015 to develop wafer-scale computing. The company introduced its first Wafer-Scale Engine and CS-1 system in 2019, making the technology available to data centers. Its systems are used for on-site supercomputers in fields including medical research, cryptography and energy. Developers can also access its computing services through a pay-as-you-go cloud offering. In 2023, it introduced the Condor Galaxy supercomputer network in partnership with G42. The WSE-3 processor and CS-3 system followed in 2024 for AI inference and training. Cerebras introduced the WSE-2 and CS-2 in 2021. The Condor Galaxy 1 supercomputer features 4 exaFLOPs of FP16 performance and 54 million cores. In 2022, researchers at Argonne National Laboratory received the Gordon Bell Special Prize for research into COVID-19 variants powered by a Cerebras CS-2 cluster.

title: Kenneth Appel
text:
Kenneth Appel
Kenneth Appel was an American mathematician who proved the four-color theorem with Wolfgang Haken at the University of Illinois in 1976. The theorem states that a map can be colored with four colors without adjoining regions sharing a color, subject to certain conditions. Their proof was controversial because it relied on thousands of computer calculations that could not be checked manually. Appel was born in Brooklyn in 1932 and earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1959. After researching cryptography at the Institute for Defense Analyses, he joined Illinois in 1961 and later chaired the mathematics department at the University of New Hampshire.

title: Scott Moncrieff Prize
text:
Scott Moncrieff Prize
The Scott Moncrieff Prize is an annual award for the translation of full-length literary works from French into English. Established in 1965, it takes its name from the translator C. K. Scott Moncrieff and is awarded to one or more translators for work judged to have literary merit by the Translators Association. The winner receives £3,000 and the runner-up £1,000; eligibility is restricted to translations first published in the United Kingdom. The Institut Français du Royaume Uni sponsors the prize, whose past sponsors have included the French Ministry of Culture, the French Embassy and the Arts Council of England. In 2023, Frank Wynne won the prize for his translation of Standing Heavy by GauZ'. In 2022, Sarah Ardizzone won for her translation of Men Don’t Cry by Faïza Guène. In 2021, Sam Taylor won for his translation of The Invisible Land by Hubert Mingarelli.

title: Charles Bennett — IBM Research biography
text:
Charles Bennett — IBM Research biography
Charles H. Bennett completed a doctorate in chemical physics at Harvard, supervised by David Turnbull and Berni Alder. He continued the research at Argonne Laboratory under Aneesur Rahman before joining IBM's research staff. His work has examined the physics of information processing, reversible computation and quantum information theory. He lists photography and music as his principal hobbies. Bennett joined IBM Research in 1973, where his projects included reversible computing and the thermodynamics of information processing. He is an IBM Fellow and belongs to both the United States National Academy of Sciences and the Royal Society in London. IBM’s biography also mentions continuing interests in photography and music.

title: The most daring space missions coming in 2025 - from China's asteroid retrieval to first private 'luxury' space station
text:
The most daring space missions coming in 2025 - from China's asteroid retrieval to first private 'luxury' space station
Plans for China’s Tianwen-2 mission called for a 2025 launch to collect material from the near-Earth asteroid Kamoʻoalewa. Scientists suspect the asteroid may be a fragment of the Moon. The mission plan called for anchoring to its surface, gathering samples and returning them to Earth. The spacecraft would then use Earth’s gravity to redirect itself toward comet 311P/PANSTARRS. Sampling was expected to take about two and a half years, followed by arrival at the comet in the mid-2030s. Kamoʻoalewa is a quasi-satellite of Earth, orbiting the Sun while remaining near our planet. It was discovered in 2016 by the Pan-STARRS survey at Haleakalā Observatory in Hawaii.

title: Josh D'Amaro — career before the Disneyland presidency
text:
Josh D'Amaro — career before the Disneyland presidency
Before joining Disney in 1998, Josh D'Amaro worked in financial planning for The Gillette Company in Boston. His first Disney job was as a senior business planner at Disneyland Resort. From 2008 to 2010, he was vice president of finance for Global Licensing in Disney's Consumer Products Division. He later oversaw Walt Disney World's resort hotels and transport services from 2014 to 2017. These positions preceded his appointment as Disneyland Resort president in 2018. The 2018 announcement also moved Michael Colglazier from leading Disneyland Resort to responsibility for the company’s Asia-Pacific parks. Colglazier had overseen a workforce of about 30,000 people and the resort’s sixtieth-anniversary Diamond Celebration. In the wider management reorganisation, the Asia-Pacific role included operations connected to Hong Kong Disneyland, Tokyo Disneyland and Shanghai Disney Resort.

title: Lewis Kay — SickKids education and experience
text:
Lewis Kay — SickKids education and experience
Lewis Kay earned a first-class honours BSc in biochemistry from the University of Alberta in Edmonton in 1983. He received his PhD in molecular biophysics at Yale in 1988, supervised by J. H. Prestegard. From 1988 to 1991 he was a postdoctoral fellow in Adrian Bax’s laboratory at the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda, Maryland. He became an assistant professor at the University of Toronto in 1992 and a professor in 1995. Kay holds the title of Senior Scientist in Molecular Medicine. His research focuses on transforming nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy techniques for studying large proteins and their complexes, particularly those involved in health and disease.

title: Opera Bohemia
text:
Opera Bohemia
Opera Bohemia is a Scottish company that began staging operas in 2010 and tours throughout the country, including remote communities. Conductor Alistair Digges and baritone Douglas Nairne founded it to widen opera audiences and provide work for young performers. Its productions use small casts without a chorus and are adapted to fit modest stages. A piano and another solo instrument often take the place of a full orchestra. For larger performances, the company uses its chamber orchestra, the Bohemia Ensemble. A 10th anniversary tour of The Merry Widow visited 18 venues and reached an audience of four thousand people across Scotland. The company has toured twice to England including a performance of Madama Butterfly in London's Middle Temple. Opera Bohemia has received Creative Scotland Lottery Funding and funding from trusts, companies and individuals.

title: ESAIL
text:
ESAIL
ESAIL was a small maritime-tracking satellite developed by the European Space Agency with LuxSpace and exactEarth. It was launched from the Guiana Space Centre in September 2020 aboard Vega flight VV16. The satellite received signals from ships’ automatic identification systems to support fisheries monitoring, fleet management, environmental protection and security. During a technology demonstration, it processed more than two million messages from 70,000 ships in one day, an improvement of 15 to 20 percent over earlier satellites. It occupied a sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 515 kilometres above the Earth and re-entered on March 3, 2025. ESAIL was developed within ESA’s Advanced Research in Telecommunications Systems programme.

title: Arianespace
text:
Arianespace
Arianespace is a French launch services company established in March 1980 and based in Évry-Courcouronnes near Paris. It operates the Ariane 6 rocket and is owned by ArianeGroup, the joint venture between Airbus and Safran. Arianespace markets launches, prepares missions and handles customer relations, while ArianeGroup designs and manufactures the rocket. At the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, Arianespace supervises teams that integrate and prepare the launch vehicles. The European Space Agency owns the launch infrastructure, and France’s CNES manages the site. The company’s first commercial launch carried Spacenet 1 into space on May 23, 1984. Arianespace was the world's first commercial launch service provider. As of October 2025, it had conducted 355 missions. By that date, it had launched over 1,100 satellites.

title: Matei Zaharia — education and early faculty positions
text:
Matei Zaharia — education and early faculty positions
Matei Zaharia studied at the University of Waterloo from 2003 to 2007, earning a Bachelor of Mathematics in honours computer science with a minor in combinatorics and optimization. He completed his computer science PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2013, advised by Scott Shenker and Ion Stoica. He was an assistant professor of computer science at MIT from 2015 to 2016 before moving to Stanford in 2016. His CV lists him as a cofounder and chief technologist of Databricks from 2013. Zaharia created Apache Spark, an open-source engine for large-scale data processing. His research spans distributed systems, cloud computing, and systems for machine learning. He received the Association for Computing Machinery's doctoral dissertation award for his work on large-scale computing systems.

title: Bonnie Bassler — Princeton biography
text:
Bonnie Bassler — Princeton biography
Bonnie Bassler earned a BS in biochemistry at the University of California, Davis, and a PhD in biochemistry at Johns Hopkins University. She undertook postdoctoral work in genetics at the Agouron Institute and joined Princeton’s faculty in 1994. She directed Princeton’s Molecular Biology Graduate Program from 2002 to 2008. Her awards include a MacArthur Fellowship in 2002 and the Wiley Prize in Biomedical Science in 2009. She was president of the American Society for Microbiology in 2010–2011. President Barack Obama nominated her to the National Science Board, on which she served for six years. Her research focuses on quorum sensing, the chemical communication process through which bacteria coordinate collective behavior in response to population density.

title: AI Killed My Job: Translators - by Brian Merchant
text:
AI Killed My Job: Translators - by Brian Merchant
Brian Merchant reported in August 2025 that translators and game localizers were experiencing sharp falls in earnings as clients adopted automated translation. Some respondents described lower rates, fewer assignments, and cuts to in-house localization teams, with some contemplating a change of career. Others emphasized that machine-translation editing had existed well before the generative AI boom. Merchant argued that the publicity surrounding newer systems helped employers justify labor cuts, even when the technology still required substantial human correction. Merchant heard from many game localizers working with Chinese mobile games. Interviewees described AI translations as homogeneous, blind to local details, or incorrect. The Translators Against the Machine initiative was gathering workers' stories and data to build solidarity and defend the profession.

title: LARES succesfully launched in orbit: satellite and mission description
text:
LARES succesfully launched in orbit: satellite and mission description
LARES, the Italian Space Agency’s Laser Relativity Satellite, entered orbit on February 13, 2012, during the first qualification launch of Europe’s Vega rocket. The mission tests general relativity by measuring frame dragging, also called the Lense-Thirring effect. Rather than carrying an active transmitter, the satellite uses optical retroreflectors to return laser pulses sent from ground stations. Those measurements establish its position accurately enough to detect small departures from Newtonian motion. The International Laser Ranging Service provides tracking, and Italian universities participated in the satellite’s design, construction, testing and subsequent data analysis under contracts with the Italian Space Agency. In 2008, the Italian Space Agency selected the prime industrial contractor for the LARES system. The payload was released very accurately into its nominal orbit.

title: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex
text:
Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex on 5 February 2026 as a model for coding and other computer-based work. It combined capabilities from GPT-5.2-Codex and GPT-5.2, with a reported increase in speed of 25%. The model was designed for extended tasks involving research, tools and complex execution, while allowing users to redirect work in progress. OpenAI said its team had used early versions to debug the model’s training, manage its deployment and interpret test and evaluation results, contributing to the development of the released model. The Codex name was previously used for an OpenAI model introduced in 2021 that translated natural-language instructions into code. That earlier model powered the initial version of GitHub Copilot.

title: Arne Slot
text:
Arne Slot
Arne Slot is a Dutch football manager and former midfielder who played for Zwolle, NAC Breda and Sparta Rotterdam. He won the Eerste Divisie with Zwolle in 2002 and again in 2012 before retiring as a player. After coaching in Zwolle’s academy and at Cambuur, he joined AZ as an assistant in 2017 and became head coach in 2019. Slot moved to Feyenoord in 2021, taking the club to the 2022 Europa Conference League final and later winning the Eredivisie and the Dutch cup. Slot was born on 17 September 1978 in Bergentheim, Overijssel, where he was raised. He started his football career at amateur side VV Bergentheim. He entered FC Zwolle's first team in 1995 at the age of 17.

title: Macmillan Publishers
text:
Macmillan Publishers
Macmillan Publishers was founded in London in 1843 by Scottish brothers Daniel and Alexander Macmillan. Its early publications included Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland in 1865 and The Jungle Book in 1894. Former British prime minister Harold Macmillan, Daniel’s grandson, chaired the company from 1964 until his death in 1986. The British and American publishing businesses have been wholly owned by Holtzbrinck Publishing Group since 1999, operating as Pan Macmillan in Britain and Macmillan Publishers in the United States. The company created Nature in 1869. George Edward Brett opened the first Macmillan office in the United States in 1869. Macmillan became the sole owner of Pan Books in 1986.

title: Boston Lyric Opera
text:
Boston Lyric Opera
Boston Lyric Opera is an opera company founded in Boston, Massachusetts, in 1976. It employs nearly 350 artists and production professionals each year, including singers, stagehands, costume makers and scenic designers.
