Its season consists of four mainstage productions in Greater Boston, including a new work. The company receives support from the Massachusetts Cultural Council and has shared productions with companies including New York City Opera, Houston Grand Opera and Glimmerglass Opera. Boston Lyric Opera is the largest and longest-lived opera company in New England. Its community work included participation in the 1999–2000 "Egypt in Boston" thematic season. In summer 2002, the company produced "Carmen on the Common", an education and community-outreach initiative culminating in two free, fully staged outdoor performances of Bizet's Carmen on Boston Common. Similar plans for Verdi's Aida in the 2005–2006 season were cancelled because of insufficient financial support.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
text:
LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
LLaMA is a family of language models with sizes from 7 billion to 65 billion parameters. The models were trained on trillions of tokens drawn entirely from publicly accessible datasets. The researchers reported that the 13-billion-parameter model surpassed GPT-3, with 175 billion parameters, on most of their benchmarks. The 65-billion-parameter version performed competitively with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B. The team made the models available to the research community. The paper was submitted to arXiv on 27 February 2023. The paper was written by Hugo Touvron and thirteen other authors. It is classified under Computation and Language in the Computer Science subject area.

title: Momentum — South Park Commons company profile
text:
Momentum — South Park Commons company profile
Momentum's founders include chief executive Santiago Suarez Ordoñez, Ashley Wilson and chief technology officer Moiz Virani. Santiago previously cofounded Blameless as its CTO and also worked as CTO of Whyline, director of engineering at Sauce Labs and a staff engineer at MuleSoft. Moiz was a founding engineer at Blameless and led backend infrastructure work at Sauce Labs and AWS. His background also includes academic research at the University of Kansas. Momentum is a portfolio company of South Park Commons. It uses AI and automation to turn customer interactions into sales insights. Its tools aim to save sales representatives time and give leaders a clear view without disrupting existing tools. Its other investors include Basis Set Ventures and FirstMark.

title: Frank Merle — academic curriculum vitae
text:
Frank Merle — academic curriculum vitae
Frank Merle was born in Marseille on November 22, 1962, and entered the École Normale Supérieure in 1982. He defended his doctorate at Université Pierre et Marie Curie on November 18, 1987, with Henri Berestycki as supervisor. He completed his habilitation there on January 9, 1991. He was an assistant professor at New York University’s Courant Institute in 1989–1990. His distinctions include the CNRS silver medal in 2005 and a Clay Research Award in 2023. Merle is a French mathematician specializing in nonlinear partial differential equations. His research examines singularity formation and finite-time blow-up in nonlinear evolution equations. He has studied nonlinear Schrödinger equations and generalized Korteweg–de Vries equations.

title: Eva Andrei — Rutgers research biography
text:
Eva Andrei — Rutgers research biography
Eva Andrei received an undergraduate degree from Tel Aviv University and a physics PhD from Rutgers University. After postdoctoral research at Bell Laboratories and Saclay, France, she joined Rutgers as an assistant professor in 1987. Her honours include the CEA Medal of Physics and the Rutgers Board of Trustees Award for Excellence in Research, received in 2010. She edited Two Dimensional Electrons on Helium and Other Cryogenic Substrates, published by Kluwer Academic Press. Her editorial roles included Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences and Solid State Communications. She held fellowships in the American Physical Society and the American Association for the Advancement of Science.

title: BLOOM (language model)
text:
BLOOM (language model)
BLOOM is a multilingual language model released in 2022 through BigScience, a year-long research initiative coordinated by Hugging Face. Its development involved hundreds of volunteer researchers and engineers from universities and industry, with funding from the French government. The autoregressive transformer model has 176 billion parameters and generates text in 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. It was trained between March and July 2022 on France’s Jean Zay public supercomputer. The source code is available under Apache 2.0, while the model parameters use BigScience’s Responsible AI License, which permits access and reuse subject to restrictions on use. BLOOM's training corpus is named ROOTS. Data extracted from the web-based OSCAR corpus accounts for 38% of ROOTS. The model was trained on approximately 366 billion tokens. It was developed using the open-source libraries DeepSpeed Megatron. BLOOM was used in the chatbots BLOOMChat and HuggingChat due to its multilingual abilities. BigScience also released BLOOMZ, a variant of BLOOM fine-tuned on the multilingual xP3 dataset to follow instructions.

title: Monika Henzinger — university and industry career
text:
Monika Henzinger — university and industry career
Monika Henzinger received her PhD from Princeton University in 1993 and was an assistant professor at Cornell from 1993 to 1996. She worked at Digital Equipment Corporation from 1996 to 1999 and at Google from 1999 to 2005. She held professorships at EPFL in Switzerland from 2005 to 2009 and the University of Vienna from 2009 to 2023. She became a professor at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria in 2023 and vice president for technology transfer in 2024. Her research group develops efficient algorithms, especially for settings in which inputs change incrementally. The group also studies differential privacy for dynamically changing inputs and for data distributed over many users or databases.

title: Tito Muñoz — artist biography
text:
Tito Muñoz — artist biography
Tito Muñoz grew up in Queens, New York, training as a violinist in the city's public schools. He continued violin studies with Daniel Phillips at Queens College before studying conducting with David Zinman and Murry Sidlin at Aspen. He won the Robert J. Harth Conductor Prize in 2005 and the Aspen Conducting Prize in 2006. His professional conducting debut came in 2006 with the National Symphony Orchestra at the Kennedy Center, at Leonard Slatkin's invitation. He later studied at the LaGuardia High School of the Performing Arts, Juilliard School’s Music Advancement Program, and the Manhattan School of Music Pre-College Division. In 2006, he made his Cleveland Orchestra debut at the Blossom Music Festival. He was awarded the 2009 Mendelssohn Scholarship sponsored by Kurt Masur and the Felix Mendelssohn-Bartholdy Foundation in Leipzig.

title: Sarajevo Film Festival
text:
Sarajevo Film Festival
The Sarajevo Film Festival began in 1995 while the Bosnian capital was under siege. Its first edition ran from 25 October to 5 November, screening thirty-seven films from fifteen countries and drawing about 15,000 spectators. The annual festival is now held in August and presents feature films and shorts from around the world. Its venues include the National Theatre, the open-air Metalac cinema and the Bosnian Cultural Center. In 2004, its best-film prize became the Heart of Sarajevo award. The festival introduced the Sarajevo Talent Campus in 2007 with the Berlinale, later renaming this educational program Talents Sarajevo in 2014.

title: List of football clubs in the United Arab Emirates
text:
List of football clubs in the United Arab Emirates
Football clubs in the United Arab Emirates are distributed across the country’s seven emirates and several league divisions. Dubai clubs include Al Nasr in the Al Nasr district, Al Wasl in Zabeel and Shabab Al Ahli in Deira. Al Ain is based in the city of the same name, while Al Jazira plays in Abu Dhabi’s Al Nahyan district. Other clubs include Sharjah, Khor Fakkan and Kalba in Sharjah emirate, Ajman in Al Rashidiyah, and Al Arabi in Umm Al Quwain. Emirates is based in Al Dhait, Ras Al Khaimah. As of February 2026, there were officially 49 football clubs in the United Arab Emirates. Fourteen clubs competed in the top division. Fifteen clubs competed in the second division. Twelve clubs competed in the third division. Eight clubs were on hiatus. Four clubs were defunct, bringing the historical total to 53 clubs.

title: St. Martin's Press
text:
St. Martin's Press
St. Martin's Press is a book publisher based in the Equitable Building in Manhattan, New York City, issuing about 700 titles annually through six imprints. Britain's Macmillan Publishers founded the company in 1952 and named it after St Martin's Lane, the London street where Macmillan had its headquarters. Its publishing lines include mainstream books under St. Martin's Press, paperbacks under St. Martin's Griffin, and mysteries and thrillers under Minotaur. Castle Point Books handles specialty nonfiction, St. Martin's Essentials publishes lifestyle titles, and Wednesday Books specializes in young adult fiction. St. Martin's acquired the science fiction, fantasy and thriller publisher Tor-Forge Books in 1987.

title: FIAPF
text:
FIAPF
The International Federation of Film Producers Associations, known by its French initials FIAPF, was established in 1933. Its secretariat is in Brussels, Belgium, and it brings together film producers’ associations from multiple countries. FIAPF accredits international film festivals and helps producers coordinate policies on copyright, intellectual property enforcement, and piracy. Its other areas of work include digital technology, technical standards, media regulation, film financing, and trade. In 2026, its accreditation covered 49 festivals in 29 countries, with festivals of the highest international impact recognized as A-Festivals. Its accredited festivals span five continents. FIAPF uses a unified accreditation list that replaced its former four-category system.

title: Stratingh Institute for Chemistry
text:
Stratingh Institute for Chemistry
The Stratingh Institute for Chemistry belongs to the University of Groningen’s Faculty of Science and Engineering in the Netherlands. It is named after Sibrandus Stratingh, known for building an early battery-powered electric car. In 2020, the institute employed about 150 people from more than 30 countries. Its researchers include Ben Feringa, a recipient of the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on molecular machines. Research areas encompass the chemistry of life, chemical conversion, and materials chemistry. The institute is located on the Zernike Campus in Groningen, in the Feringa Building and Linnaeusborg. Its staff members also include Nathalie Katsonis and Sijbren Otto.

title: Microsoft Gaming — leadership announcement of February 2026
text:
Microsoft Gaming — leadership announcement of February 2026
On 20 February 2026, Microsoft announced Asha Sharma as Executive Vice President and CEO of Microsoft Gaming, reporting to Satya Nadella. Matt Booty was appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Content Officer, reporting to Sharma. The leadership announcement described Microsoft Gaming as serving more than 500 million monthly active users across its platforms. Before taking this role, Sharma had been Chief Operating Officer at Instacart and had held a vice-presidential position at Meta. Microsoft said its games organization encompassed nearly 40 studios across Xbox, Bethesda, Activision Blizzard and King. The succession followed Phil Spencer’s decision to retire after 38 years at Microsoft, including 12 years leading its gaming business.

title: Neil Critchley
text:
Neil Critchley
Neil Critchley is an English football manager and former player who made one Football League appearance for Crewe Alexandra. After retiring as a player at 24, he coached at Crewe and became joint academy director in 2007 before joining Liverpool’s under-18 setup in 2013. He stood in for Jürgen Klopp for two first-team cup matches during the 2019–20 season. Critchley took charge of Blackpool in March 2020 and led the club to promotion from League One through the playoffs in his first full season. He later worked as Steven Gerrard’s assistant at Aston Villa and briefly managed Queens Park Rangers.

title: David Fincher
text:
David Fincher
David Fincher is an American filmmaker born on August 28, 1962. He co-founded Propaganda Films in 1986 and directed music videos for Madonna, the Rolling Stones and other recording artists before establishing his feature-film career. His first feature was Alien 3 in 1992, followed by the thriller Seven in 1995. He later directed Fight Club, Zodiac and Gone Girl. The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, The Social Network and Mank each earned him an Academy Award nomination for directing. He became fascinated with filmmaking at the age of eight and began making films on an 8mm camera. Industrial Light & Magic hired him in 1983 as an assistant cameraman and matte photographer.

title: Boston Symphony Orchestra
text:
Boston Symphony Orchestra
The Boston Symphony Orchestra was founded in 1881 by Henry Lee Higginson. It performs primarily at Boston’s Symphony Hall and spends its summer season at Tanglewood. The Boston Pops, established by Higginson in 1885 for lighter music, shares many of the orchestra’s players but has its own conductor and schedule. It is the second-oldest orchestra in the United States. It is one of the five major American symphony orchestras commonly called the "Big Five". Its first conductor was George Henschel. The orchestra's first concert took place on October 22, 1881. The orchestra has made gramophone recordings since 1917. It has also played on film soundtrack recordings, including Schindler's List.

title: Eoghan McCabe — autobiographical profile
text:
Eoghan McCabe — autobiographical profile
Eoghan McCabe was born in Dublin, Ireland in 1984. He studied computer science at Trinity College Dublin. His early company, Eoghan McCabe Limited, became Contrast, an agency designing and developing web applications. The team also created the crash-monitoring service Exceptional, which it sold to Jonathan Siegel in 2011. He made his first website on Geocities in 1996. At age 16, he worked in a local hotel bar clearing tables. He subsequently learned to program at a local software company. He built websites for small Irish businesses throughout college. He began his computer science course in 2002. He won the Ludgate Award for a final-year webcam face-tracking project.

title: Park Avenue Armory Appoints Deborah Warner as New Artistic Director
text:
Park Avenue Armory Appoints Deborah Warner as New Artistic Director
Park Avenue Armory announced Deborah Warner as its next Anita K. Hersh Artistic Director on 13 January 2026. She would begin that month, complete planning for the 2027 season and take full responsibility for the 2028 season onward. The British director’s career spanned more than four decades of theatre, opera and productions in unconventional spaces. She had served as Resident Director of the Royal Shakespeare Company and Associate Director of the National Theatre, and was the first woman to win the Olivier Award for Best Director. Her work would follow that of Pierre Audi, Alex Poots and Kristy Edmunds. The theatre and opera director was scheduled to start work in January 2026, with responsibilities for the 2027 season and planning beyond it. Her career included directing Shakespeare for the Royal Shakespeare Company and serving as an associate director of the National Theatre. The Armory hosts performances in a flexible 55,000-square-foot Drill Hall as well as more intimate historic rooms.

title: Benjamin Ayers — Georgia career profile, 2014
text:
Benjamin Ayers — Georgia career profile, 2014
Benjamin C. Ayers earned his PhD at Texas at Austin and his accounting bachelor’s and taxation master’s at Alabama. He was a certified public accountant in Alabama and, before his PhD, worked at KPMG in Atlanta and Tampa and Complete Health in Birmingham. He joined Georgia’s faculty in 1996, became Tull School of Accounting director in 2005, and held the Earl Davis Chair in Taxation. In April 2014 he was named dean of the Terry College, effective July 1. His teaching honours included the Richard B. Russell Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching. He taught introductory tax classes to undergraduates and a tax research class for master's-level students. He received 11 teaching awards at the school, college and university levels. He received the American Taxation Association's Outstanding Manuscript Award twice.

title: Trellix
text:
Trellix
Trellix is a privately held cybersecurity company formed in 2022 from FireEye’s products business and McAfee Enterprise. Its hardware, software and services support attack investigations, malware protection and assessments of IT security risks. Symphony Technology Group bought FireEye’s name and products business for $1.2 billion in June 2021, then acquired McAfee Enterprise for $4 billion the following month. The group combined the businesses under the Trellix name to provide extended detection and response services. McAfee Enterprise’s security service edge operation remained separate, becoming Skyhigh Security. In January 2025, Symphony Technology Group hired Vishal Rao to take over as CEO of Trellix. At its inception in January 2022, Trellix had more than 40,000 customers. The business focuses on threat detection and response using machine learning and automation.

title: Aviad Maizels — education and earlier ventures
text:
Aviad Maizels — education and earlier ventures
Aviad Maizels holds a B.S. from the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology and an M.S. from the Weizmann Institute of Science. He founded PrimeSense and later became a founder of Bionaut Labs. Maizels also completed a master’s degree at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he later served on the international board. He helped establish medical-technology company Bionaut Labs and later held the role of executive chairman. Before that he was chief executive and founder of the three-dimensional sensing company PrimeSense, which Apple acquired in 2013. His professional profile also identifies him as a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer.

title: Rigmor and Carl Holst-Knudsen Award for Scientific Research
text:
Rigmor and Carl Holst-Knudsen Award for Scientific Research
The Rigmor and Carl Holst-Knudsen Award for Scientific Research was established in Denmark in 1956 on the birthday of Carl Holst-Knudsen, then chairman of Aarhus University’s board. Presented annually on May 28, the award grew in value from 10,000 to 100,000 Danish kroner. Researchers do not apply for it; recipients are recognized for significant results that indicate promise for future work. Past recipients include physicist Lene Hau and economist Tim Bollerslev, both honored in 2008, and computer scientist Bjarne Stroustrup, who received the award in 2010. Dorthe Berntsen of the Department of Psychology received the award in 2007. Maria Fabricius Hansen of the Department of Art History received the award in 2006.

title: Anne Dejean — scientific curriculum vitae
text:
Anne Dejean — scientific curriculum vitae
Anne Dejean earned an MA in genetics at the University of Paris VI in 1980, a PhD in molecular biology there in 1983 and a doctorate in biochemistry in 1988. Her doctoral and postdoctoral work at Institut Pasteur was supervised by Pierre Tiollais. She became director of the Nuclear Organization and Oncogenesis laboratory at Institut Pasteur in 2003. She also headed INSERM Unit 993, Molecular and Cellular Biology of Tumors. Her research investigates how alterations in nuclear proteins contribute to cancer. She helped establish the role of the PML–RARα fusion protein in acute promyelocytic leukemia. Her work also examines SUMOylation, a reversible protein modification that regulates nuclear organization and gene expression.

title: Terns Pharmaceuticals — founder interview in 2019
text:
Terns Pharmaceuticals — founder interview in 2019
In a February 2019 interview, Terns Pharmaceuticals founder and then-CEO Weidong Zhong described the company's early development. He said he and his cofounders started the company in early 2017, with operations first in the San Francisco Bay Area and shortly afterwards in Shanghai. Terns was developing drugs for NASH and liver disease, using partnerships with pharmaceutical companies as well as its own discovery work. Zhong had previously worked at Novartis, Gilead and Schering-Plough. Its pipeline included drug candidates targeting different stages of disease with complementary mechanisms of action. Zhong said the company's goal was to bridge global drug discovery innovation with accelerated clinical development in China.

title: Karl Münchinger
text:
Karl Münchinger
Karl Münchinger was a German conductor born in Stuttgart in 1915. He studied at the city’s Hochschule für Musik and worked as an organist and church choir director before establishing his conducting career. In 1941 he became principal conductor of the Hanover Symphony, remaining for two years. After the Second World War, he founded the Stuttgart Chamber Orchestra. The ensemble made its Paris debut in 1949 and its American debut in San Francisco in 1953, and recorded extensively for Decca under his direction. He helped revive Johann Pachelbel's Canon in D with a 1960 recording made with the Stuttgart Chamber Orchestra. In 1977, the Stuttgart Chamber Orchestra became the first German ensemble to visit the People's Republic of China. Münchinger retired in 1988.

title: JoeySat
text:
JoeySat
JoeySat is a communications technology demonstrator developed by the European Space Agency, the UK Space Agency and Eutelsat OneWeb. Launched on a Falcon 9 in May 2023, it tested beam hopping during a two-year primary mission, switching coverage rapidly between locations as demand changed. The satellite was built by Airbus OneWeb Satellites, a joint venture between Airbus and OneWeb. Its digitally processed communications payload was developed by SatixFy. JoeySat was supported through ESA's Sunrise partnership project, part of its Advanced Research in Telecommunications Systems programme. It operated in low Earth orbit rather than geostationary orbit. The launch took place from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

title: Syracuse — chancellor appointment announced in March 2026
text:
Syracuse — chancellor appointment announced in March 2026
On March 3, 2026, Syracuse University announced J. Michael Haynie as its 13th chancellor and president, with a planned start on July 1. The appointment followed a recommendation by the search committee and a unanimous vote of the Board of Trustees. Haynie was already the university’s vice chancellor for strategic initiatives and innovation and executive dean of the Whitman School of Management. He founded the D’Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, which addresses policy, economic and wellness issues affecting military-connected people. Syracuse named him University Professor in 2018 and awarded him its Chancellor’s Medal in 2021. The university noted his more than two decades of service within the Syracuse community.

title: Seven missions launched to test optimised data transfer from space
text:
Seven missions launched to test optimised data transfer from space
ESA reported on 31 March 2026 that Belgian company EDGX had launched a compact data-processing payload aboard the Transporter-16 mission the previous day. The hand-sized device combines graphics processing with AI optimisation so satellites can process information in orbit while limiting power consumption. The mission would measure its power use during demanding computing tasks. Designed to be flexible rather than fixed to a single task, the payload can be reconfigured to work with other spacecraft systems as mission needs change. Its development received support from ESA’s Industrial Competitiveness programme within the agency’s Advanced Research in Telecommunications Systems initiative. The flight carried eight CubeSats and a hosted payload backed by ESA on SpaceX Transporter-16 on 30 March 2026. Some demonstrations involved laser links between satellites and ground stations, complementing conventional radio-frequency communication. Five CubeSats were developed within ESA’s Greek Connectivity programme for the Greek government.

title: Fortinet
text:
Fortinet
Fortinet is a cybersecurity company headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. Its security products include physical firewalls, endpoint protection and intrusion detection systems for computer networks. Brothers Ken and Michael Xie founded the business in 2000 under the name Appligation, later changing it to ApSecure and then Fortinet. The Fortinet name came from the phrase “Fortified Networks”. Its first product, the FortiGate firewall, appeared in 2002, followed by antivirus and antispam software. The company subsequently expanded into wireless access points, sandbox security and messaging protection, and went public in November 2009.

title: MediaTek
text:
MediaTek
MediaTek began as a unit of United Microelectronics Corporation, a Taiwanese company, designing chipsets for home entertainment equipment. The business was incorporated separately on 28 May 1997 and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on 23 July 2001 under the code 2454. It initially designed optical-drive chipsets before expanding into DVD players, digital televisions, mobile phones, smartphones and tablets. MediaTek established a mobile-device design division in 2004; seven years later, its annual orders exceeded 500 million mobile system-on-chip units for feature phones and smart devices. In the third quarter of 2020, it became the largest smartphone-chipset vendor, with a 31 percent market share.

title: Ventyx Biosciences — 2024 annual report
text:
Ventyx Biosciences — 2024 annual report
Ventyx Biosciences was incorporated in Delaware in November 2018. Its 2024 annual report gave the principal executive office address as 12790 El Camino Real, Suite 200, San Diego, California 92130. At December 31, 2024, it had 79 full-time employees and 3 part-time employees. Of its employees, 21 held a PhD or MD and 20 worked in research and development. A reduction in force implemented on December 5, 2023 affected approximately 20% of the workforce. The 2024 annual filing includes operating information for Ventyx’s drug-development pipeline and its clinical-stage programmes. It records the company’s principal offices in San Diego, California and details employee and research-related expenses. The filing also discusses risks connected with clinical trials, funding requirements and regulatory approval for new therapeutics.

title: Max Planck Institute for Chemistry
text:
Max Planck Institute for Chemistry
The Max Planck Institute for Chemistry is a research institute in Mainz, Germany, also known as the Otto Hahn Institute and belonging to the Max Planck Society. Its predecessor, the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Chemistry, was founded in Berlin in 1911. Research examines chemical processes throughout the Earth system, especially interactions involving the atmosphere and biosphere. Investigators study relationships among air, water, soil, living organisms, and climate over timescales extending from Earth history to the Anthropocene. The institute has departments devoted to aerosol chemistry, atmospheric chemistry, climate geochemistry, and multiphase chemistry, alongside additional research groups. The founding director was Ernst Beckmann. Otto Hahn served as director from 1928 to 1946. The institute moved to the campus of Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz in 1949. The Climate Geochemistry Department operates the research sailing yacht S/Y Eugen Seibold. The Atmospheric Chemistry Department studies ozone and other atmospheric photo-oxidants, their chemical reactions, and global cycles.

title: Spike Jonze
text:
Spike Jonze
Spike Jonze is the professional name of American filmmaker, actor, musician, and photographer Adam Spiegel, born in 1969. He began by photographing BMX riders and skateboarders and later directed skateboarding films and music videos. His first two feature films, Being John Malkovich and Adaptation, were written by Charlie Kaufman. He also helped create and executive-produce MTV’s Jackass franchise. He subsequently directed films from his own screenplays, including Where the Wild Things Are and Her. Her earned him the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. Jonze co-founded the skateboard company Girl Skateboards in 1993 with Rick Howard, Mike Carroll and Megan Baltimore. He co-starred in David O. Russell's war comedy Three Kings (1999).

title: MANTIS (satellite)
text:
MANTIS (satellite)
MANTIS was an Earth-observation satellite built by Open Cosmos with backing from the European and UK space agencies. The 12U CubeSat tested high-resolution multispectral imaging and onboard data processing. It launched aboard a Falcon 9 rocket in November 2023 and ended its mission by deorbiting in October 2025. The imager demonstrated by MANTIS was the integrated Standard Imager for Microsatellites (iSIM). MANTIS was the first space mission supported by ESA's InCubed programme, managed by the agency's ɸ-lab. The satellite delivered its first Earth images on 20 November 2023. MANTIS was used to de-risk technologies for Atlantic Constellation Pathfinder, UKSA's contribution to the international Atlantic Constellation.

title: Qualys
text:
Qualys
Qualys is an American technology company based in Foster City, California, providing cloud security and compliance services. Its QualysGuard software, launched in 2000, scanned corporate networks for vulnerabilities and looked for available patches. The platform later added compliance tools, malware detection and web application scanning. Qualys listed on Nasdaq under the symbol QLYS in September 2012, raising $87.5 million in net proceeds. In 2015, it introduced a cloud platform and a lightweight agent for continuous monitoring of IT infrastructure and applications. In November 2023, Qualys released Enterprise TruRisk Management software, which aggregates cyber risk signals to provide a risk-scoring framework for companies to measure and reduce IT risk. In May 2024, Qualys launched a managed security services partner portal as part of its global partner program. In March 2026, Qualys debuted Agent Val, an agentic AI tool for exploit validation and autonomous remediation.

title: Apertus (LLM)
text:
Apertus (LLM)
Apertus is a public language model developed by the Swiss AI Initiative, a collaboration between EPFL, ETH Zurich and the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre. Released on September 2, 2025, it uses the Apache 2.0 license and is available to download through Hugging Face. The model was trained on more than 1,800 languages and comes in versions with eight billion and 70 billion parameters. Apertus was initially designed for business and research use cases around the world. The model was developed with the aim of adhering to European copyright law. At launch, its creators emphasized multilinguality, transparency, and auditability as priorities. Chatbots were a secondary rather than a primary use case.

title: National Gilbert & Sullivan Opera Company
text:
National Gilbert & Sullivan Opera Company
The National Gilbert & Sullivan Opera Company is an English professional repertory company devoted to Gilbert and Sullivan’s Savoy operas. It was founded in 1995 to perform at the International Gilbert and Sullivan Festival and stages full-scale productions with an orchestra, period settings and costumes. The company generally presents three or four productions each summer, including performances in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. It began taking productions to additional venues in 2010 and, from 2014, toured several British cities in repertory, giving as many as 42 performances on a tour. In 2014, the festival registered the company with Companies House as the National Gilbert & Sullivan Opera Company. Its performances are accompanied by the National Festival Orchestra. The company has presented all 13 extant Savoy Operas.

title: Cynthia Dwork — Princeton education and career profile
text:
Cynthia Dwork — Princeton education and career profile
Cynthia Dwork earned a BSE in electrical engineering and computer science at Princeton in 1979 and a PhD in computer science at Cornell in 1983. Before her planned move to Harvard in January 2017, she was a distinguished scientist at Microsoft Research in Silicon Valley. Her father was mathematician Bernard Dwork, who taught at Princeton from 1964 and became emeritus in 1993. Dwork earned a computer-science doctorate at Cornell University in 1983 and later worked for Microsoft Research. The 2016 university profile reported more than one hundred refereed journal and conference publications and two dozen patents. Her mathematical contributions established rigorous ways to analyse data while protecting individuals’ privacy. She was scheduled to join Harvard’s computer-science faculty in January 2017.

title: Uri Segal
text:
Uri Segal
Uri Segal is an Israeli conductor born in Jerusalem in 1944. He studied violin and conducting at the Rubin Academy of Music before attending London’s Guildhall School of Music from 1966 to 1969. After winning the Dimitri Mitropolous Conducting Competition in New York in 1969, he spent a year assisting Leonard Bernstein at the New York Philharmonic. Segal subsequently led the Bournemouth Symphony Orchestra and the Philharmonia Hungarica, and served as artistic director of the Israel Chamber Orchestra. In 1990, he became music director of the Chautauqua Symphony Orchestra and founded Osaka’s Century Orchestra, which he led until 1998. His tenure as music director of the Chautauqua Symphony Orchestra continued through 2007. He subsequently became the Century Orchestra's Laureate Conductor. Segal married Ilana Finkelstein in 1966. They have three daughters and a son.

Oven Chips — 2026-01-13 (episode 3483773)

Today, he's following production of their best seller, the straight cut frozen Home Chips. Of course, when it comes to making chips, the main ingredient is potatoes. And as Paddy steps out to the delivery yard, a lorry full of 28 tonnes of them has just arrived.

title: Addis Ababa Science and Technology University
text:
Addis Ababa Science and Technology University
Addis Ababa Science and Technology University (Amharic: አዲስ አበባ ሳይንስና ቴክኖሎጂ ዩኒቨርስቲ), or AASTU, is a higher education institute in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The main campus is located in the Akaky Kaliti subcity, Kilinto area around Tulu dimtu. The concept of Addis Ababa Science and Technology University had a direct and reasonable connection with the Five-Year Growth and Transformation Plan (2010–2015) of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. As it was stated in the plan, the establishment of well institutionalized and strong science and technology universities and institutes of technology will serve as a cornerstone to build an economically developed and industrialized state of Ethiopia.

title: St. Paul University Manila
text:
St. Paul University Manila
St. Paul University Manila (SPUM), also referred by its acronym SPU Manila, is a private, Catholic coeducational basic and higher education institution established and run by the Congregation of the Sisters of Saint Paul of Chartres in Manila, Philippines. It was established in 1912 by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres (SPC), a religious congregation founded in Chartres, France in 1698. It was previously an all-girls' school and turned co-ed beginning school year 2005–2006. In 1912, St. Paul Manila opened a Kindergarten school with an enrollment of six girls, upon request of the families in the neighborhood.The school was named St. Paul Institution.

title: Modibbo Adama Federal University of Technology, Yola
text:
Modibbo Adama Federal University of Technology, Yola
The university's name was changed to Modibbo Adama University of Technology,(MAUTECH) Yola in 2011 with the approval of the then President and Commander in Chief, Dr. Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, GCFR, and it became effective on October 1 of that year. It is named after Modibbo Adama Ibn Hassan(1809-1847), a great scholar, an erudite educationist, an outstanding leader and the founder of the Fombina Kingdom (The Present Adamawa Emirate). As the first ruler and founder of the Emirate, Modibbo Adama Ibn Hassan was one of the disciples and flag bearers of Sheikh Usman Ibn Fodio of the Sokoto Caliphate. The new name took effect from 1 October 2011.

title: One-Hit Wonders at the BBC: Volume 3 — 2026-03-07 (episode 3562631)
text:
One-Hit Wonders at the BBC: Volume 3 — 2026-03-07 (episode 3562631)
The episode “One-Hit Wonders at the BBC: Volume 3” aired on 7 March 2026. It is season 2026, episode 3 of “At the BBC” (TVmaze series ID 24062), with a listed runtime of 60 minutes. This instalment digs deeper into the vaults to unearth more unforgettable one-offs and near misses, reminding why the charts remain such a thrilling, unpredictable arena.

text:

text:
Keir Starmer: Where Did It All Go Wrong? — 2026-03-27 (episode 3576818)

title: University of Kashmir
text:
University of Kashmir
University of Kashmir (UoK), informally known as Kashmir University (KU), is a public state university located in the Hazratbal neighbourhood, on the western side of Dal Lake in the city of Srinagar, in Jammu and Kashmir, India, which was established in 1948. The university offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programs in the fields of liberal arts, business, commerce & management studies, education, law, applied sciences & Technology, biological sciences, physical & material sciences, social sciences, medicine, dentistry, engineering, oriental learning, and music & fine arts. It was awarded Grade "A++" by the NAAC in June 2025. It was awarded rank 34 among universities in India by NIRF ranking 2025.

title: Mar 26 Thur — 2026-03-26 (episode 3577508)
text:
Mar 26 Thur — 2026-03-26 (episode 3577508)
The episode “Mar 26 Thur” aired on 26 March 2026. It is season 2026, episode 77 of “NBC Nightly News” (TVmaze series ID 9539), with a listed runtime of 30 minutes. It's "too much to bear," she tells Hoda Kotb in a deeply moving conversation about the search for answers. Savannah opens up to Hoda Kotb about the outpouring of love and support that she's felt since her mother was taken 54 days ago.

text:
HUNTER DOOHAN: From Arkansas Bullying to Global Stardom & How He Finally Found His Voice — 2026-01-13 (episode 3509681)

Hunter opens up about growing up closeted in Arkansas, losing his father to ALS, and the way grief shaped his early adulthood.

title: Istanbul Technical University
text:
Istanbul Technical University
Istanbul Technical University, also known as Technical University of Istanbul (Turkish: İstanbul Teknik Üniversitesi, commonly referred to as İTÜ), is a public technical university located in Istanbul, Turkey. It is the world's third-oldest technical university dedicated to engineering and natural sciences as well as social sciences recently. İTÜ is ranked 79th globally and first in Turkey in the field of Engineering and Technology, as well as 182nd globally and first in Turkey in the field of Natural Sciences, according to the QS World University Rankings for 2025. The university has 92 undergraduate programs and 188 graduate programs in 14 faculties, 277,160 m2 of laboratory space, and 12 research centers.

title: Mary Poppins Knockoff and Filial Grief Turned Property Beef — 2026-03-18 (episode 3528142)
text:
Mary Poppins Knockoff and Filial Grief Turned Property Beef — 2026-03-18 (episode 3528142)

She claims safety concerns over a new housemate with a troubled past prompted her sudden departure. In the second case, a grieving mother accuses her late daughter's ex-boyfriend of withholding her belongings after a fatal car accident.

title: University of Atlántico
text:
University of Atlántico
The University of Atlántico (Spanish: Universidad del Atlántico), also called Uniatlántico, is a public, departmental, coeducational, research university based in the city of Barranquilla, Atlántico, Colombia. It is the largest higher education institution by student population in the Colombian Caribbean region with 24,113 students, and a faculty of 656 full-time equivalent professors. The university was established by the ordinance No. 24 of 1941 as the Institute of Technology of Atlántico (Spanish: Instituto de Tecnología del Atlántico), under the tutelage of philosopher Julio Enrique Blanco. Then, it changed its name to the present by Ordinance No. 42 of June 15, 1946.

title: University of Mary Washington
text:
University of Mary Washington
University of Mary Washington (UMW) is a public liberal arts university in Fredericksburg, Virginia. Established in 1908 as the State Normal and Industrial School for Women at Fredericksburg, the institution later became known as Fredericksburg Teachers College, and was named Mary Washington College in 1938 after Mary Ball Washington, mother of the first president of the United States, George Washington. The General Assembly of Virginia changed the college's name to University of Mary Washington in 2004 to reflect the addition of graduate and professional programs to the central undergraduate curriculum, as well as the establishment of more than one campus.

title: Breaking the Deadlock (series 84620)
text:
Breaking the Deadlock (series 84620)
The series “Breaking the Deadlock” has TVmaze series ID 84620 and premiered on 20 September 2024. Its listed language is English. The broadcast network listed for the series is PBS. Breaking the Deadlock brings together people from across the political spectrum in a way that requires them to go beyond the usual talking points and speak to our core values as Americans," said moderator Aaron Tang. "By using hypothetical scenarios that rhyme with reality, we create space for honest introspection and conversation—and even some surprising breakthroughs." Each episode of Breaking the Deadlock dives into essential questions of community, accountability and personal responsibility, sparking legal, moral and ethical reflections.

title: Banner Health
text:
Banner Health
Banner Health is a nonprofit health system in the United States, based in Phoenix, Arizona. It operates 33 hospitals and several specialized facilities across 6 states. The health system is the largest employer in Arizona and one of the largest in the United States with over 55,000 employees. The organization provides emergency and hospital care, hospice, long-term/home care, outpatient surgery, labs, rehabilitation services, pharmacies, and primary care. In 2024, it reports $14.1 billion in revenue for the previous year. Banner Health was created in 1999 through a merger between Lutheran Health Systems, based in North Dakota, and Samaritan Health System, based in Phoenix, Arizona.

title: Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry
text:
Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry
The Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry (MPIB; German: Max-Planck-Institut für Biochemie) is a research institute of the Max Planck Society located in Martinsried, a suburb of Munich. The institute was founded in 1973 by the merger of three formerly independent institutes: the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, the Max Planck Institute of Protein and Leather Research (founded 1954 in Regensburg), and the Max Planck Institute of Cell Chemistry (founded 1956 in Munich). With about 750 employees in currently nine research departments and more than 20 research groups, the MPIB is one of the largest institutes of the Max Planck Society.

title: UPMC Hillman Cancer Center
text:
UPMC Hillman Cancer Center
The UPMC Hillman Cancer Center, previously the University of Pittsburgh Cancer Institute (UPCI), is a National Cancer Institute (NCI)-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center located in the Hillman Cancer Center in the Shadyside neighborhood of Pittsburgh, adjacent to UPMC Shadyside. The only NCI-designated cancer center in Western Pennsylvania, Hillman is composed of collaborative academic and research efforts between the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC), and Carnegie Mellon University. Hillman provides clinical cancer care to some 74,000 patients treated at its facilities at both the Hillman Cancer Center location in the Shadyside neighborhood of Pittsburgh and at UPMC-affiliated sites throughout Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, and overseas locations.

title: North West England: Judging — 2026-02-24 (episode 3555604)
text:
North West England: Judging — 2026-02-24 (episode 3555604)

They need to impress a panel of exacting judges: Michelin-starred chef Tom Kerridge, former Great British Menu Champion of Champions Lorna McNee, and comedian and all-round food enthusiast Phil Wang. The guest judge is Debbie McWilliams, a veteran film casting director responsible for casting James Bond films since 1981. How will she judge dishes celebrating the British film industry?

title: 60 Minutes (series 4022)
text:
60 Minutes (series 4022)
The series “60 Minutes” has TVmaze series ID 4022 and premiered on 24 September 1968. Its listed language is English. The broadcast network listed for the series is CBS. 60 Minutes has been on the air since 1968, beginning on a Tuesday, but spending most of its time on Sundays, where it remains today. This popular news magazine provides both hard hitting investigations, interviews and features, along with people in the news and current events. 60 Minutes has set unprecedented records in the Nielsen's ratings with a number 1 rating, five times, making it among the most successful TV programs in all of television history.

text:
Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University
Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University (Russian: Санкт-Петербургский политехнический университет Петра Великого, romanized: Sankt-Peterburgskiy politekhnicheskiy universitet Petra Velikogo), abbreviated as SPbPU (СПбПУ), is a public technical university located in Saint Petersburg, Russia. The university houses one of the country's most advanced research labs in hydro–aerodynamics. The university's alumni include Nobel Prize winners, such as Pyotr Kapitsa and Zhores Alferov, physicists and atomic weapon designers such as Yulii Khariton, Nikolay Dukhov, Abram Ioffe, Aleksandr Leipunskii, and Yakov Zeldovich, aircraft designers and aerospace engineers, such as Yulii Khariton, Oleg Antonov, Nikolai Polikarpov, and Georgy Beriev, and chess grandmasters, such as David Bronstein. title: Field Museum of Natural History
text:
Field Museum of Natural History
The Field Museum of Natural History (FMNH; also known as the Field Museum) is a private–public natural history museum in Chicago, Illinois, and is one of the largest such museums in the world. The museum is popular for the size and quality of its educational and scientific programs, as well as its extensive scientific specimen and artifact collections. A private nonprofit institution, the museum operates in close partnership with the municipal government agency Chicago Park District, which owns the land and building. The museum is run by a private Board of Trustees and funded through a combination of ticket sales, memberships, donations, endowments, and grants, along with some public funding for specific programs or maintenance.

title: Rafael Urdaneta University
text:
Rafael Urdaneta University
Rafael Urdaneta University; URU (Spanish: Universidad Rafael Urdaneta) is a private, non-profit university founded in 1973, located at La Vereda del Lago (Maracaibo, Venezuela), by the Rafael Urdaneta foundation and the Rafael Urdaneta university civic association. It receives its name from the general Rafael Urdaneta, Zulian father of Venezuelan independence. Rafael Urdaneta University is a higher education institute whose purpose is to generate and apply the imparted knowledge to contribute to the evolution of the human being and to the formation of professionals with values, independent, competitive and compromised to the scientific, technical and humanistic development of the social environment to elaborate sustainable projects that resolve the problems of the State and the Nation.

title: Marshall Space Flight Center
text:
Marshall Space Flight Center
The Marshall Space Flight Center (officially the George C. Marshall Space Flight Center; MSFC), located in Redstone Arsenal, Alabama (Huntsville postal address), is the U.S. government's civilian rocketry and spacecraft propulsion research center. As the largest NASA center, MSFC's first mission was developing the Saturn launch vehicles for the Apollo program. Marshall has been the lead center for the Space Shuttle main propulsion and external tank; payloads and related crew training; International Space Station (ISS) design and assembly; computers, networks, and information management; and the Space Launch System. Located on the Redstone Arsenal near Huntsville, MSFC is named in honor of General of the Army George C. Marshall.

title: Jordan University Hospital
text:
Jordan University Hospital
Jordan University Hospital (JUH) (Arabic: مستشفى الجامعة الأردنية) is a public teaching hospital located on the University of Jordan campus in the Jubeiha district of Amman, Jordan. Established in 1973 as The Great Amman Hospital (Arabic: مستشفى عمان الكبير), it was integrated into the University of Jordan in 1975 and renamed Jordan University Hospital. JUH is the first university-affiliated teaching hospital in Jordan, and has grown into a major tertiary care center serving patients from across Jordan and neighboring countries. The hospital handles a high volume of patients (over half a million annually) and offers advanced medical services in numerous specialties.

title: Geosciences Barcelona (GEO3BCN)
text:
Geosciences Barcelona (GEO3BCN)
Geosciences Barcelona (acronym: GEO3BCN), formerly known as Institute of Earth Sciences Jaume Almera (or in Spanish Instituto de Ciencias de la Tierra Jaume Almera, ICTJA) is an earth science public research institute of the Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC). It was created  in Barcelona (Spain) in 1965 (41.3847°N 2.1191°E﻿ / 41.3847; 2.1191) and it is considered among the top research institutes in Earth Sciences in Spain. It is also known in Catalan as Institut de Ciències de la Terra Jaume Almera and was created as the Instituto de Geología de Barcelona. Its former name (before 2020) referred to the Spanish geologist Jaume Almera.

title: United Nations Capital Development Fund
text:
United Nations Capital Development Fund
The United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans and guarantees, first and foremost for the least developed countries (LDCs) among the developing countries. As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact where the needs are greatest—a capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate—to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

title: College of Europe

College of Europe
The College of Europe in Bruges was founded in 1949 as a result of the 1948 Congress of Europe in The Hague by leading historical European figures and founding fathers of the European Union, including Salvador de Madariaga, Winston Churchill, Paul-Henri Spaak and Alcide De Gasperi, to promote "a spirit of solidarity and mutual understanding between all the nations of Western Europe and to provide elite training to individuals who will uphold these values" and "to train an elite of young executives for Europe". After the fall of communism, the College opened an additional campus in Natolin, Poland, that was donated to the institution by the Polish government in 1992.

title: Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology
text:
Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology
The Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology Bhopal (MANIT or NIT Bhopal or NIT-B) is a public technical university located in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India. It is part of a group of publicly funded institutions in India known as National Institutes of Technology. It is named after the Independent India's first Minister of Education (India), scholar and independence activist Maulana Abdul Kalam Azad who is commonly remembered as Maulana Azad. Established in the year 1960 as Maulana Azad College of Technology (MACT) or Regional Engineering College (REC), Bhopal, it became a National Institute of Technology in 2002 and was recognised as an Institute of National Importance under the NIT Act in 2007.

title: Ariel University
text:
Ariel University
Ariel University (Hebrew: אוניברסיטת אריאל), previously a public college known as the Ariel University Center of Samaria, is an Israeli university located in the urban Israeli settlement of Ariel in the West Bank. The college  was founded in 1982 as a regional branch of Bar-Ilan University and was originally located in the settlement of Kedumim, After moving  to a larger campus in Ariel, it  became the largest Israeli public college. In 2004–2005, the affiliation with Bar-Ilan ended and it became an independent college. On 17 July 2012, the Council for Higher Education in Judea and Samaria voted to grant the institution full university status.

title: Maejo University

Maejo University (MJU; also spelled Maecho University; Thai: มหาวิทยาลัยแม่โจ้; RTGS: Mahawitthayalai Mae Cho) in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, is the oldest agricultural institution in the country. Founded in 1934 as the Northern Agricultural Teachers Training School, it was restructured and renamed several times until it gained the status of a full-fledged public university in 1996 and since then has been known as Maejo University. Maejo University main campus at Chiang Mai is composed of the faculties of Business, Economics, Liberal Arts, Tourism Development, Information Technology, Fisheries Technology and Aquatic Resources, Animal Sciences and Technology, Renewable Energy, Administrative, Landscape and Environmental Design, Agricultural Production, Science, and Engineering and Agro-Industry.

title: Toronto Metropolitan University
text:
Toronto Metropolitan University
Toronto Metropolitan University (TMU or Toronto Met), formerly known as Ryerson University, is a public research university located in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The university's core campus is situated within the Garden District in downtown Toronto, although it also operates facilities elsewhere in the city and a satellite campus in Brampton for its medical school. The university includes nine academic divisions: the Faculty of Arts, the Faculty of Community Services, the Faculty of Engineering and Architectural Science, the Faculty of Science, The Creative School, the Lincoln Alexander School of Law, the Ted Rogers School of Management, the School of Medicine, and the Yeates School of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies.

title: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel
text:
GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel
The GEOMAR - Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel (GEOMAR), formerly known as the Leibniz Institute of Marine Sciences (German: Leibniz-Institut für Meereswissenschaften, IFM-GEOMAR), is a research institute in Kiel, Germany. It was formed in 2004 by merging the Institute for Marine Science (Institut für Meereskunde Kiel, (IFM)) with the Research Center for Marine Geosciences (GEOMAR) and is co-funded by both federal and provincial governments. It was a member of the Leibniz Association until 2012 and is coordinator of the FishBase Consortium. Since 2012 it is member of the Helmholtz Association and named GEOMAR - Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel.

title: Corvinus University of Budapest
text:
Corvinus University of Budapest
Corvinus University of Budapest (Hungarian: Budapesti Corvinus Egyetem) is a private research university in Budapest, Hungary. The university currently has an enrolment of approximately 9,600 students, with a primary focus on business administration, economics, and social sciences, operating in Budapest and Székesfehérvár since 1948. Corvinus University accepts students at six faculties and offer courses leading to degrees at the bachelor, master and doctoral level in specialisations taught in Hungarian, English, French or German. Corvinus alumni include a former prime minister of Hungary, governors of the Hungarian National Bank as well as various members of the Hungarian political and business elite.

Jenderal Soedirman University
Jenderal Soedirman University (Indonesian: Universitas Jenderal Soedirman, Javanese: ꦲꦸꦤꦶꦮ꦳ꦼꦂꦱꦶꦠꦱ꧀​ꦗꦺꦤ꧀ꦢꦼꦫꦭ꧀​ꦱꦸꦢꦶꦂꦩꦤ꧀, abbreviated as Unsoed) is a public university located in Purwokerto, Banyumas Regency, Central Java, Indonesia and was established on September 23, 1963. He was born in the Banyumas region. Due to its location nearby to Mount Slamet and Purwokerto as a relatively small city, Unsoed is mostly preferred by students because of its cold and comfortable environment and provides an affordable living costs for university students in general.

title: Wayamba University of Sri Lanka
text:
Wayamba University of Sri Lanka
Wayamba University of Sri Lanka (Sinhala: ශ්‍රී ලංකා වයඹ විශ්වවිද්‍යාලය, romanized: śrī laṁkā vayam̆ba viśvavidyālaya, Tamil: இலங்கை வயம்ப பல்கலைக்கழகம், romanized: Ilaṅkai vayampa palkalaikkaḻakam) is the thirteenth national university in Sri Lanka. It was established as the Affiliated University College of North Western Province in 1991 and it became the Rajarata University of Sri Lanka "Wayamba mandapa" in 1996. It was a full-fledged university naming as Wayamba University of Sri Lanka in 1999. The main purpose of the university is offering English-medium degrees, diplomas and certificate courses (internal and external) in areas such as Agriculture, Applied Science, Management and Technology for students and working professionals.

title: Federal University of Lafia
text:
Federal University of Lafia
The Federal University of Lafia (formerly Federal University, Lafia) is a public university in Lafia, the capital of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. It was established on 9 February 2011 as one of nine new federal universities created under the Federal Government’s university expansion programme to increase access to higher education. The university commenced academic activities in September 2012 with new students that made up the first set of students to be trained by the university Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ekanem Ikpi Braide. In October 2025, Professor Mohammed Isa Kida was appointed as the Vice-Chancellor of the university for a five-year term, succeeding Professor Shehu Abdul Rahman.

title: Quadram Institute
text:
Quadram Institute
The Quadram Institute is a centre for food and health research, combining Quadram Institute Bioscience (formerly the Institute of Food Research), the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals' endoscopy centre and aspects of the University of East Anglia's Norwich Medical School and the Faculty of Science. It is located on the outskirts of Norwich, England, and is a member of the Norwich Research Park. The institute is housed in a purpose-built facility on the Norwich Research Park that opened in 2018. Its founding partners are Quadram Institute Bioscience, University of East Anglia, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital and the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council.

title: Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University
text:
Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University
Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University (FAFU) is a provincial public university of agriculture and forestry in Fuzhou, Fujian, China. It is affiliated with the Province of Fujian, and co-funded by the Fujian Provincial People's Government, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, and the National Forestry and Grassland Administration. In 1952, Fujian Agricultural College was established by the merger of the then Agricultural College of Xiamen University (厦门大学农学院) and the then Agricultural College of Fuzhou University (福州大学农学院). In October 2000, the then Fujian Agricultural University and the then Fujian Forestry College (福建林学院) merged to form the new Fujian Agricultural and Forestry University.

University of Sarajevo
The University of Sarajevo (Bosnian: Univerzitet u Sarajevu; Croatian: Sveučilište u Sarajevu; Serbian: Универзитет у Сарајеву) is a public university located in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. With 20 faculties, three academies and three faculties of theology and with 23,127 enrolled students as of 2021, it ranks among the largest universities in the Balkans in terms of enrollment. Since opening its doors in 1949, a total of 122,000 students have received bachelor's degrees, 3,891 have received master's degrees and 2,284 have received doctorate degrees in 45 different fields. It is now widely regarded as the most prestigious university in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and employs more than one thousand faculty members.

title: Guangxi Minzu University

Guangxi Minzu University
Guangxi Minzu University (simplified Chinese: 广西民族大学; traditional Chinese: 廣西民族大學, Zhuang: Gvangjsih Minzcuz Dayoz, abbreviated GXMZU) is a provincial research university in Nanning, Guangxi. Established in 1952 to serve the ethnic minority populations in Guangxi, the university has historical strengths in ethnology and foreign languages. Originally a branch campus of the Central Institute for Nationalities, the university has evolved into an independent university which grants bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees across 26 colleges, academic departments, and professional schools. Half of its 16,000 students are classified as an ethnic minority, with representation from 53 out of 55 recognized ethnic minority groups including the Zhuang, Miao, Yao, and Yi peoples.

title: Morehouse College
text:
Morehouse College
Morehouse College is a private, historically black, men's liberal arts college in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. Anchored by its main campus of 61 acres (25 ha) near downtown Atlanta, the college has a variety of residential dorms and academic buildings east of Ashview Heights. Along with Spelman College, Clark Atlanta University, Morris Brown College, and the Morehouse School of Medicine, the college is a member of the Atlanta University Center consortium. Founded by William Jefferson White in 1867 in response to the liberation of enslaved African Americans following the American Civil War, Morehouse stressed preparatory and religious instruction in the Baptist tradition for students who had been prevented from receiving education by former slave laws.

title: El Colegio de México
text:
El Colegio de México
El Colegio de México, A.C. (commonly known as Colmex, English: The College of Mexico) is a Mexican institute of higher education, specializing in teaching and research in social sciences and humanities. The college was founded in 1940 by the Mexican Federal Government, the Bank of Mexico (Banco de México), the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), and the Fondo de Cultura Económica. In the late 1930s, following the end of the Spanish Civil War, Mexican president Lázaro Cardenas created the House of Spain in Mexico (1938–1940) to host Spanish intellectuals in exile in Mexico; Mexico was the only country that in 1939 welcomed Spanish refugees.

The Institute of Spectroscopy Russian Academy of Sciences (ISAN) (in some sources the abbreviation used is ISAS, IS RAS) is a Russian research institution located in Troitsk, Moscow 

At present (2010) ISAN has eight research departments, which activity covers practically all kinds of spectroscopies: atomic, molecular, plasma, gases, liquids, condensed matter, amorphous solids, glasses, crystals, nanostructures, polymers, biological systems. The available equipment allows for measurements in a broad spectral range; with ultimate spectral, spatial and temporal resolutions; in a broad range of temperatures and measurement times; with application of external fields. title: Natural Resources Canada

Natural Resources Canada
Natural Resources Canada (NRCan; French: Ressources naturelles Canada; RNCan) is the department of the Government of Canada responsible for natural resources, energy, minerals and metals, forests, earth sciences, mapping, and remote sensing. It was formed in 1994 by amalgamating the Department of Energy, Mines and Resources with the Department of Forestry. Under the Constitution Act, 1867, primary responsibility for natural resources falls to provincial governments, however, the federal government has jurisdiction over off-shore resources, trade and commerce in natural resources, statistics, international relations, and boundaries. The department administers federal legislation relating to natural resources, including energy, forests, minerals and metals.

Hohai University (HHU; Chinese: 河海大学; pinyin: Héhǎi Dàxué) is a public university in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. It is affiliated with the Ministry of Education of China, and co-sponsored by the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Water Resources, the State Oceanic Administration, and the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government. title: Technological University Dublin

Technological University Dublin
Technological University Dublin (Irish: Ollscoil Teicneolaíochta Bhaile Átha Cliath) or TU Dublin is Ireland's first technological university. It was established on 1 January 2019, with a history going back to 1887 through the amalgamated Dublin Institute of Technology which progressed from the first technical education institution in Ireland, the City of Dublin Technical Schools. It is the second-largest third-level institution in Ireland, with a student population of 28,500. The university was formed by the amalgamation of three existing institutes of technology in the Dublin area – Dublin Institute of Technology, Institute of Technology, Blanchardstown, and Institute of Technology, Tallaght, taking over all functions and operations of these institutions.

It has international branches and affiliate schools. A brainchild of Ali Khamenei, the university has provided Islamic education exclusively to international students (including female scholars) mostly at a graduate level, in a combined seminary and academic format focused on the study of the Comparative Religion, Quran, Hadith, Islamic Jurisprudence, Islamic Philosophy and Discourse, Islamic Mysticism, Economics, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, Education, Management, Persian Language and Literature, and Arabic. It is a research and education institution qualified as a Social Organization (SO) under the auspices of the Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (MCTIC) and the Ministry of Education (MEC) of Brazil. Academic work began at the university in 1990 with the matriculation of its pioneer students. It was later renamed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to "Yakubu Gowon University" on 16 December 2024, in honor of General Yakubu Gowon, a former head of state and president of Nigeria on his 90th birthday, "for his exceptional contribution to Nigeria's unity and his commitment to the country's progress".

title: Purple Mountain Observatory
text:
Purple Mountain Observatory
Purple Mountain Observatory, also known as Zijinshan Astronomical Observatory, is a dual-use astronomical observatory operated by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and the People's Liberation Army Aerospace Force (PLAASF). It is headquartered at Purple Mountain, east of Nanjing, with off-site sensor installations located across the country. The observatory has a very active open science role, serving as China's primary contribution to the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee, global asteroid impact avoidance efforts, and calculating the official Chinese calendar. Since the early 2000s, the observatory has gained a significant classified intelligence role, serving as China's primary optical space domain awareness capability.

title: Stanford University
text:
Stanford University
Leland Stanford Junior University, commonly referred to as Stanford University, is a private research university in Stanford, California, United States. It was founded in 1885 by railroad magnate Leland Stanford (the eighth governor of and then-incumbent United States senator representing California) and his wife, Jane, in memory of their only child, Leland Stanford Jr., who died from typhoid at the age of 15. The university admitted its first students in 1891, opening as a coeducational and non-denominational institution. It struggled financially after Leland died in 1893 and again after much of the campus was damaged by the 1906 San Francisco earthquake.

Instituto de Assistência Médica ao Servidor Público Estadual (IAMSPE) (State Government Employee Medical Assistance Institute) is an economically self-sufficient governmental health system in the Brazilian State of São Paulo that attends to the health needs of state government employees, their families, and dependents. It is a huge institution, and includes the State Government Employee Hospital (Hospital do Servidor Público Estadual) "Francisco Morato de Oliveira" (HSPE-FMO) in the capital, São Paulo, inaugurated in July 1961. It was founded in 1952 as Departamento de Assistência Médica ao Servidor Público (DAMSPE) in the State of São Paulo. In 1961, it was opened as HSPE-FMO and 1966 it became IAMSPE.

The Royal Observatory of Belgium (Dutch: Koninklijke Sterrenwacht van België; French: Observatoire royal de Belgique; German: Königliche Sternwarte von Belgien) has been situated in the Uccle municipality of Brussels since 1890. It is part of the institutions of the Belgian Federal Science Policy Office (BELSPO). The Royal Observatory was first established in Saint-Josse-ten-Noode in 1826 by King William I of the Netherlands under the impulse of the astronomer and mathematician Adolphe Quetelet. It was home to a 100 cm (39 in) diameter aperture Zeiss reflector in the first half of the 20th century, one of the largest telescopes in the world at the time.

The Carlos III Health Institute (Spanish: Instituto de Salud Carlos III; ISCIII) is a Spanish public health research institute, legally constituted as a public research agency (organismo público de investigación), a type of quasi-autonomous entity under Spanish law. The ISCIII is integrated in the Department of Science and Innovation, although it also reports to the Department of Health in the institute's activities relating health, healthcare and its planning. The institute is named after King Charles III. It was founded in 1986 to promote research in biomedicine and health sciences and to develop and provide scientific and technical guidance for the Spanish National Health System and the benefit of society in general.

The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is the component of the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) led by the under secretary of veterans affairs for health that implements the healthcare program of the VA through a nationalized healthcare service in the United States, providing healthcare and healthcare-adjacent services to veterans through the administration and operation of 146 VA Medical Centers (VAMC) with integrated outpatient clinics, 772 Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOC), and 134 VA Community Living Centers (VA Nursing Home) Programs. title: University of London
text:
University of London
The University of London (UoL; abbreviated as Lond or more rarely Londin in post-nominals) is a federal public research university in London, England, United Kingdom. The university was established by royal charter in 1836 as a degree-awarding examination board for students holding certificates from University College London, King's College London, and "other such institutions, corporate or unincorporated, as shall be established for the purpose of Education, whether within the Metropolis or elsewhere within our United Kingdom". It is one of three institutions to have claimed the title of the third-oldest university in England. It moved to a federal structure with constituent colleges in 1900.

title: Human Sciences Research Council
text:
Human Sciences Research Council
The Human Sciences Research Council (HSRC) of South Africa is Africa's largest dedicated social science and humanities research agency and policy think tank. It primarily conducts large-scale, policy-relevant, social-scientific projects for public-sector users, for non governmental organisations and international development agencies in support of development nationally, in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) and in Africa. The HSRC also seeks to contribute to the research and development strategy of the HSRC's parent Department of Science and Technology, especially through its mission to focus on the contribution of science and technology to addressing poverty. The HSRC originates in the National Bureau of Education and Social Research (founded in 1929).

The University of Batna 2 (Mostefa Ben Boulaïd) (Arabic: جامعة باتنة 2 مصطفى بن بولعيد) is a non-profit Algerian public University located in Fesdis, Wilaya of Batna in Algeria. It was founded in 1977 as University of Batna and then restructured in July 2015 by presidential decree, which led to a split into two distinct universities, namely University of Batna 1 and University of Batna 2. title: Institute for Advanced Studies in Basic Sciences

Institute for Advanced Studies in Basic Sciences

The goal of establishing IASBS was to provide a leading research-based institute in advanced science topics for both researchers and students in Iran. The institute offers various M.Sc. and PhD degrees in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Geophysics, Biophysics, Biochemistry and Chemistry. Although IASBS was established as a graduate-level degree-granting institution, it also offers a B.Sc. program in Computer Engineering.

title: Central Philippine University
text:
Central Philippine University
Central Philippine University (also known as Central or CPU) is a private Protestant research university  in Iloilo City, Philippines. Established in 1905 through a grant from the American industrialist and philanthropist John D. Rockefeller, as the Jaro Industrial School and Bible School under the supervision of the American Baptist Foreign Mission Society, it is "the first Baptist and the second American and Protestant-founded university in the Philippines and in Asia". The university pioneered nursing education in the Philippines through the establishment of the Union Mission Hospital Training School for Nurses (now CPU College of Nursing) in 1906, the first nursing school in the Philippines.

title: University of Hagen
text:
University of Hagen
The University of Hagen (German: FernUniversität in Hagen, informally often referred to as FU Hagen) is a public research university that is primarily focused on distance teaching. While its main campus is located in Hagen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, the university maintains more than 50 study and research centers in Germany and throughout Europe. According to the Federal Statistical Office of Germany, it is Germany's second-largest university. The university was founded in 1974 as a public research university by the state Nordrhein-Westfalen and began its research and teaching activities in 1975. It was founded following the idea of UK's Open University to provide higher and continuing education opportunities through a distance education system in Germany.

CHUMT also offers a number of graduate programs, including a Master of Science in Medical Laboratory Science, a Master of Science in Nursing, a Master of Science in Rehabilitation Sciences, and a Master of Science in Health Care Management. title: Nanyang Technological University
text:
Nanyang Technological University
Nanyang Technological University (NTU) is a national public research university in Singapore. Founded in 1981, it is also the second oldest autonomous university in the country. In response to Singapore’s economic restructuring in the 1970s amid a shortage of engineers, the government established the Nanyang Technological Institute (NTI) in 1981 on the former campus of Nanyang University, with engineering and applied science-focused programmes that emphasised laboratory training and industrial attachments. NTI was elevated to full university status and officially inaugurated as NTU on 1 July 1991 through parliamentary legislation, incorporating the National Institute of Education to support national goals of industrial upgrading and research-intensive higher education in science and technology.

title: Kobe University
text:
Kobe University
Kobe University (神戸大学, Kōbe daigaku), also known in the Kansai region as Shindai (神大), is a national research university located in Kobe, Hyōgo, Japan. The university was established in 1949, but the academic origins of Kobe University trace back to the establishment of Kobe Higher Commercial School in 1902, which was renamed as Kobe University of Commerce in 1929, and Kobe University of Economics in 1940. It comprises 14 graduate schools and 11 undergraduate faculties, and has a total enrollment of about 16,000 students in undergraduate and graduate programs. International students accounted for 1,179 members of the student body as of 1 May 2021.

title: Institute of Economic Growth
text:
Institute of Economic Growth
The Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) is an autonomous, multidisciplinary Centre for advanced research and training. Established in 1958, its faculty of about 23 social scientists (economists, demographers and sociologists) and a large body of supporting research staff focus on areas of social and policy concern. IEG's research falls into nine broad themes: Agriculture and rural development, environment and resource economics; globalization and trade; industry, labour and welfare; macro-economic policy and modeling; population and development; health policy; and social change and social structure. In addition, the Institute organizes regular training programmes for the trainee officers of the Indian Economic Service and occasional courses for officers of the Indian Statistical Service, NABARD, and university teachers.

title: Prince Sultan University
text:
Prince Sultan University
Prince Sultan University (PSU) (Arabic: جامعة الأمير سلطان), formerly Prince Sultan College, is a private university in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located in the King Salman Neighborhood. Established in 1998, it is the first private institute of Saudi Arabia and was named after the country's then-defense minister Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz, who later served as the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia from 2005 until his death in 2011. Initially, it was founded as Prince Sultan Private College in 1998 by the Riyadh Philanthropic Society for Sciences and received university status in 2003. The university offers a number of bachelor's and master's degrees in various business, technical, and humanities fields.

title: Kharkiv National Medical University
