University of Notre Dame
The University of Notre Dame du Lac (known simply as Notre Dame;   NOH-tər-DAYM; ND) is a private Catholic research university in Notre Dame, Indiana, United States. The university was founded in 1842 by members of the Congregation of Holy Cross, a Catholic religious order of priests and brothers. Its main campus covers 1,261 acres (510 ha) in a suburban setting and has landmarks such as the Golden Dome main building, Sacred Heart Basilica, the Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes, the Word of Life mosaic mural, and Notre Dame Stadium. Notre Dame is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research spending and doctorate production".

title: Charles Darwin University
text:
Charles Darwin University
Charles Darwin University (CDU) is an Australian public university with two campuses in Darwin and six satellite campuses in metropolitan and regional areas of the Northern Territory and New South Wales. It was established in 2003 after the merger of Northern Territory University, the Menzies School of Health Research, and Centralian College. It is the largest tertiary education provider in the Northern Territory and the first dual-sector university in Australia, offering both academic degree and vocational education programs. It has close ties to First Nations learning and research and was recognized as the most equitable university in Australia in 2025.

The Autonomous University of Mexico State   (Spanish: Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México) (UAEM) is a public university in the State of Mexico, Mexico. It is the largest university institution in the state with over 84,500 students, with its central campus located in the state capital of Toluca. Formalised as a university under the UAEM name in 1956, the institution traces its origins back to 1828 with the foundation Instituto Literario del Estado de México, in the former state capital of Tlalpan. In 1943 the institution was augmented to become the Instituto Científico y Literario de Toluca (ICLA), and thirteen years later obtaining its present name and institutional status.

The university bears the name “19 May”, which marks the date when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of the Republic of Turkey, came to Samsun in order to start the War of Independence. OMU consists of 16 Faculties, 1 Conservatoire (OMU Samsun State Conservatoire), 3 Schools (School of Civil Aviation, School of Foreign Languages, Samsun Health School), 11 Vocational Schools and 5 Institutes (Educational Sciences, Fine Arts, Health Sciences, Science and Technology, and Social Sciences). Its 2,175-acre main campus is centred on Atakum municipality in Samsun.

For nearly 50 years, IFPRI has worked with policymakers, academics, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, development practitioners, and others to carry out research, capacity strengthening, and policy communications on food systems, economic development, and poverty reduction. It is part of Northwell Health and is one of two primary teaching hospitals for the Zucker School of Medicine, alongside Long Island Jewish Medical Center, offering residency programs, postgraduate training programs and clinical fellowships. North Shore University Hospital is a Level I Trauma Center, has 806 beds and has a staff of approximately 7,000. The hospital is considered the flagship quaternary care facility of the Northwell system and as such offers care in all medical specialties, including cardiovascular services, cancer care, orthopedics, maternal-fetal medicine and women's health services.

text:
Cologne University of Applied Sciences
Cologne University of Applied Sciences, officially called TH Köln – University of Applied Sciences (German: Technische Hochschule Köln, abbreviated TH Köln) is an institute of higher education located in Cologne, Germany, established in 1971. It was created from a merger of numerous smaller colleges, the oldest of which was the Royal Provincial Trade School, founded in 1833, and renamed Trade College of the City of Cologne on 15 December 1879. TH Köln is the largest University of Applied Sciences in Germany by number of students, having about 21,000 students and 440 professors and headquartered in Cologne Südstadt. The TH Köln offers a total of 100 bachelor's and master's degrees.

title: Trinity College Dublin
text:
Trinity College Dublin
The College of the Holy and Undivided Trinity of Queen Elizabeth near Dublin, branded by the board as Trinity College, the University of Dublin, and officially incorporated as Trinity College Dublin (TCD; Irish: Coláiste na Tríonóide, Baile Átha Cliath), is the sole constituent college of the University of Dublin in Ireland. Founded in 1592 by Queen Elizabeth I through a royal charter, it is one of the seven ancient universities of Great Britain and Ireland. As Ireland's oldest university, Trinity contributed to Irish literature during the Victorian and Georgian eras and played a notable role in the recognition of Dublin as a UNESCO City of Literature.

title: Crop Trust
text:
Crop Trust
The Crop Trust, officially known as the Global Crop Diversity Trust, is an international nonprofit organization with a secretariat in Bonn, Germany. Its mission is to conserve and make available the world's crop diversity for food security. Established in 2004, the Crop Trust is the only organization whose sole mission is to safeguard the world's crop diversity for future food security. Through an endowment fund for crop diversity, the Crop Trust provides financial support for key international and national genebanks that hold collections of diversity for food crops available under the International Treaty for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA).

title: Singidunum University
text:

Singidunum University (Serbian: Универзитет Сингидунум, romanized: Univerzitet Singidunum) is a private university in Belgrade, Serbia which offers undergraduate, master and doctoral academics studies in three scientific fields – social sciences and humanities; technical sciences; and natural sciences and mathematics. As of 2023–24 academic year, the university consists of three faculties, has 391 academic staff and 9,330 enrolled students, which makes it the largest private university in Serbia. The first faculty was founded in 1999, and the university itself was established on 17 January 2005. The university is organized according to the principles of the Bologna Declaration (Bologna Process) education model, and it applies the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS).

Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS) is a public, deemed, research university for higher education and research in basic sciences under the Department of Science & Technology, Government of India. Established on 29 July 1876 by Mahendralal Sarkar, a private medical practitioner, it focuses on fundamental research in basic sciences. It is India's oldest research institute located at Jadavpur, South Kolkata near Jadavpur University, Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute and Indian Institute of Chemical Biology. It is spread over a limited area of 9.5 acres and currently in the process of building an advanced SMART campus at Baruipur.

title: Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso
text:
Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso
The Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso (Spanish: Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso) (PUCV), also known as Universidad Católica de Valparaíso (UCV), is one of six Catholic universities in Chile and one of the two pontifical universities in the country, along with the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile. Founded in 1928, it is located in Valparaíso Region and has about 18,000 students. It is recognized in Chile as an institution with high academic prestige and as a research university due to its acquired research funds and offered postgraduate degrees in the fields of science, engineering, humanities and arts. As a Catholic university, it answers directly to the Holy See and the Bishopric of Valparaíso.

title: Indira Gandhi National Open University

Indira Gandhi National Open University
Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) is a central open and distance learning university located in Delhi, India. Named after the former prime minister of India, Indira Gandhi, the university was established in 1985 with a budget of ₹20 million, after the Parliament of India passed the Indira Gandhi National Open University Act, 1985 (IGNOU Act 1985). IGNOU, operated by the Government of India is the world's largest university, with enrollment of over 3,000,000 students. It provides 333 academic programs through its 21 Schools of Studies, supported by a network of 67 Regional Centres and 2,257 Learner Support Centres (LSCs).

National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur (NIT Jamshedpur or NITJSR) is an Institute of National Importance for Technical Education located at Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India. Established as a Regional Institute of Technology on 15 August  1960, it was upgraded to National Institute of Technology (NIT) on 27 December 2002 with the status of a Deemed University. It is one of the 31 NITs in India, and as such is directly under the control of the Ministry of Education (MHRD). It is the third in the chain of 8 NITs established as a part of the Second Five Year Plan (1956–61) by the Government of India.

title: Asian Development Bank Institute

Asian Development Bank Institute
The Asian Development Bank Institute (ADBI) is an Asian think tank focused on identifying effective development strategies for Asia and the Pacific, and on providing support to ADB member countries in managing development challenges. It was established in Tokyo in 1996 as a subsidiary of Asian Development Bank, with initial and subsequent financing from the Government of Japan. ADBI is located on the 8th floor of the Kasumigaseki Building in Kasumigaseki, Chiyoda, Tokyo. ADBI was ranked 1st in the world among government-affiliated think tanks in the 2020 Global Go To Think Tanks Index Report by the Think Tanks and Civil Societies Program of the University of Pennsylvania.

title: Republic Polytechnic
text:
Republic Polytechnic
Republic Polytechnic (RP) is a post-secondary education institution and statutory board under the purview of the Ministry of Education in Woodlands, Singapore. Established in 2002, RP is renowned for its sports science programs. It is also the first and only polytechnic in Singapore to use the problem-based learning (PBL) pedagogy for all of its programs. Under the problem-based learning (PBL) pedagogy, RP students will typically receive a problem statement from their lecturers at the start of each day before exploring the solutions to the problem in a group of three to five, and presenting the final solution to the class—where students will receive feedback from their lecturers and classmates.

title: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
text:
Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve is a United States national park and preserve in south central Alaska. The park, the largest in the United States, covers the Wrangell Mountains and a large portion of the Saint Elias Mountains, which include most of the highest peaks in the United States and Canada, yet are within 10 miles (16 km) of tidewater, one of the highest reliefs in the world. The park's high point is Mount Saint Elias at 18,008 feet (5,489 m), the second tallest mountain in both the United States and Canada. The park has been shaped by the competing forces of volcanism and glaciation, with its tall mountains uplifted by plate tectonics.

Open University of Sri Lanka
The Open University of Sri Lanka (OUSL; Sinhala: ශ්‍රී ලංකා විවෘත විශ්වවිද්‍යාලය, Tamil: இலங்கை திறந்த பல்கலைக்கழகம்) is a national university in Sri Lanka. It is unique within the Sri Lankan national university system for being the only university to offer programs of study leading to certificate, diploma, degrees and postgraduate degrees up to PhD level through the Open and Distance Mode of Learning (ODL). The degrees awarded by the university are treated as equivalent to degrees awarded by any other Sri Lankan University under the preview of the University Grants Commission. The OUSL Main Campus and Colombo regional centre (C010) is located in Colombo in Nawala, Nugegoda.

title: University of Iowa Children's Hospital

University of Iowa Children's Hospital
University of Iowa Stead Family Children's Hospital, formerly University of Iowa Children's Hospital and Children's Hospital of Iowa, is a pediatric acute care academic children's hospital located in Iowa City, Iowa, United States. The hospital was founded in 1919 and its current facility, opened in 2017, overlooks the university's football home, Kinnick Stadium. The hospital has 190 inpatient pediatric beds and is affiliated with the University of Iowa Carver College of Medicine. The hospital provides comprehensive pediatric specialties and subspecialties to pediatric patients aged 0–21 throughout Iowa and is one of the only children's hospitals in the region and state.

STEM-intensive, multi-disciplinary deemed university in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Established in the year 1987 by industrialist Jeppiaar Jesuadimai, it is a Christian minority educational institution with its patron as Saint Anthony. The university is a research institute that specializes in the engineering fields, and has been accredited with Grade "A++" by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) and "Category 1 University" by the University Grants Commission (UGC). Sathyabama's main campus is at Sholinganallur, with the dental college nearby at Sithalapakkam and a secondary satellite campus at Sriperumbudur.

title: Icddr,b

Icddr,b
icddr,b (formerly known as the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh) is an international health research organisation located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It is dedicated to saving lives through research, treatment and addresses some of the most critical health concerns facing the world today, ranging from improving neonatal survival to HIV/AIDS. In collaboration with academic and research institutions worldwide, icddr,b conducts research, training and extension activities, as well as programme-based initiatives, to develop and share knowledge for global lifesaving solutions. icddr,b is one of the leading research institutes of the Global South, releasing, according to the Thomson Reuters Web of Science, 18 percent of the Bangladesh's publications.

title: Weber State University
text:
Weber State University
Weber State University (pronounced  WEE-bər) is a public university in Ogden, Utah, United States. It was founded in 1889 as Weber Stake Academy by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and changed to its current name in 1991. As of fall 2023, the student population was 30,536 students, consisting of 16,020 undergraduate students, 1,002 graduate students and 13,514 concurrent enrollment students, making it the third-largest public university in the state. Weber State University has over 225 degree programs and 7 colleges, including the Dr. Ezekiel R. Dumke College of Health Professions and the College of Engineering, Applied Science & Technology.

title: University of Freiburg
text:
University of Freiburg
The University of Freiburg (colloquially German: Uni Freiburg), officially the Albert Ludwig University of Freiburg (German: Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg), is a public research university located in Freiburg im Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The university was founded in 1457 by the Habsburg dynasty as the second university in Austrian-Habsburg territory after the University of Vienna. Today, Freiburg is the fifth-oldest university in Germany, with a long tradition of teaching the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences and technology and enjoys a high academic reputation both nationally and internationally. The university is made up of 11 faculties and attracts students from across Germany as well as from over 120 other countries.

title: Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus

Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus
Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus (SUTS) is the foreign branch campus of Swinburne University and is located in Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia. Established in 2000, Swinburne Sarawak operates as a partnership between the Sarawak State Government and Swinburne Australia. The initiative behind the Sarawak campus is part of a long-term strategy by Swinburne Australia to "globalise its operations and provide its students with international living, working and learning opportunities". The Swinburne Sarawak campus operates as a full-fledged branch campus, joining three other Swinburne campuses in Melbourne, Australia, and is under the academic control of Swinburne's Higher Education Division in Australia.

University of Milan
The University of Milan (Italian: Università degli Studi di Milano; Latin: Universitas Studiorum Mediolanensis), officially abbreviated as UniMi, or colloquially referred to as La Statale ("the State university"), is a public research university in Milan, Italy. It is one of the largest universities in Europe, with 64,878 students and a permanent teaching and research staff of 2,566 (4,653 including all researchers) as of 2025. The university's main campus spans 930 acres (380 ha) in the suburb of Vestal. It was established by an Act of Parliament in 1985 by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India. The Vice President of India is the Chancellor along with the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry acting as the Chief Rector and the President of India is the Visitor of the university. The university is a collegiate university with its jurisdiction spread over the Union Territory of Puducherry located in Tamil Nadu (Pondicherry and Karaikal), Kerala (Mahé) and Andhra Pradesh (Yanam), and Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

WSB University (Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu w Dąbrowie Górniczej until 15 April 2018) is an academic higher education institution established in 1995. title: California Institute of Technology
text:
California Institute of Technology
The California Institute of Technology (branded as Caltech) is a private research university in Pasadena, California, United States. The university is responsible for many modern scientific advancements and is among a small group of institutes of technology in the United States that are devoted to the instruction of pure and applied sciences. The institution was founded as a preparatory and vocational school by Amos G. Throop in 1891 and began attracting influential scientists such as George Ellery Hale, Arthur Amos Noyes, and Robert Andrews Millikan in the early 20th century. The vocational and preparatory schools were disbanded and spun off in 1910, and the college assumed its present name in 1920.

The Adeleke University is a privately-owned institution located in Ede, a town in Osun State, southwestern Nigeria. It was established by Chief Adedeji Adeleke in the year 2011 through the Springtime Development Foundation (SDF), a philanthropic, non-profit organization established by Chief Adedeji to assist less privileged students in obtaining quality higher education. The State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (STMA; 国家烟草专卖局) is a Chinese central government agency responsible for national tobacco monopoly regulation, under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Chartered in 1984 through the policy of one institution with two names, the two agencies are co-located in the same office and share the same website. China Tobacco enjoys a legal monopoly in the country, accounting for 96% of cigarette sales in the country, and is the world's largest manufacturer of tobacco products by revenue.

title: The Texas Heart Institute

The Texas Heart Institute
The Texas Heart Institute, founded by Denton Cooley in 1962, is a nonprofit organization dedicated to reducing the devastating toll of cardiovascular disease through innovative and progressive programs in research, education and improved patient care. The Institute is located within the Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center at the Texas Medical Center in Houston, Texas. In 2024, in its annual survey of “America's Best Hospitals,” U.S. News & World Report ranked the Texas Heart Institute at  Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center number 19 in the United States for heart care. title: Southern Nevada Water Authority

Southern Nevada Water Authority
The Southern Nevada Water Authority (SNWA) is a government agency that was founded in 1991 to manage Southern Nevada's water needs on a regional basis in Clark County. SNWA provides wholesale water treatment and delivery for the greater Las Vegas Valley and is responsible for acquiring and managing long-term water resources for Southern Nevada. From its inception, the SNWA has worked to acquire additional water resources, manage existing and future water resources, construct and operate regional water facilities and promote water conservation. The SNWA is governed by a seven-member board of directors, which comprises one elected official from each governing board of the SNWA's seven member agencies.

title: Rutgers University
text:
Rutgers University
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, commonly referred to as Rutgers University or simply Rutgers ( RUT-gərz), is a large public land-grant research university consisting of three campuses in New Jersey. Chartered in 1766, Rutgers was originally called Queen's College and was affiliated with the Dutch Reformed Church. It is the eighth-oldest college in the United States, the second-oldest in New Jersey (after Princeton University), and one of nine colonial colleges that were chartered before the American Revolution. In 1825, Queen's College was renamed Rutgers College in honor of Colonel Henry Rutgers, whose substantial gift to the school had stabilized its finances during a period of uncertainty.

title: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
The Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT; German: Karlsruher Institut für Technologie) is both a German public research university in Karlsruhe, Baden-Württemberg, and a research center of the Helmholtz Association. KIT was created in 2009 when the University of Karlsruhe (TH) (German: Universität Karlsruhe (TH)), founded in 1825 as a public research university and also known as the "Fridericiana", merged with the Karlsruhe Research Center (Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe), which had originally been established in 1956 as a national nuclear research center (Kernforschungszentrum Karlsruhe, or KfK). By combining academic education with large-scale non-university research, KIT integrates research, teaching, and innovation in a single institutional structure that is unique within the German research landscape.

National University of Jujuy
The National University of Jujuy (Spanish: Universidad Nacional de Jujuy, UNJU) is an Argentine national university, situated in the city of San Salvador de Jujuy, capital of Jujuy Province. Its precursor, the Instituto Superior de Ciencias Económicas (Economic Sciences Institute), was established by Governor Horacio Guzmán in 1959. Redesignated the Provincial University of Jujuy in 1972, a program of decentralization of the country's national university system, as outlined by presidential adviser Dr. Alberto Taquini, resulted in the school's formal establishment as such on November 11, 1973. The university maintains sixteen schools and five institutes, the latter of which are specialized in mining, geology, and zoology.

title: Budapest University of Technology and Economics
text:
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
The Budapest University of Technology and Economics (Hungarian: Budapesti Műszaki és Gazdaságtudományi Egyetem, shortened to Műegyetem), official abbreviation BME, is a public research university located in Budapest, Hungary. It is the most significant university of technology in the country and is considered the world's oldest institute of technology with university rank and structure, founded in 1782. More than 110 departments and institutes operate within eight faculties. The University employs about 1100 lecturers, 400 researchers and other degree holders as well as numerous invited lecturers and practising specialists, including 34 members of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. The university issues about 70% of Hungary's engineering degrees. Training courses are provided in Hungarian, English, German, French and Russian. The university moved to its current site near Gellért square in 1910. The first women students enrolled in 1925. Its official name changed to Budapest University of Technology and Economics in 2000. The university's steering body is the Senate.

title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Political Self-Advocacy Instrument for nursing (PSAI‑N) as an Evidence‑Based Practice Tool
text:
Psychometric Evaluation of the Political Self-Advocacy Instrument for nursing (PSAI‑N) as an Evidence‑Based Practice Tool
The first listed author of “Psychometric Evaluation of the Political Self-Advocacy Instrument for nursing (PSAI‑N) as an Evidence‑Based Practice Tool”, Hetal Desai, is affiliated with William Paterson University. The work was published on March 26, 2026 in Journal of Comprehensive Nursing Research and Care. Psychometric evaluation examines the reliability and validity of instruments used to measure constructs that cannot be observed directly. Internal consistency concerns the relationships among items intended to measure the same construct. Construct validity concerns whether an instrument's scores support the interpretation of the construct it is designed to measure. In nursing, evidence-based practice integrates research evidence with clinical expertise and patients' preferences and values.

title: Ruppin Academic Center
text:
Ruppin Academic Center
Ruppin Academic Center (Hebrew: הַמֶרְכָּז הַאָקָדֶמִי רוּפִּין), also known as Ruppin College, is a college in Israel, which has the status of an institutional settlement. It was established in 1949, is named after Arthur Ruppin, and is located near the moshav Kfar Monash, and within the Hefer Valley Regional Council area. In 2015, it had 4,500 students, whilst the village had a population of 294 in 2024. It was originally called "Midreshet Ruppin" and the "Ruppert School". It was established to provide management education in agriculture, the kibbutz, and the moshav. In 2001, it became a public school. It has four schools covering economics and business administration, social and communal sciences, engineering, and marine sciences. It has 15 academic departments. It awards bachelor's and master's degrees. Its School of Marine Sciences was founded in 1997 and was originally known as the Marine College of Israel.

In “ARIMA-based prediction of global trends in Trichostrongylus infection among humans, ovines, and bovines”, published on January 2, 2026, W. Wei is the first listed author. The institutional affiliation given for W. Wei is Inner Mongolia Agricultural University. The article appeared in the Journal of Helminthology. A systematic review identified 240 eligible studies with annual prevalence data across 60 countries. Following Kalman smoothing, annual prevalence time series covered 1947–2024 for humans, 1966–2024 for ovines, and 1962–2024 for bovines. The fitted models were ARIMA(0,1,1) for humans, ARIMA(3,0,0) for ovines, and ARIMA(0,1,1) for bovines. Forecast 95% confidence intervals were reported to convey uncertainty in the projected trends.

title: Synthesis of glycosyl chlorides and fluorides via a mild chlorination strategy
text:
Synthesis of glycosyl chlorides and fluorides via a mild chlorination strategy
On January 28, 2026, Carbohydrate research published the article “Synthesis of glycosyl chlorides and fluorides via a mild chlorination strategy” online. The PubMed author list begins with Dey S. Glycosyl halides are carbohydrate derivatives in which a halogen atom is bonded to the anomeric carbon. The anomeric carbon is the carbonyl-derived carbon that becomes a new stereocenter when many monosaccharides cyclize. Glycosyl chlorides can serve as glycosyl donors in reactions that form glycosidic bonds. Glycosyl fluorides contain a carbon–fluorine bond at this position. The configuration at the anomeric center is described using the alpha and beta designations. Glycosylation is a central transformation in the chemical synthesis of oligosaccharides.

In 1922, the Pedagogical Faculty was established. The first graduating class in 1925 included 34 economists and 26 lawyers. In May 1943, the university reopened in Skhodnya, 12 km northwest of Moscow. The university returned to Minsk in the summer of 1944. In 1949, the university was named after Vladimir Lenin to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the Byelorussian SSR. In 1975, the Faculty of Radiophysics and Electronics was split off from the Faculty of Physics.

title: Long-Term Outcomes and Risk Factors for Mortality After Single Ventricle Palliation for Asplenia Syndrome
text:
Long-Term Outcomes and Risk Factors for Mortality After Single Ventricle Palliation for Asplenia Syndrome
On January 30, 2026, Journal of the American Heart Association published the article “Long-Term Outcomes and Risk Factors for Mortality After Single Ventricle Palliation for Asplenia Syndrome” online. The PubMed author list begins with Kobayashi Y. The retrospective review analyzed 151 patients with asplenia syndrome who underwent single ventricle palliation between 1990 and 2024. Mortality was the primary end point, and risk factors were assessed using Cox regression over a mean follow-up of 9.3 years. The median age at initial operation was 35 days. Overall, 62 patients (41%) died, while 66 (44%) were alive after Fontan completion. Total anomalous pulmonary vein connection, pulmonary atresia, and at least moderate atrioventricular valve regurgitation were independent risk factors for mortality in the overall cohort.

title: TriHealth
text:
TriHealth
TriHealth, Inc. is a nonprofit integrated health system based in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States. Formed in 1995, the system operates five general acute-care hospitals: Bethesda North, Good Samaritan, Bethesda Butler, McCullough-Hyde Memorial Hospital, and TriHealth Clinton Regional Hospital (formerly Clinton Memorial Hospital). In addition to its inpatient hospitals, TriHealth operates two regional freestanding emergency departments—Bethesda Arrow Springs in Lebanon and Good Samaritan Western Ridge in Green Township—along with ambulatory outpatient centers and primary care practices throughout Southwest Ohio. The organization is one of the largest employers in greater Cincinnati, with approximately 13,000 workers. TriHealth was established through an operating partnership between the sponsors of Bethesda Hospital and Good Samaritan Hospital. In November 2012, TriHealth acquired the Butler County Medical Center in Hamilton, Ohio, reopening it as Bethesda Butler Hospital. In 2015, TriHealth finalized an affiliation agreement with McCullough-Hyde Memorial Hospital that retained a local community board of directors. In January 2020, TriHealth initiated an $85 million expansion and modernization project at Bethesda North Hospital in Montgomery, Ohio. In February 2023, TriHealth announced a multi-year, $250 million master facility plan to modernize and expand Good Samaritan Hospital. The plan included construction of a new five-story, 168,000-square-foot clinical services building.

Sheffield, has Binghamton University as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. The article appeared in Paleobiology, published by Cambridge University Press. Its coauthors are Maggie R. Limbeck, Jennifer E. Bauer, April M. Wright, and Peter J. Wagner. The study examines divergence time estimations and character rate evolution in Diploporita, Eublastoidea, and Paracrinoidea. It uses reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo and fossilized birth–death models to investigate evolutionary rates through anatomical subunit partitioning. Results suggest similar rates among the three groups, although Paracrinoidea shows elevated rates in several anatomical subunits. Linked clock models had more support than unlinked clock models.

title: Kaniv Nature Reserve
text:
Kaniv Nature Reserve
The Kaniv Nature Reserve (Ukrainian: Канівський природний заповідник) is a protected nature reserve of Ukraine that covers a portion of the right bank of the Dnieper River, and two floodplain islands in the river itself. The reserve is in the center of Ukraine, along the northeast edge of the Dnieper Upland. It was created to protect valuable forest-steppe and floodplain habitat. The site is known for an abundance of archaeological sites left by cultures back to the Paleolithic. The reserve is a unit of the Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, and is located in Cherkasy Oblast. The reserve was originally founded in 1923 as the National Forest Steppe Reserve. A protective zone of 1,353 hectares surrounds the reserve's borders. The reserve straddles the transition zone between the Central European mixed forests and East European forest steppe ecoregions. Forests cover 85% of the reserve. Elm and oak are the most common trees. A total of 233 bird species have been recorded at the site. The reserve's Museum of Nature is open to the public. Reserve staff offer guided tours on three ecological routes that are open only in the warm months.

title: MrBZIP, a MrWETA-interacting transcription factor, mediates oxidative and heat stress tolerance in conidia of Metarhizium robertsii
text:

“MrBZIP, a MrWETA-interacting transcription factor, mediates oxidative and heat stress tolerance in conidia of Metarhizium robertsii” was published electronically in Journal of invertebrate pathology on January 29, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Wu H. The researchers used a yeast two-hybrid system to screen for potential MrWETA-interacting proteins in M. robertsii. Sequencing analysis identified MrBZIP as a Basic-leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factor and a potential MrWETA partner. Transcriptomic analysis showed that deletion of Mrbzip altered the expression of 198 genes, mostly associated with cellular component and metabolic pathways in GO and KEGG analyses, respectively. Loss of Mrbzip did not significantly affect conidiation, conidial germination, or virulence.

The Islamic University in Uganda (IUIU) is a multi-campus university offering courses at certificate, diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The main campus of the university is in Mbale, about 222 kilometres (138 mi) north-east of Kampala, Uganda's capital and largest city. The idea to establish IUIU was conceived at the second summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in 1974. The university was inaugurated in February 1988 with 80 students. Its main objective is to serve the higher education needs of the English-speaking Muslim community in Southern and Eastern Africa. The university also enrolls non-Muslim students, who are free to practice their different religions. As of December 2014, IUIU had four campuses. The Females' Campus is in Kabojja, 8 kilometres (5 mi) west of Kampala's central business district. This campus admits only female students.

title: Effectiveness, safety, and biomarker analysis of sacituzumab govitecan in Chinese metastatic breast cancer: a multicenter real-world study
text:
Effectiveness, safety, and biomarker analysis of sacituzumab govitecan in Chinese metastatic breast cancer: a multicenter real-world study
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Effectiveness, safety, and biomarker analysis of sacituzumab govitecan in Chinese metastatic breast cancer: a multicenter real-world study” in Therapeutic advances in medical oncology to March 25, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Li M. The study included 165 metastatic breast cancer patients treated with sacituzumab govitecan between June 2023 and December 2024 at four institutions in China. Demographic and clinical data were collected and analyzed retrospectively. Sacituzumab govitecan was administered intravenously at 10 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day treatment cycle. Among 103 patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, median real-world progression-free survival was 5.1 months and median real-world overall survival was 19.7 months. Among 62 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease, median real-world progression-free survival was 5.8 months. No new safety signal was observed in the study.

The reported path coefficient is 0.975. The R-square value is 0.95, indicating that SIAKANG explains 95% of the variation in satisfaction.

title: Transcriptional and functional dissection of cytochrome P450 and ABC transporters underlying tobacco tolerance in Lasioderma serricorne
text:
Transcriptional and functional dissection of cytochrome P450 and ABC transporters underlying tobacco tolerance in Lasioderma serricorne
The article “Transcriptional and functional dissection of cytochrome P450 and ABC transporters underlying tobacco tolerance in Lasioderma serricorne” appeared online in Journal of insect physiology on March 28, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Zafar J. The study compared the transcriptomes of Lasioderma serricorne larvae reared on tobacco and an artificial diet. Tobacco-fed larvae showed significant upregulation of genes involved in metabolic detoxification, including 92 cytochrome P450s, 74 ATP-binding cassette transporters, 37 glutathione S-transferases, 30 UDP-glycosyltransferases and 21 carboxylesterases. Spatiotemporal profiling identified several ABC transporters and cytochrome P450s as enriched in the midgut. RNAi-mediated knockdown of LsCYP6TC1 reduced transcript abundance and decreased larval survival to 36.1% compared with controls. Co-silencing of LsABCA1 and LsABCG1 significantly reduced larval survival to 77.1%.

title: Fujian University of Technology
text:
Fujian University of Technology
Fujian University of Technology (Chinese: 福建理工大学) is a public university located in Fuzhou, Fujian, China. The Chinese Ministry of Education established the university in 2002 as a merger of the Fujian College of Architecture and Civil Engineering and the Fujian Institute of Technology. The predecessor of both institutions was the noted "Fujian Gaogong" (Fujian Advanced Technological School) originating from "Canxia Jingshe" (Canxia Elementary Technological School), which was co-founded in 1896 by Lin Shu, an eminent Fujian scholar and translator and Chen Baochen, tutor of the last Chinese emperor Puyi during the Qing dynasty. The university abbreviation is FJUT. The university has three campuses, known as Shanxi Campus, Cangshan Campus and Pudong Campus. Its campuses occupy a total area of 40.5 hectares (607 mu). The university has 47 laboratories. Its teaching equipment has a total value of 71,420,000 yuan. FJUT consists of 13 departments, two teaching divisions, a school for adults' further education and vocational education, and a software professionals training base. The two teaching divisions are the Political Science Division and the Physical Education Division.

title: The ASKAP-FLASH survey: A first look at the multiwavelength properties and redshift distribution of compact radio sources
text:
The ASKAP-FLASH survey: A first look at the multiwavelength properties and redshift distribution of compact radio sources
William Roster is the first author listed for “The ASKAP-FLASH survey: A first look at the multiwavelength properties and redshift distribution of compact radio sources” (2026), with Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics as the institution named for that author. The publication appeared in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia on April 24, 2026. The study characterises optical counterparts to more than 45,000 bright compact radio sources identified across FLASH fields observed up to April 2025. Photometric redshifts are estimated for FLASH continuum sources cross-matched to the tenth data release of the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys because most candidate absorbers lack spectroscopic redshift measurements. The study also examines sources with optical counterparts in the eROSITA X-ray survey to investigate their active galactic nucleus content, multiwavelength properties, and environments.

title: Prenatal Stress Induces Changes in Behavior, HPA Axis, Inflammation, and Oxidative Stress in Adult Rats Offspring
text:
Prenatal Stress Induces Changes in Behavior, HPA Axis, Inflammation, and Oxidative Stress in Adult Rats Offspring
The article “Prenatal Stress Induces Changes in Behavior, HPA Axis, Inflammation, and Oxidative Stress in Adult Rats Offspring” appeared online in Neurochemical research on February 28, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Aguiar-Geraldo JM. Thirteen pregnant Wistar rats were exposed to chronic unpredictable prenatal stress from gestational day 14 until birth. At postnatal day 60, offspring began seven days of twice-daily intraperitoneal treatment with lithium (47.5 mg/kg) or saline. Behavior was assessed using the open field test to evaluate free movements. Female offspring of stressed dams showed hyperactivity. The offspring's brain and serum showed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, oxidative damage markers, and HPA axis hormone levels. Lithium administration reduced only the biochemical alterations.

title: Implementing a Technology-Integrated Problem-Based Learning (TIPBL) Strategy in a Higher Education Mathematics Classroom
text: Implementing a Technology-Integrated Problem-Based Learning (TIPBL) Strategy in a Higher Education Mathematics Classroom “Implementing a Technology-Integrated Problem-Based Learning (TIPBL) Strategy in a Higher Education Mathematics Classroom ” appeared in International Journal of Education in Mathematics, Science and Technology on March 27, 2026. The record lists Joshua M. Ayade as its second author and Biliran Province State University as that author’s institution. The study examined TIPBL among first-year Bachelor of Secondary Education students majoring in Mathematics at a state university in the Philippines. It used a collaborative action research design with a modified explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach. Qualitative insights came from post-intervention interviews. Results indicated high academic grit and a growth-oriented mathematical mindset. Qualitative themes included concerns about over-reliance on technology and disparities in access.

title: Integration of a Rotary Pressure Exchanger in CO2-Based Refrigeration System: Thermodynamic Modeling and Energy–Environmental Benefits
text:
Integration of a Rotary Pressure Exchanger in CO2-Based Refrigeration System: Thermodynamic Modeling and Energy–Environmental Benefits
In “Integration of a Rotary Pressure Exchanger in CO2-Based Refrigeration System: Thermodynamic Modeling and Energy–Environmental Benefits”, published on February 3, 2026, Ayan Sengupta is the first listed author. The institutional affiliation given for Ayan Sengupta is BITS Pilani. Mani Sankar Dasgupta is also listed as an author. The article appears in the Journal of Energy Resources Technology, Part A: Sustainable and Renewable Energy. The study investigates supermarket refrigeration in warm to hot climates. It develops a thermodynamic model for the pressure exchanger from computational fluid dynamics simulations across ambient temperatures of 13 °C to 40 °C. The proposed system demonstrates annual energy savings of 4.16–6.57% compared with a multi-ejector CO2 system. It achieves a 10.8–24.2% reduction in carbon footprint relative to an R448A system. Gas-cooler pressure, receiver pressure, and rotor speed are identified as key variables affecting pressure exchanger performance. The pressure exchanger can deliver a pressure lift between 3.18 bar and 53 bar.

The Pacific National University (PNU) is a public university in Khabarovsk, Russia, established in 1958. PNU has over 12,000 students in 80 various academic majors. Yuriy S. Marfin, the rector of the Pacific National University The university began as the Khabarovsk Automobile Highway Institute, founded by the USSR Ministry of Higher Education. Azimul Hasan is also listed as an author. The review examines CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and metabolic engineering in microalgae and terrestrial plants for biosensing and bioremediation. It discusses fluorescent or colorimetric reporters for detecting environmental toxins. Examples include microalgal strains with inserted genes for herbicide-degrading enzymes and CRISPR-edited plants with increased heavy metal uptake capacity. The review also addresses biosafety containment, regulatory hurdles, and the need for robust genetic toolkits in non-model species.

title: Disentangling Psychopathology and Social Cognition in 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome with Psychotic Symptoms and Schizophrenia
text:
Disentangling Psychopathology and Social Cognition in 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome with Psychotic Symptoms and Schizophrenia
On April 24, 2026, Schizophrenia bulletin open published the article “Disentangling Psychopathology and Social Cognition in 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome with Psychotic Symptoms and Schizophrenia” online. The PubMed author list begins with Berardelli I. The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome results from the loss of genetic material on the long arm of chromosome 22. Its clinical manifestations can include congenital heart defects, palatal abnormalities, immune deficiency, and learning difficulties. The deletion usually arises spontaneously but can also be inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. People with the syndrome have an elevated risk of developing schizophrenia. Social cognition encompasses mental processes used to perceive and interpret social information, including emotion recognition and understanding other people's mental states. In schizophrenia, difficulties in social cognition can contribute to impaired everyday social functioning.

The second listed author of “Predictors of osteo-articular infection in Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia in a tertiary center between 2017 and 2022”, Diego Castanares Zapatero, is affiliated with UCLouvain. The work was published on January 9, 2026 in Journal of Bone and Joint Infection. The retrospective study was conducted at a single tertiary-care hospital in Brussels, Belgium. Among 489 consecutive patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, 141 (28.8 %) had a concomitant osteo-articular infection. Longer duration of bacteremia and community-acquired bacteremia were associated with osteo-articular infection. Active cancer and intensive care unit admission for bacteremia were associated with a lower likelihood of osteo-articular infection.

title: Advanced Flexible Bioelectrodes for Next-Generation Implantable Triboelectric Nanogenerators
text:

“Advanced Flexible Bioelectrodes for Next-Generation Implantable Triboelectric Nanogenerators” was published electronically in International journal of biomaterials on April 27, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Nirwan VP. The fabrication of novel bioelectrodes using electrospun nanofibers and a prototype for a sustainable triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is explored in this study. Poly(lactic acid-caprolactone) (PLCL) was electrospun as the matrix of the bioelectrode and functionalized with a commercial graphene XT3. Afterward, the fibers were coated with graphene ink (Gr.ink) or poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS). PEDOT:PSS-coated fibers showed the highest Young's modulus at 98 MPa. A TENG device was assembled using PEDOT:PSS-covered PLCL/graphene fiber mats as electrodes and poly(lactic acid) with poly(glycerol sebacate) as active contact layers.

The optical fingerprinting platform uses two cadmium-free CIS/ZnS quantum dot formulations deposited side-by-side. Under multiwavelength excitation, each formulation exhibits dual-peak emission, producing a combined four-peak spectral profile. Wavelength, full width at half-maximum, and intensity are extracted from each peak across nine excitation wavelengths to obtain 108 independent spectral features. These features are converted into a 216-bit binary fingerprint. Statistical analysis found a mean inter-Hamming distance of 0.512 ± 0.028 and a collision margin of 99-123 differing bits.

text:

“Theory of spiral magnetism in Weyl semimetal SmAlSi” was published on March 5, 2026. Its first listed author, Lasin Thaivalappil, has National Sun Yat-sen University as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. SmAlSi is an intermetallic compound containing samarium, aluminium, and silicon. It crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric tetragonal structure. Weyl semimetals contain isolated band crossings called Weyl nodes in their electronic band structures. Each Weyl node carries a topological charge associated with its chirality. Spiral magnetic order describes a spatial arrangement in which the directions of magnetic moments rotate periodically through a crystal. Samarium belongs to the lanthanide series, whose magnetism commonly involves electrons in partially filled 4f shells. The Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction is an antisymmetric exchange interaction that can favor noncollinear arrangements of magnetic moments in systems with suitable broken inversion symmetry.

title: Low-load blood flow restriction with elastic bands elicits superior gains in sprint and jump performance compared to heavy-load training in In-season collegiate basketball players
text:
Low-load blood flow restriction with elastic bands elicits superior gains in sprint and jump performance compared to heavy-load training in In-season collegiate basketball players
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Low-load blood flow restriction with elastic bands elicits superior gains in sprint and jump performance compared to heavy-load training in In-season collegiate basketball players” in Journal of sports sciences to March 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with He T. The study involved 18 Division I basketball players during a competitive season. Participants performed back squats twice weekly for eight weeks at approximately 30% of one-repetition maximum in the blood flow restriction group or approximately 75% in the heavy-load group. Both groups achieved similar one-repetition maximum strength gains. Blood flow restriction adaptations occurred with a 3.6-fold lower mechanical training load. Covariate analysis confirmed that the results were independent of playing time.

text:

The study was conducted from April 2024 to April 2025 in six randomly selected government and private orphanage homes in Lucknow. It included 114 children aged 11–18 years. Data were collected using a pretested questionnaire. Nutritional status was assessed using WHO BMI-for-age standards. School dropout was reported by 58.8% of children. Normal nutritional status was found in 82.5% of participants, while 5.3% were thin and 12.3% were overweight or obese. Pallor was observed in 13.2% of participants. text:
Hydroclimatic Drivers of Groundwater Resilience in Cold Humid Regions
The article “Hydroclimatic Drivers of Groundwater Resilience in Cold Humid Regions” appeared online in Ground water on March 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Blin N. The study investigates a cold humid basin in the Great Lakes Basin with strong groundwater-surface water interactions. It uses the coupled groundwater-surface water model GSFLOW to evaluate groundwater's potential buffering capacity on surface water systems. Results show a strong linear relationship between changes in mean annual precipitation and groundwater recharge. Annual precipitation increases exceeding 165 mm were required to generate positive changes in recharge. Groundwater buffering capacity was particularly significant in areas with shallow water tables and during hydrological recession periods. Spatial analysis indicated greater sensitivity to precipitation changes in areas with deeper water tables.

Active matter research connects statistical physics with biology and materials science.

The PubMed author list begins with Xiong Y. The study integrated multidimensional structural MRI features, including gray matter volume and cortical thickness, using a support vector machine. title: Brno University of Technology
text:
Brno University of Technology
Brno University of Technology (BUT; Czech: Vysoké učení technické v Brně, VUT) is a public technical university in Brno, Czech Republic. Founded on 19 September 1899 as the first Czech university in Moravia, the university comprises 8 faculties and three university institutes and has more than 18,000 students. Its teaching and research are centred on engineering and technology, particularly civil engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science and information technology, alongside architecture, natural sciences, economics and management, fine arts and design. The university initially had four professors and 47 students, who could study only civil engineering. Teaching in mechanical engineering began in 1900. In 1911, the university moved into a new building on Veveří Street, which is still used by the Faculty of Civil Engineering.

title: Sexual and Gender Minorities in Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation (OTDT): A Survey of Canadian OTDT Health Care Workers
text:
Sexual and Gender Minorities in Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation (OTDT): A Survey of Canadian OTDT Health Care Workers
The article “Sexual and Gender Minorities in Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation (OTDT): A Survey of Canadian OTDT Health Care Workers” appeared online in Canadian journal of kidney health and disease on March 27, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Leeies M. The study used a cross-sectional survey of Canadian OTDT health care workers conducted from August to October 2024. Responses from 123 completed surveys were analyzed out of 600 eligible respondents (21%). Respondents were mainly coordinators (61%) and physicians (25%). Most respondents (77%) felt that gender-neutral, behavior-focused donor eligibility assessments would confer low or no risk for donor-derived infections in transplant recipients. Respondents had varied opinions on how HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis should influence donor risk assessments. Only 11% of respondents reported receiving targeted training in cultural humility in the care of 2SLGBTQ+ patients in the organ or tissue donation system.

title: NAD+ subcellular partitioning mediated by miR-183 and miR-96 regulates muscle stem cell differentiation
text:
NAD+ subcellular partitioning mediated by miR-183 and miR-96 regulates muscle stem cell differentiation
On March 31, 2026, Journal of molecular cell biology published the article “NAD+ subcellular partitioning mediated by miR-183 and miR-96 regulates muscle stem cell differentiation” online. The PubMed author list begins with Ma M. The study found that loss of miR-183 and miR-96 impaired skeletal muscle regeneration after injury and triggered premature differentiation of muscle stem cell-derived primary myoblasts. The mechanism involves miRNA-mediated targeting of SLC25A51, a mitochondrial NAD+ transporter that increases mitochondrial NAD+ while reducing cytoplasmic NAD+. The results suggest that reduced cytoplasmic NAD+ diminishes SIRT1-mediated deacetylation, increasing H4K16ac at myogenic gene promoters to promote differentiation. Mitochondrial NAD+ accumulation stimulates the tricarboxylic acid cycle, raising ATP and citrate levels. These metabolites allosterically activate the ACLY pathway, increasing acetyl-CoA production to supply acetyl groups for H4K16ac.

title: Liverpool John Moores University
text:
Liverpool John Moores University
Liverpool John Moores University (abbreviated LJMU) is a public research university in the city of Liverpool, United Kingdom. The university can trace its origins to the Liverpool Mechanics' School of Arts, established in 1823. This later merged to become Liverpool Polytechnic. In 1992, following an Act of Parliament, the Liverpool Polytechnic became what is now Liverpool John Moores University. It is named after Sir John Moores, a local businessman and philanthropist, who donated to the university's precursor institutions. The university had 25,050 students in 2024/25, of which 20,105 are undergraduate students and 4,945 are postgraduate, making it the 30th largest university in the UK by total student population.

title: Impact of post-mortem time and temperature on microbiological safety, structural integrity, and biomaterial properties of human peroneus longus tendons
text:

The PubMed author list begins with Wang S. The study evaluated post-mortem intervals of up to 36 hours against current American Association of Tissue Banks standards. Staining revealed significantly reduced collagen intensity in warm tendons with extended intervals. Cooling preserved collagen content for up to 12 hours beyond the standard.

title: Simulation modeling of neighborhood-level differences in life course health outcomes: a proof of concept
text:
Simulation modeling of neighborhood-level differences in life course health outcomes: a proof of concept
On April 8, 2026, Innovation in aging published the article “Simulation modeling of neighborhood-level differences in life course health outcomes: a proof of concept” online. The PubMed author list begins with Dalton JE. The researchers used electronic health records to construct a probabilistic dynamic systems model simulating each patient's life course in a large primary care population. The model accounted for specific relationships by sex and Area Deprivation Index quintile. It predicted long-term incidence of 10 chronic conditions and all-cause mortality. The model demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration, with a C-statistic of 0.871 for 10-year mortality. A hypothetical initiative reducing the number of smokers by 10% had minimal effect on life expectancy disparities in the general patient population but meaningfully narrowed disparities when focused on high-deprivation neighborhoods.

title: Associations Between Cognitive Risk Scores and Objective Cognition by Sexual Orientation: Evidence From the CLSA
text:
Associations Between Cognitive Risk Scores and Objective Cognition by Sexual Orientation: Evidence From the CLSA
The article “Associations Between Cognitive Risk Scores and Objective Cognition by Sexual Orientation: Evidence From the CLSA” appeared online in Research on aging on January 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Grady A. The study used baseline data from 2011–2015 from the Comprehensive cohort of the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging. It compared 309 lesbian, gay, and bisexual older adults with 16,207 heterosexual older adults. Cognitive risk was assessed using the Australian National University - Alzheimer's Disease Risk Index (ANU-ADRI). Cognitive performance was measured using a composite score based on six cognitive tests. The analytic strategy combined t-tests, chi-square tests, and linear regression models. LGB participants had lower cognitive risk scores than heterosexual participants. LGB participants reported higher rates of depression and smoking and lower social engagement. LGB participants scored significantly higher on cognitive performance than heterosexual participants. This cognitive performance difference remained after controlling for ANU-ADRI score, race, and income.

title: Optimising the use of the rapid response systems
text:
Optimising the use of the rapid response systems
On February 27, 2026, Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses published the article “Optimising the use of the rapid response systems” online. The PubMed author list begins with Jones D. Rapid response systems are hospital safety structures designed to identify and respond to clinical deterioration in patients outside intensive care units. Their activation criteria commonly include abnormalities in respiratory rate, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, or level of consciousness. A medical emergency team is one model of the clinical response component. Early warning scores combine physiological observations to help identify patients at risk of deterioration. These systems also include processes for reviewing events and improving the organisation of care.

text:
Sex as a biological variable in human dental pulp stem cells: An exploratory epigenomic and transcriptomic comparison
The article “Sex as a biological variable in human dental pulp stem cells: An exploratory epigenomic and transcriptomic comparison” appeared online in Regenerative therapy on April 21, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Yamada S. Dental pulp stem cells are mesenchymal stromal cells found in the soft connective tissue inside teeth. They can differentiate into odontoblast-like cells that produce mineralized tissue. Their capacity for self-renewal and differentiation has made them a subject of regenerative dentistry research. Epigenomic studies examine regulatory features such as DNA methylation and chromatin organization without changing the underlying DNA sequence. Transcriptomic studies examine the RNA molecules expressed by cells under particular conditions. Biological sex can influence cellular gene expression through sex chromosomes and hormonal signaling.

Nanjing Normal University (NJNU; Chinese: 南京师范大学; pinyin: Nánjīng Shīfàn Dàxué) is a provincial public university in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. It is affiliated with the Province of Jiangsu, and co-sponsored by the Ministry of Education and the provincial government. The university is part of the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211. As of 2020, NNU has three campuses in Nanjing, namely Xianlin, Suiyuan, and Zijin. It consists of 28 colleges and schools with an enrollment of 18,369 undergraduates and 12,564 graduate students, including 1,525 doctoral candidates. Nanjing Normal University traces its history to the establishment of Sanjiang Normal School in 1902. In 1952, schools and departments of Nanjing University and University of Nanking were merged to establish Nanjing Normal College on the former site of Ginling College. In 1984, Nanjing Normal College was renamed Nanjing Normal University. In 2000, Nanjing Polytechnic of Power Engineering was incorporated into the university.

title: Between the subject and the self
text:
Between the subject and the self
“Between the subject and the self” was published on January 20, 2026. Its last listed author, Antonio-José Silvestre-López, has Universitat Jaume I as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. The article appeared in Review of Cognitive Linguistics. Its publisher is John Benjamins Publishing Company. Charles M. Mueller is the first listed author. The paper analyzes a corpus of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy defusion exercises to identify the patterns of construal they typically evoke. Its findings show frequent use of the Divided-Person metaphor, with the Self and Subject operating within an actual or potential force dynamic configuration. Deliteralization exercises show shifts in the balance of strength between the Subject and Self. Observation exercises contrast a steady-state configuration involving a coerced Agonist with another steady-state pattern in which a potentially coercing force no longer impinges on the Agonist.

text:
Deep profiling of lupus nephritis kidneys reveals dynamic changes in myeloid cells associated with disease progression
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Deep profiling of lupus nephritis kidneys reveals dynamic changes in myeloid cells associated with disease progression” in Annals of the rheumatic diseases to April 28, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Hoover PJ. Lupus nephritis is kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease. Immune complexes can accumulate in renal tissue and trigger complement activation and inflammatory injury. Clinical manifestations include proteinuria, blood in the urine, and impaired kidney function. Kidney biopsy is used to classify the pattern of injury and assess inflammatory activity and chronic damage. Myeloid cells include monocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils, which participate in innate immune responses. Macrophages can contribute both to tissue injury and to the clearance of cellular debris.

title: Alliance Treaty as Wedge Strategy: The Origin of the China-North Korea 1961 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance
text:
Alliance Treaty as Wedge Strategy: The Origin of the China-North Korea 1961 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance
Dated January 22, 2026, “Alliance Treaty as Wedge Strategy: The Origin of the China-North Korea 1961 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance” names Khang X. Vu in the first author position. Boston College is the sole institution recorded for that author. The article appears in the Journal of East Asian Studies. Its publisher is Cambridge University Press. The article develops a triangular theory of alliance formation, arguing that China signed the treaty to drive a wedge between North Korea and the Soviet Union rather than to deter South Korea and the United States. It tests this theory by process tracing events in the China–North Korea–Soviet Union triangle from 1948 to 1961. It also uses a plausibility probe of the China–North Vietnam–Soviet Union triangle from 1954 to 1965. The conclusion discusses implications for the contemporary China–North Korea–Russia bloc and alliance politics in the Asian context.

title: Lower limb muscle herniation in an adolescent
text:

The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Lower limb muscle herniation in an adolescent” in Anales de pediatria to January 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Jiménez García L. Muscle herniation is the protrusion of muscle tissue through a defect in the surrounding fascia. In the lower leg, the tibialis anterior is a commonly affected muscle. Fascial defects may be congenital or acquired following trauma. The resulting bulge can become more prominent during muscle contraction or standing and less apparent at rest. Some muscle hernias are painless, whereas others cause discomfort during exercise. Dynamic ultrasonography can demonstrate muscle protruding through the fascial defect during movement. Management depends on symptoms and may include activity modification and compression garments.

The work was published on February 18, 2026 in Physical Review B. Dual-unitary quantum circuits use local gates that remain unitary under a particular reshuffling of their input and output indices. This property allows their tensor networks to be interpreted as unitary evolution in either the temporal or spatial direction. Such circuits provide analytically tractable models of quantum many-body dynamics. A common construction arranges two-site gates in alternating layers acting on neighboring pairs of sites. Bipartite entanglement in a pure state can be quantified by the von Neumann entropy of a subsystem's reduced density matrix. For a finite subsystem, this entropy cannot exceed the logarithm of its Hilbert-space dimension.

The economist Fred Hirsch developed the concept of positional goods in his 1976 book Social Limits to Growth. title: Readout fidelity enhancement via transient response exclusion in superconducting qubits
text:
Readout fidelity enhancement via transient response exclusion in superconducting qubits
“Readout fidelity enhancement via transient response exclusion in superconducting qubits” appeared in Physical Review A on March 26, 2026. The record lists Wei-En Lin as its first author and National Central University as that author’s institution. Superconducting qubits are commonly measured through their coupling to microwave resonators. In dispersive readout, the qubit state shifts the resonator response, allowing the states to be distinguished through the transmitted or reflected microwave signal. A resonator takes a finite time to respond after a measurement pulse begins, producing a transient before its response approaches steady state. Readout fidelity quantifies how reliably a measurement identifies the prepared qubit state. Measurement errors can arise from amplifier noise, overlap between signal distributions, and qubit relaxation during acquisition.

title: Performance improvement of deorbitalized exchange-correlation functionals
text:
Performance improvement of deorbitalized exchange-correlation functionals
“Performance improvement of deorbitalized exchange-correlation functionals” was published on April 3, 2026. Its last listed author, A. C. Cancio, has Ball State University as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. In density functional theory, the exchange-correlation functional accounts for many-electron effects not represented by the classical electrostatic energy and the noninteracting kinetic energy. Meta-generalized gradient approximations can depend on the orbital kinetic energy density in addition to the electron density and its gradient. Deorbitalization replaces this orbital-dependent ingredient with an approximation expressed through the density and its spatial derivatives. The resulting functional can be evaluated without explicit orbital information for that ingredient. Such approximations connect the development of meta-generalized gradient functionals with research on orbital-free kinetic energy functionals.

College of Staten Island
The College of Staten Island (CSI) is a public college in Staten Island, New York, United States. It is one of the 11 four-year senior colleges within the City University of New York system (CUNY), and one of the two four-year senior colleges within the CUNY system with a program in engineering. Programs in the liberal arts, sciences, engineering, and professional studies lead to PhD degrees, master's degrees, bachelor's and associate degrees. title: A Latent Profile Analysis of Psychological Adaptation Among Caregivers of Children with Strabismus: A Cross-Sectional Study
text:
A Latent Profile Analysis of Psychological Adaptation Among Caregivers of Children with Strabismus: A Cross-Sectional Study
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “A Latent Profile Analysis of Psychological Adaptation Among Caregivers of Children with Strabismus: A Cross-Sectional Study” in Journal of multidisciplinary healthcare to March 24, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Mo Y. The study surveyed 409 caregivers. Latent profile analysis classified caregivers based on depression symptoms, resilience, and social support. The analysis identified three profiles: vulnerable and distressed (36.19%), paradoxically distressed (7.34%), and resilient and adapted (56.47%). Multiple logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with profile membership. Low education was a risk factor for the vulnerable and distressed group. Age below 30 years was a strong risk factor for the paradoxically distressed group. Having two children was a protective factor for the paradoxically distressed group. The children's clinical features showed no significant association with caregivers' psychological adaptation profiles.

title: Does Maternal Smoking Affect the Efficacy of Antenatal Betamethasone in Reducing Respiratory Distress Syndrome? A Secondary Analysis of the Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids (ALPS) Trial
text:
Does Maternal Smoking Affect the Efficacy of Antenatal Betamethasone in Reducing Respiratory Distress Syndrome? A Secondary Analysis of the Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids (ALPS) Trial
In “Does Maternal Smoking Affect the Efficacy of Antenatal Betamethasone in Reducing Respiratory Distress Syndrome? A Secondary Analysis of the Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids (ALPS) Trial”, published on January 11, 2026, Chunfa Jie is the second listed author. The institutional affiliation given for Chunfa Jie is Des Moines University. The article appeared in North American Proceedings in Gynecology and Obstetrics - Supplemental. The analysis included 1,421 participants after seven participants were excluded because of missing neonatal resuscitation data. Participants were assigned two intramuscular injections of 12 mg betamethasone 24 hours apart. Maternal smoking was defined as any cigarette use during pregnancy, with status determined at enrollment and frequency and amount not recorded. The primary respiratory outcome combined respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn, and apnea. The primary composite respiratory outcome occurred in 14.4% of neonates born to smokers and 13.9% of those born to non-smokers.

The research aims to provide an integrative framework for measuring employee well-being in tourism-dependent Small Island States. Its first part reviews literature on employee well-being measurement in the tourism sector. The article presents a multi-level model of sustainable human development in tourism that distinguishes three levels of employee well-being. Its second part draws on the authors’ fieldwork and expertise on well-being measurement in five Small Island States during 2019-2022.

Prairie View A&M University (PVAMU or PV) is a public historically black (HBCU) land-grant university in Prairie View, Texas, United States. title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
text:
Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description

Its second listed author, Valerio Melani, has Università degli Studi di Firenze as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. The article appeared in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma. The publisher is Cambridge University Press. The other listed authors are Andrea Maffei and Gabriele Vezzosi. The article considers several two-variable generalizations of the affine Grassmannian, defined as quotients of the double loop group of a smooth affine algebraic group over an algebraically closed field. It proves that these generalizations are representable by ind-schemes when the group is solvable. For a smooth surface with a flag of subschemes, it gives a geometric interpretation in terms of bundles and trivialisation data on appropriate loci depending on the flag.

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences
Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (Nynorsk: Høgskulen på Vestlandet; Bokmål: Høgskolen på Vestlandet), or HVL, is a Norwegian public institution of higher education, established in January 2017 through the merging of formerly independent colleges across five campuses: Bergen, Førde, Haugesund, Sogndalsfjøra and Stord. Its oldest programs – teacher education in Stord – can be traced to 1839. The total number of students at HVL is about 16000, and there are 1800 academic and administrative staff. Its main campus is in the Kronstad neighborhood of Bergen, Norway. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences provides professional education within health and social sciences, engineering, economic and administrative science, music and teaching.

The school offers graduate and postgraduate training, and is active in research. Following tradition, new Bachelors of Engineering (B.Eng) graduating from Polytechnique Montréal receive an Iron Ring, during the Canadian Ritual of the Calling of an Engineer ceremony. Polytechnique Montréal was founded in 1873 to teach technical drawing and other useful arts. In 1958, it moved to its current location on the Université de Montréal campus. The school's campus is located on the northern face of Mount Royal. Its main building is the highest building on the main campus of the Université de Montréal. A SLOWPOKE-2 reactor was installed at Polytechnique Montréal in 1976. The reactor is used for research, teaching, neutron generation and isotope production.

Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul
The Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul (Portuguese: Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul, UFMS), is a public university located in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul in Brazil. It has, in addition to the main campus in Campo Grande (the State's capital), nine campuses located in the following inland cities: Aquidauana, Chapadão do Sul, Corumbá, Coxim, Naviraí, Nova Andradina, Paranaíba, Ponta Porã and Três Lagoas. title: Helsesykepleieres tilnærminger for å anerkjenne foreldre ved bekymring for barns oppvekstmiljø
text:
Helsesykepleieres tilnærminger for å anerkjenne foreldre ved bekymring for barns oppvekstmiljø
The first listed author of “Helsesykepleieres tilnærminger for å anerkjenne foreldre ved bekymring for barns oppvekstmiljø”, Anette Sola Foss, is affiliated with University of Stavanger. The work was published on January 16, 2026 in Nordisk tidsskrift for helseforskning. Margareth Kristoffersen is also listed as an author. The study aimed to describe how public health nurses acknowledge parents when concerns arise about a child’s upbringing environment. It used a qualitative design with a strategic sample. Eight public health nurses participated in individual interviews. Content analysis identified three themes: clarifying concerns with parents, downplaying concerns to parents, and expressing concerns to parents. The findings describe a relational context characterized by respect, care and solidarity that may support parents’ development of self-understanding. Verbalizing concerns can risk offending parents, but nurses do so when necessary to safeguard the child. Organizational support and leadership can facilitate reflection on acknowledging parents without overlooking the child’s best interests.
