title: Missouri State University
text:
Missouri State University
Missouri State University (MSU or MO State), formerly Southwest Missouri State University, is a public university in Springfield, Missouri, United States. Founded in 1905 as the Fourth District Normal School, it is the state's second-largest university by enrollment, with 23,418 students in the fall semester of 2023. The school also offers associate degree programs at two-year campus in West Plains, Missouri, and a bachelor's degree in business programs at Liaoning Normal University in China. The university operates a fruit research station in Mountain Grove, Missouri, and a Department of Defense and Strategic Studies program in Arlington, Virginia. Classes began on June 11, 1906, with 543 students in an off-campus facility. The school's original primary purpose was to prepare teachers for the public school system. Its first permanent campus building was Academic Hall. The building is now known as Carrington Hall, named after the school's first president, William T. Carrington. Carrington Hall serves as the university's administrative center. In 1995, the state legislature granted the university a statewide mission in public affairs.

title: Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
text:
Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
The Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (Norwegian: Norsk utenrikspolitisk institutt; NUPI) is a Norwegian research institution based in Oslo, Norway. It was established by the Norwegian parliament in 1959. NUPI is funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research. NUPI researchers are independent. Kari Osland became director in 2023 and is the institute's first female director. The institute employs research professors, senior researchers, researchers, and non-academic staff. As of January 2022, its five research groups covered Security and defence; Russia, Asia and International Trade; Peace, Conflict and Development; Global Order and Diplomacy; and Climate and Energy. In 1996, the directorship changed from a permanent appointment to a once-renewable six-year appointment.

title: Gly343 mutation enhances gentiobiose conversion efficiency of GH3 family β-glucosidase from Thermotoga maritima STB25
text:
Gly343 mutation enhances gentiobiose conversion efficiency of GH3 family β-glucosidase from Thermotoga maritima STB25
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Gly343 mutation enhances gentiobiose conversion efficiency of GH3 family β-glucosidase from Thermotoga maritima STB25” in International journal of biological macromolecules to January 28, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Liu X. The study used a rational design strategy for site-directed mutagenesis at the Gly343 residue of β-glucosidase derived from Thermotoga maritima STB25. Molecular docking simulations indicated that Gly343 regulates the microenvironment of the substrate-binding pocket. The G343H mutant achieved a gentiooligosaccharide conversion rate of 30.40%, compared with 18.01% for the wild-type enzyme. Kinetic analysis showed that the mutants had higher catalytic constants and catalytic efficiencies than the wild type. Structural simulations suggested that the mutations favor transglycosylation by weakening enzyme–substrate binding affinity.

Isolation, purification and characterization of betulinic acid derivative from the root bark of Afzelia africana and its antiplasmodial and antimicrobial activities
On April 25, 2026, International journal of biochemistry and molecular biology published the article “Isolation, purification and characterization of betulinic acid derivative from the root bark of Afzelia africana and its antiplasmodial and antimicrobial activities” online. The PubMed author list begins with Vigbedor BY. The study's methods included column fractionation and purification, mass spectrometry, and characterization using 1H, 13C, DEPT-135, HSQC, COSY and HMBC. Antimicrobial testing used micro-broth dilution, while antiplasmodial activity was assessed using an MSF assay. Repeated column chromatographic fractionation and TLC profiling yielded a 15 mg white crystal characterized as betulinic acid. The compound showed antiplasmodial activity against the 3D7 strain of P. falciparum, with an IC50 of 12.89 ± 0.52 µg/mL.

title: University of Pardubice

University of Pardubice
University of Pardubice (Czech: Univerzita Pardubice or UPA) is a university in Pardubice, the Czech Republic. In 2021 it had nearly 8,000 students. It is the only university in Pardubice Region. After World War II, chemical factories in the city requested the establishment of a specialised university nearby. The university was founded in 1950 as Vysoká škola chemická (Chemical Institute). It was renamed Vysoká škola chemicko-technologická (Institute of Chemical Technology) in 1954. New faculties have been added since 1990. The institution adopted the name University of Pardubice in 1994. The Faculty of Art Restoration, established in 2005, is in Litomyšl.

title: Maternal Perceptions Regarding the Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Vaccine Following FDA Approval of Abrysvo®
text:
Maternal Perceptions Regarding the Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Vaccine Following FDA Approval of Abrysvo®
Allison M Sweeney is the first author listed for “Maternal Perceptions Regarding the Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Vaccine Following FDA Approval of Abrysvo®” (2026), with Southern Illinois University School of Medicine as the institution named for that author. The publication appeared in North American Proceedings in Gynecology and Obstetrics - Supplemental on January 11, 2026. The study administered a pre-education survey at prenatal visits between 28w0d and 31w6d gestational age. A total of 49 patients completed the pre-education survey. When asked whether they would receive Abrysvo® in pregnancy upon provider recommendation, 60% indicated willingness, 22% were unwilling, and 18% were unsure. At the end of the season, only 19% of the surveilled patients had documented receipt of Abrysvo®. The follow-up survey identified inconvenience in obtaining the vaccine in a timely manner as the primary barrier to vaccination.

title: An antiageing telomere-protective effect of superoxide dismutase-rich Tetraselmis chui in human cells
text:
An antiageing telomere-protective effect of superoxide dismutase-rich Tetraselmis chui in human cells
The article “An antiageing telomere-protective effect of superoxide dismutase-rich Tetraselmis chui in human cells” appeared online in Nutrition and health on March 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Blázquez-Moreno A. The study evaluated a Tetraselmis chui-derived ingredient with high superoxide dismutase activity, termed TSOD, in neonatal human fibroblasts under standard conditions and oxidative conditions induced by H2O2. Three dilutions of a phosphate-buffered saline extract were assessed after four and eight weeks of treatment. Under standard culture conditions, no significant differences in telomere-related variables were observed between control and treated cells after four weeks. Under oxidative stress conditions, TSOD_A and TSOD_C significantly increased median telomere length and the 20th percentile, while reducing critically short telomeres below 3 kbp and the telomere shortening rate.

title: Assessing Core Abilities Across the Mental Health Spectrum: Development and Initial Evaluation of the E-SWAN-G
text:
Assessing Core Abilities Across the Mental Health Spectrum: Development and Initial Evaluation of the E-SWAN-G
The article “Assessing Core Abilities Across the Mental Health Spectrum: Development and Initial Evaluation of the E-SWAN-G” appeared online in Assessment on March 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Cervin M. The study evaluated the Extended Strengths and Weaknesses Assessment of Normal Behavior-General Instrument (E-SWAN-G), designed to capture core strengths and difficulties across the mental health spectrum. A youth version was completed by 603 parents. An adult version was completed by 607 adults. Both versions comprised 60 items each. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported 13 identical first-order factors across the two versions. Internal consistency was mostly good to excellent. Concurrent and incremental validity were supported. Scalar measurement invariance held across the two versions. A brief 32-item version with conserved psychometric properties was developed. The E-SWAN-G is freely available.

title: Etiologies of community-acquired febrile illness identified by TaqMan Array Card qPCR on blood samples: a systematic review and meta-analysis

Cheng, is affiliated with McGill University Health Centre. The work was published on April 8, 2026 in Journal of Clinical Microbiology. The museum is located in the Grund quarter on the eastern bank of the Alzette river, next to the Neumünster Abbey cultural centre. The museum is composed of eight separate scientific sections, spanning the natural sciences: botany, ecology, geology and mineralogy, geophysics and astrophysics, palaeontology, vertebrate zoology, and invertebrate zoology. The museum moved to the Vauban Barracks in Pfaffenthal in 1892. In 1922, it moved to the Old Gendarmerie on the Fishmarket, sharing the site with the National Museum of History and Art. On 11 January 1990, the Chamber of Deputies agreed to restore Saint Jean's Hospice in Grund for the museum. The new site opened in June 1996 across three buildings dedicated respectively to collection displays, teaching classrooms, and research laboratories.

The Structure of Psychopathology on Reddit: Network Analysis of Mental Health Communities in Relation to the ICD Diagnostic System

The PubMed author list begins with Evkoski B. The study examined associations between mental disorders reflected in Reddit user activity and their alignment with ICD diagnostic categories. Researchers manually curated 114 mental health communities from the 20,000 most active subreddits in 2022. The communities were labeled into 49 disorders across 9 ICD diagnostic categories. The article “Adjunctive Muscle Relaxants and Opioid Use Following Total Knee Arthroplasty” appeared online in Journal of pharmacy practice on March 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Grindeland CJ. The retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent elective total knee arthroplasty from July 2012 to July 2020. title: Discrete-time quantum walk of locally interacting walkers
text:
Discrete-time quantum walk of locally interacting walkers

National Tsing Hua University is the sole institution recorded for that author. A discrete-time quantum walk evolves a quantum state through successive applications of a unitary step operator. In the coined formulation, an internal degree of freedom controls the direction of a position shift. Quantum interference distinguishes this evolution from a classical random walk. For multiple walkers, the state space includes the position degrees of freedom of each walker. Local interactions couple walkers when their positions satisfy a specified proximity condition. Such interactions can generate entanglement between walkers that initially occupy a product state.

text:

The PubMed author list begins with Qu F. Bone marrow samples from patients with myeloma bone disease were analyzed to correlate CCL3 levels with bone turnover markers. Human myeloma cell lines IM9 and XG-1 were treated with bortezomib and/or rosuvastatin. Cell viability was assessed using a CCK-8 assay. CCL3 expression was measured by ELISA and Western blot. CCL3 levels were significantly elevated in patients with myeloma bone disease and positively correlated with the severity of bone destruction. The combination treatment enhanced osteoblast activity, suppressed osteoclast formation, and improved survival in the mouse model.

title: Transparent Culture of Network Society: The Relationship Between Technology and Human withing the Framework of Actor-Network Theory
text:

The study combines Actor-Network Theory with Foucauldian discourse analysis and adopts a critical ethnographic approach. It examines transparency as an ideological force embedded in contemporary design, media, and spatial practices. title: Incidence and Survival of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Over Two Decades: A Population-Based Study
text:
Incidence and Survival of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Over Two Decades: A Population-Based Study

The PubMed author list begins with Lorenzen MOB. The nationwide study examined HLH incidence and outcomes in Denmark from 2000 to 2023. Adults aged 18 years or older with HLH and triggering diseases were identified using the Danish National Patient Registry and/or the Danish Pathology Registry. Researchers identified 325 cases. Hematologic malignancies were the triggering diagnosis in 46% of cases, mostly lymphomas (32%). There was no clear improvement in overall survival over time. One-year overall survival was 31% for hematologic malignancy-associated HLH, compared with 75% for idiopathic HLH.

title: Multiscale complexity of two-dimensional Ising systems with short-range, ferromagnetic interactions
text:
Multiscale complexity of two-dimensional Ising systems with short-range, ferromagnetic interactions
Dated February 13, 2026, “Multiscale complexity of two-dimensional Ising systems with short-range, ferromagnetic interactions” names Ibrahim Al-Azki in the first author position. RMIT University is the sole institution recorded for that author. The Ising model represents magnetic moments as discrete spin variables that can take two possible values. Ferromagnetic interactions energetically favor neighboring spins pointing in the same direction. The PubMed author list begins with Nyman JS. The study used male DBA/2 mice with and without streptozotocin-induced hyperglycemia and diets with and without canagliflozin at 50 ppm. Body mass and non-fasting blood glucose were measured weekly until euthanasia at 22 weeks of age. Canagliflozin pretreatment significantly lowered circulating glucose but not to non-diabetic levels. Pretreatment did not affect bone strength or the ability of insulin therapy to improve bone strength. Insulin treatment partially reversed the diabetes-related decline in bound water in the bone matrix.

title: State University of Londrina
text:
State University of Londrina
The State University of Londrina (Portuguese: Universidade Estadual de Londrina, UEL) is a public higher education institution located in the city of Londrina, in the state of Paraná, Brazil. It is one of the largest state universities in Brazil, with students from all over the country. The university was established in 1970 through the merger of existing higher education faculties in Londrina. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programs across the humanities, sciences, health professions, and other fields. Its University Hospital serves as a teaching facility for health sciences students and provides public medical care. The institution also maintains a university library system and supports research and community outreach activities.

title: Modification of Little's law estimates a higher number of needed staff for a veterinary anesthesia service compared to the traditional formula
text:
Modification of Little's law estimates a higher number of needed staff for a veterinary anesthesia service compared to the traditional formula
On February 27, 2026, Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association published the article “Modification of Little's law estimates a higher number of needed staff for a veterinary anesthesia service compared to the traditional formula” online. The PubMed author list begins with Clark-Price SC. The study was conducted between May 7 and August 9, 2024. The health care modification incorporated an efficiency factor of 0.8 and a patient-to-staff ratio of 1:1 for anesthesia. Calculations covered 1 to 25 cases with mean anesthesia durations of 60 to 300 minutes at 30-minute intervals. Anesthesia duration was defined as the time from premedication to extubation. Results were rounded up to the nearest whole number. The formulas' results were compared using a Wilcoxon signed rank test for each duration interval.

title: Supervised, Individualised Exercise Across Pregnancy and Postpartum for Pregnancy-Related Lumbopelvic Pain: A Multicentre Pragmatic, Site-Allocated Cluster Trial

Supervised, Individualised Exercise Across Pregnancy and Postpartum for Pregnancy-Related Lumbopelvic Pain: A Multicentre Pragmatic, Site-Allocated Cluster Trial

The PubMed author list begins with Oishi K. The trial enrolled pregnant women with pregnancy-related low back and pelvic girdle pain at 28 weeks' gestation or later. Participants were allocated by study site to leaflet, exercise, or exercise plus belt groups. All groups received exercise leaflets. The exercise plus belt group additionally received a pelvic belt. Of 127 participants enrolled, 107 completed follow-up. Functional impairment was assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index at 5 days, 1 month, and 3 months postpartum.

title: Gansu Agricultural University

Gansu Agricultural University
Established in 1946, Gansu Agricultural University (GAU) is a non-profit public higher education institution in the city of Lanzhou, Gansu. IIT Kharagpur
The Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur or IIT KGP) is a public institute of technology, research university, and autonomous institute established by the Government of India in Kharagpur, West Bengal. Founded in 1951, the institute is the first of the IITs to be established and is recognized as an Institute of National Importance. The institution was designated an Institute of Eminence by the Government of India in 2019. The institute was initially established to train engineers after India attained independence in 1947. However, over the years, the institute's academic capabilities diversified with offerings in Science, management, law, Agriculture, architecture, humanities, medicine, etc.

title: Alabama State University
text:
Alabama State University
Alabama State University (Alabama State, 'Bama State, or ASU) is a public historically Black university (HBCU) in Montgomery, Alabama, United States. Founded in 1867 during the Reconstruction era, it was one of about 180 "normal schools" established by state governments in the 19th century to train teachers for the rapidly growing public common schools. It was one of 23 established to train African-Americans to teach in segregated schools. ASU is a member-school of the Thurgood Marshall College Fund. Alabama State's athletic teams, known as the Hornets, compete in NCAA Division I as members of the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC). The institution was originally named the Lincoln Normal School of Marion. The university moved from Marion to Montgomery in 1887. It became a full four-year institution in 1928. The State Board of Education approved the name Alabama State University in 1969. Alabama State offers 47 degree programs, including 31 bachelor's, 11 master's, two Education Specialist, and three doctoral programs. The university offers the W.E.B. DuBois Honors Program for undergraduate students who meet above-average performance criteria. Alabama State is accredited by the Commission on Colleges of the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools. In 2025, MacKenzie Scott donated $38 million to ASU.

title: The role of far-red fluorescing chlorophylls in the quenching of LHCII
text:
The role of far-red fluorescing chlorophylls in the quenching of LHCII
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “The role of far-red fluorescing chlorophylls in the quenching of LHCII” in Photosynthesis research to January 29, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Šebelík V. The study compared isolated trimeric LHCII, denoted F680, with aggregated LHCII prepared in a glycerol-rich medium, denoted F730. The researchers used time-resolved fluorescence and ultrafast transient-absorption spectroscopy, including intensity cycling to separate annihilation-free dynamics. The red-emissive chlorophyll states were populated in less than 100 picoseconds and displayed properties consistent with states having a low transition-dipole moment. The findings suggest that far-red-fluorescing chlorophylls are markers of the quenched LHCII configuration rather than direct quenchers.

title: In-vitro Synergistic Inhibitory Effects of Methanolic Leaf Extracts of Newbouldia laevis and Lasianthera africana on Pathogenic Bacteria
text:
In-vitro Synergistic Inhibitory Effects of Methanolic Leaf Extracts of Newbouldia laevis and Lasianthera africana on Pathogenic Bacteria
In “In-vitro Synergistic Inhibitory Effects of Methanolic Leaf Extracts of Newbouldia laevis and Lasianthera africana on Pathogenic Bacteria”, published on February 28, 2026, T.I Mbata is the first listed author. The institutional affiliation given for T.I Mbata is Federal Polytechnic Nekede. The article appeared in AGE Journal of Science. S. Adeyemo is also listed as an author. Antibacterial tests used agar well diffusion and checkerboard techniques. Phytochemical analysis detected alkaloids, flavonoids, tannins, saponins, terpenoids, and phenolic compounds. Ciprofloxacin at 0.5-1.0 µg/mL served as a positive control. Checkerboard tests showed an indifferent response to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with a FICI of 1.20. The tests showed an additive interaction with Salmonella spp., with a FICI of 0.75. For Escherichia coli, the tests showed a synergistic effect, with a FICI of 0.48. Further pharmacological and toxicity studies were recommended.

title: Institute of Space and Astronautical Science
text:
Institute of Space and Astronautical Science
Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (宇宙科学研究所, Uchū Kagaku Kenkyūsho), or ISAS, is a Japanese national research organization of astrophysics using rockets, astronomical satellites and interplanetary probes which played a major role in Japan's space development. Established as part of the University of Tokyo in 1964, the institute spun off from the university to come under direct purview of the Ministry of Education. Since 2003, it is a division of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). ISAS originated within the Institute of Industrial Science at the University of Tokyo, where Hideo Itokawa experimented with miniature solid-fuel rockets in the 1950s. ISAS launched Japan's first interplanetary probes, Sakigake and Suisei, to Halley's Comet in 1985. It also launched Hiten, Japan's first lunar probe, in 1990.

title: University of Haripur

University of Haripur
The University of Haripur (UOH) (Urdu: جامعہ ہری پور) is a public university situated in Haripur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. title: Sensing of metabolic signals via GPR183 promotes occupation of lung macrophage niches by monocytes

Sensing of metabolic signals via GPR183 promotes occupation of lung macrophage niches by monocytes

title: Floquet polaron and molecule in a highly polarized Fermi gas with periodically modulated interactions
text:
Floquet polaron and molecule in a highly polarized Fermi gas with periodically modulated interactions

The study finds that generalized time-periodic Floquet polaron and molecule emerge as quasistationary quasiparticle states. The study further characterizes these impurity states through experimentally measurable spectral functions and radio-frequency spectra.

title: Is lower limb muscle power by vertical jump a sensitive and specific measure for screening sarcopenia compared to handgrip strength and chair stand test?
text:
Is lower limb muscle power by vertical jump a sensitive and specific measure for screening sarcopenia compared to handgrip strength and chair stand test?
“Is lower limb muscle power by vertical jump a sensitive and specific measure for screening sarcopenia compared to handgrip strength and chair stand test?” was published electronically in Brazilian journal of physical therapy on January 29, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Dos Santos LM. The cross-sectional study included 214 older adults without mobility limitations. Participants had a mean age of 70.6 years and an age range of 60–88 years. Women accounted for 84.6% of participants. Sarcopenia was defined using the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP2) algorithm, requiring low muscle strength and mass. Jump height was measured using a mobile app. Jump power was estimated using a validated equation. Sarcopenia prevalence was 4.7%, and probable sarcopenia prevalence was 12.1%. Jump power demonstrated 90% sensitivity, 82.1% specificity, and an area under the curve of 0.9146.

title: Effect of virtual reality (VR) technology on anxiety control and acrophobia reduction: A randomized controlled trial in Iran
text:
Effect of virtual reality (VR) technology on anxiety control and acrophobia reduction: A randomized controlled trial in Iran
The third listed author of “Effect of virtual reality (VR) technology on anxiety control and acrophobia reduction: A randomized controlled trial in Iran”, Seyed Reza Sajadi, is affiliated with Mashhad University of Medical Sciences. The work was published on February 27, 2026 in Cambridge Prisms: Global Mental Health. The trial was conducted in Birjand, Iran, in 2020. It recruited 120 participants, who were randomly allocated to intervention and control groups. The intervention group underwent a single simulated exposure to height using a virtual reality headset. The Beck Anxiety Inventory and a researcher-developed questionnaire were administered as pre-tests to assess acrophobia. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 23, with a significance level of 0.05. Immediately after exposure, anxiety and acrophobia scores were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group. There were no significant differences between groups before exposure or one month later.

Franklin & Marshall College (F&M) is a private liberal arts college in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, United States. Founded in 1787 as Franklin College and later merged with Marshall College in 1853, it is one of the oldest colleges in the United States. F&M is named after Benjamin Franklin, who gave the college its first endowment, and John Marshall. Founded in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, F&M's early years were bilingual, serving the local Pennsylvania Dutch community in German and English. Originally founded as the German College and Charity School, Franklin College received its charter in 1787 from the Pennsylvania General Assembly as a German-language alternative to the University of Pennsylvania.

Chinese Academy of Sciences
The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS; Chinese: 中国科学院) is the national academy for natural sciences and the highest consultancy for science and technology of the People's Republic of China. It is the world's largest research organization, with 106 research institutes, 2 universities, 71,300 full-time employees, and 79,000 graduate students, and ranked first in the 2025 SCImago Institutions Rankings. The Chinese Academy of Sciences has historical origins in the Academia Sinica during the Republican era and was formerly also known by that name until the 1980s. The academy functions as the national scientific think tank and academic governing body, providing advisory and appraisal services on issues stemming from the national economy, social development, and science and technology progress.

title: Tribological Performance of Magnetorheological Fluid in Compliant Contact
text:
Tribological Performance of Magnetorheological Fluid in Compliant Contact
The first listed author of “Tribological Performance of Magnetorheological Fluid in Compliant Contact”, Žáček Jiří, is affiliated with Brno University of Technology. The work was published on February 4, 2026 in Journal of Tribology. The study measured wear loss and the coefficient of friction for six sealing materials flooded by magnetorheological fluid. Polyurethane-based sealing material exhibited the lowest wear. Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) exhibited the lowest coefficient of friction. Polyurethane materials were approximately 3.5 times more resistant to abrasion than nitrile butadiene rubber seals and 2.5 times more resistant than PTFE. Particle concentrations within the tested range of 22–40 vol% did not significantly affect abrasiveness. Magnetorheological fluid subjected to long-term mechanical loading exhibited nearly a threefold increase in abrasiveness compared with new fluid.

National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) is the third largest Institute of the National Institutes of Health, located in Bethesda, Maryland, United States. It is tasked with allocating about $3.6 billion in FY 2020 in tax revenue to advancing the understanding of the following issues: development and progression of disease, diagnosis of disease, treatment of disease, disease prevention, reduction of health care disparities within the American population, and advancing the effectiveness of the US medical system. NHLBI's Director is Gary H. Gibbons (2012–present). The National Heart Institute and the National Advisory Heart Council were established following passage of the National Heart Act in 1948. title: The impact of digital transformation on the business performance of retail enterprises
text:
The impact of digital transformation on the business performance of retail enterprises
“The impact of digital transformation on the business performance of retail enterprises” appeared in Business Performance Review on March 18, 2026. The record lists Loan Thi Thanh Nguyen as its second author and Hanoi University of Industry as that author’s institution. The study examines digital transformation and the financial performance of Vietnamese retail businesses using quantitative methods. It analyzes data from 190 businesses in large cities with high population densities and robust socioeconomic development. Data were collected using Google Forms, arranged in a spreadsheet, cleaned in Excel, and analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences software. The research model includes six independent variables: cloud computing, the Internet of Things, big data, social media, artificial intelligence, and blockchain technology. Regression analysis found that all six variables positively affect business performance. Cloud computing showed the strongest impact, followed by the Internet of Things and social media. Big data analytics and blockchain technology showed relatively moderate effects, while artificial intelligence had the weakest influence.

title: Rates of Self-Reported Skin Cancer in Current and Retired Elite Australian Cricketers
text:
Rates of Self-Reported Skin Cancer in Current and Retired Elite Australian Cricketers
The article “Rates of Self-Reported Skin Cancer in Current and Retired Elite Australian Cricketers” appeared online in The Australasian journal of dermatology on January 29, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Orchard JW. The study invited current and retired members of the Australian Cricketers Association to complete a questionnaire on self-reported skin cancer and associated risk factors. Responses came from 451 participants, representing 29% of the 1530 people invited, and 39% of respondents were female. Very fair- or fair-skinned players and those who lived at lower latitudes as adults reported higher rates of all skin cancers. Females were less likely than males to report basal cell carcinomas. The head, face and neck region accounted for slightly over half of all skin cancer cases.

title: Materiality, Cognition, Agency and Vitality: Inter-relational Exchanges with Non-Human Forms in Vicki Hastrich’s Night fishing
text:
Materiality, Cognition, Agency and Vitality: Inter-relational Exchanges with Non-Human Forms in Vicki Hastrich’s Night fishing

title: National Institute of Technology, Warangal

The institute was renamed as the National Institute of Technology, Warangal in 2002. Classes at the permanent site in Kazipet commenced in January 1963. The bachelor's programme in Chemical Engineering began in 1964. The institute started its MBA programme in 2000. The Innovation Garage is a student-run multidisciplinary workspace for innovation that operates around the clock. Bachelor of Technology admissions for Indian students are based on the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE – Main). MTech students are admitted through the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE).

title: Pressure sintering effect on the uniaxial compressive strength of reconstituted and compacted Antarctic snow
text:
Pressure sintering effect on the uniaxial compressive strength of reconstituted and compacted Antarctic snow
“Pressure sintering effect on the uniaxial compressive strength of reconstituted and compacted Antarctic snow” was published on April 1, 2026. Its first listed author, Enzhao Xiao, has Polar Research Institute of China as the sole institutional affiliation in the publication record. The article appears in the Journal of Glaciology. Its publisher is Cambridge University Press. The study compared pressure sintering under 40 KPa pressure with conventional sintering in experiments on reconstituted and compacted Antarctic snow. The experimental group reached a final density of 0.521 g cm −3, compared with 0.500 g cm −3 in the control group. The experimental group's compressive strength was 0.246 MPa, 86% higher than the control group's 0.132 MPa. Mesoscale analysis showed a 54% increase in the minimum cut density index in the pressure-applied direction. The directional connectivity index improved by 39% along the same axis.

Early maladaptive schemas are enduring patterns of memories, emotions, cognitions, and bodily sensations concerning oneself and relationships with others. Jeffrey Young developed the concept within schema therapy, an integrative psychotherapeutic approach drawing on cognitive and behavioral traditions. Schema theory links these patterns to unmet core emotional needs during childhood and adolescence. In this framework, surrender, avoidance, and overcompensation are broad categories of coping responses to schemas. Systematic reviews use explicit methods to identify, select, and synthesize research addressing a defined question.

Originally, VASP was based on code written by Mike Payne (then at MIT), which was also the basis of CASTEP. It was then brought to the University of Vienna, Austria, in July 1989 by Jürgen Hafner. The main program was written by Jürgen Furthmüller, who joined the group at the Institut für Materialphysik in January 1993, and Georg Kresse. An early version of VASP was called VAMP. Goethe University Frankfurt (German: Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main) is a public research university located in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. It was founded in 1914 as a citizens' university, which means it was founded and funded by the wealthy and active liberal citizenry of Frankfurt. The original name in German was Universität Frankfurt am Main (University of Frankfurt am Main). In 1932, the university's name was extended in honour of one of the most famous native sons of Frankfurt, the poet, philosopher and writer/dramatist Johann Wolfgang von Goethe. The university currently has around 48,000 students, distributed across four major campuses within the city.

title: Addressing Teacher Burnout Through Artificial Intelligence-Driven Support Systems: A Qualitative Case Study in A Private Higher Education Institution
text:
Addressing Teacher Burnout Through Artificial Intelligence-Driven Support Systems: A Qualitative Case Study in A Private Higher Education Institution

The publication appeared in QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice on February 28, 2026. The research focused on twelve teaching personnel from Guagua National Colleges. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis framework. Participants reported limited and inconsistent institutional support mechanisms, often relying on informal coping strategies to manage professional stress. Participants emphasized that these technologies must remain human-centered and guided by ethical governance. The study contributes to an AI-Guarded Teacher Retention Roadmap integrating technological support with institutional and ethical considerations.

title: Particles, trajectories, and diffusion: Random walks in cooling granular gases

Originally called Hochschule der Bundeswehr München, the institution was supposed to offer civilian academic education for military officers. As an uncommon feature amongst German universities, the University of the Bundeswehr Munich unifies a more theoretical research university division and a more practical-oriented College of Applied Sciences branch. Today, the university has an increasing number of civilian and international students. The academic year is organized into trimesters rather than semesters. Very capable students can complete both a bachelor's degree and a master's degree in less than four years. The university is located in Neubiberg in the south of Munich, Bavaria. Its campus formerly hosted the Air Force officer school and included a military airport. Former runways are still used for scientific testing of vehicles. Most students live in individual student dormitories on campus next to the university buildings. Campus sports facilities include gyms, tennis courts and golf ranges.

title: Entropic and kinetic susceptibility equality out of equilibrium
text:
Entropic and kinetic susceptibility equality out of equilibrium
In “Entropic and kinetic susceptibility equality out of equilibrium”, published on April 13, 2026, Takaaki Monnai is the first listed author. The institutional affiliation given for Takaaki Monnai is Seikei University. In statistical physics, susceptibility measures how an observable responds to a perturbation of a system. Linear response theory describes the contribution that is first order in the perturbation strength. At thermal equilibrium, fluctuation-dissipation relations connect response functions with spontaneous fluctuations. Nonequilibrium systems can sustain currents through exchanges of energy or matter with their surroundings. In stochastic descriptions of nonequilibrium response, entropic contributions are associated with entropy flow and time-reversal asymmetry. Kinetic contributions can depend on time-symmetric properties of trajectories, such as the frequency of transitions between states.

Polar Research Institute of China
The Polar Research Institute of China is the main state research institute of the People's Republic of China for the study of Earth's polar regions. The PRIC is an agency within China's Ministry of Natural Resources and conducts polar scientific research, polar observation, and scientific expeditions. It is based in Shanghai, China. The PRIC operates the icebreaking research vessels Xue Long and Xue Long 2. The institute develops polar exploration and observation technologies and equipment. Its research teams focus on areas including polar security and policy research, polar ice and climate change, polar atmosphere, space physics and astronomy. The institute is an active member of the University of the Arctic. The PRIC and the University of Iceland signed an agreement in 2012 to establish the China-Iceland Arctic Observatory. title: Modelling surfactant effects on the onset of spontaneous droplet breakup in both regular and irregular T-junction microchannels
text:
Modelling surfactant effects on the onset of spontaneous droplet breakup in both regular and irregular T-junction microchannels
The first listed author of “Modelling surfactant effects on the onset of spontaneous droplet breakup in both regular and irregular T-junction microchannels”, Jinggang Zhang, is affiliated with Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology. The work was published on January 23, 2026 in Journal of Fluid Mechanics. The study uses a lattice Boltzmann method to investigate breakup in surfactant-free and surfactant-laden droplets. During droplet neck contraction, neck thinning shifts from inertia dominated to interfacial tension dominated, causing spontaneous rapid neck collapse due to Rayleigh–Plateau instability. The critical neck thickness for spontaneous breakup increases with the microchannel height-to-width ratio in both systems. Surfactants decrease the critical neck thickness at a given height-to-width ratio, with their effects becoming stronger as that ratio increases. An irregular microchannel is established by incorporating a constriction section into the upper microchannel wall. Four empirical formulas are proposed to predict critical neck thickness under varying constriction depths and lengths in the two systems.

title: Several kinds of Gaussian quantum channels related to Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering
text:

Taiyuan University of Science and Technology is the sole institution recorded for that author. Gaussian quantum channels are quantum channels that map Gaussian states to Gaussian states. In continuous-variable quantum information, Gaussian states are characterized by their first moments and covariance matrices. Gaussian channels act on these quantities through affine transformations of the first moments and corresponding transformations of the covariance matrix with added noise. Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering concerns the ability of one party's local measurements to prepare conditional states for another party that cannot be explained by a local hidden-state model. Steering can be asymmetric, so its presence may depend on which party performs the measurements. Optical attenuation and amplification provide standard examples of Gaussian quantum channels.

Nara Women's University (奈良女子大学, Nara joshi daigaku) is a national women's university located in Nara, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is one of two national women's universities in the country, the other being Ochanomizu University. The university was originally established in 1908 to train women teachers for ordinary schools. It was reorganized and given its current name in 1949. It was formerly called Nara joshi kōtō shihan gakkō (Nara advanced teachers college for women). As of 2013, its three faculties were Letters, Science, and Human Life and Environment. As of 2013, it offered master's and doctoral courses in Humanities and Sciences. The campus's Memorial Hall, formerly the main hall, is designated an Important Cultural Property. The Main Gate is also designated an Important Cultural Property.

title: Laparoscopic Management of Disseminated Peritoneal Leiomyomatosis in a Patient Without a History of Myomectomy
text:
Laparoscopic Management of Disseminated Peritoneal Leiomyomatosis in a Patient Without a History of Myomectomy
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Laparoscopic Management of Disseminated Peritoneal Leiomyomatosis in a Patient Without a History of Myomectomy” in CRSLS : MIS case reports from SLS to March 27, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with de Nadai Filho N. The report describes a 46-year-old woman who presented with lower abdominal pain and urinary symptoms. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging revealed a lobulated leiomyomatous uterus. During surgery, multiple nodules were unexpectedly identified on the omentum, pelvic peritoneum, and intestinal serosa. Histopathological analysis confirmed leiomyoma without atypia. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged within 24 hours. One-year follow-up MRI demonstrated stable residual nodules with no features suggestive of malignancy.

title: Reliability Analysis of Probabilistic Competing Failure Systems with Both Selective and Global Failure Propagation Effects

Reliability Analysis of Probabilistic Competing Failure Systems with Both Selective and Global Failure Propagation Effects

University of Science and Technology Beijing is the sole institution recorded for that author. The article appeared in the International Journal of Mathematical, Engineering and Management Sciences. The study investigates reliability modeling for systems subject to probabilistic competing failure behaviors and complicated failure propagation effects. Local failure affects only the component itself, whereas propagated failure can have either a system-wide global effect or a selective effect on other components. The paper presents a combinatorial reliability methodology demonstrated through step-by-step analysis of a smart home sensor system. The proposed method is verified through comparison with the Markov method.

title: Bridging Clinical and Entrepreneurial Intelligence: The Dual Acumen Model for Integrating Scientific Expertise and Innovation Strategy in Healthcare Leadership
text:
Bridging Clinical and Entrepreneurial Intelligence: The Dual Acumen Model for Integrating Scientific Expertise and Innovation Strategy in Healthcare Leadership
The article “Bridging Clinical and Entrepreneurial Intelligence: The Dual Acumen Model for Integrating Scientific Expertise and Innovation Strategy in Healthcare Leadership” appeared online in Healthcare management forum on January 30, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Battle C. This qualitative multiple-case study examined how 21 physicians in the United States developed and applied "dual acumen," the integration of scientific expertise and entrepreneurial intelligence to advance healthcare innovation. Guided by effectuation theory, data were analyzed by NVivo 12 for thematic coding. Findings demonstrate how physician entrepreneurs navigated uncertainty through five effectual principles: bird-in-hand, affordable loss, crazy quilt, lemonade, and pilot-in-the-plane. These principles informed the development of the Dual Acumen Model, an empirically derived framework explaining how physicians translate clinical insights into entrepreneurial practice and system-level innovation.

title: Epigenetic maintenance of the injury response state in glioblastoma stem cells
text:
Epigenetic maintenance of the injury response state in glioblastoma stem cells

The PubMed author list begins with Molaei F. The study used a phenotypic genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screen in patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells, based on cell surface expression of the injury response marker CD44. The researchers validated EP300 regulation of the injury response state using CRISPR gene editing and A-458 inhibitor treatment. Perturbation of the histone acetyltransferase EP300 decreased CD44 cell surface expression and disrupted injury response transcriptional state identity through epigenome dysregulation. Loss of this state identity coincided with decreased self-renewal and invasion in glioblastoma stem cells. It also coincided with delayed tumor initiation and progression in a mouse glioblastoma model.

title: Enhanced sensing of a weak Stark field under the influence of Aubry-André-Harper criticality
text:
Enhanced sensing of a weak Stark field under the influence of Aubry-André-Harper criticality

The Aubry–André–Harper model describes particle hopping on a lattice with a quasiperiodically modulated potential. In its standard one-dimensional form, it exhibits a transition between spatially extended and localized states as the modulation strength increases. Its quasiperiodicity arises from an incommensurate ratio between the potential modulation period and the lattice spacing. A uniform static field introduces a potential energy that varies linearly with position along the field direction. Quantum Fisher information quantifies the sensitivity of a quantum state to changes in a parameter. The quantum Cramér–Rao bound relates this information to a lower bound on the variance of an unbiased parameter estimator.

The PubMed author list begins with Wu M. The study analyzed 24,174 participants using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 2009 to 2018. Twenty loci were isolated and characterized from samples collected in shallow coastal waters off Ceará, Brazil. No linkage disequilibrium was detected. Alleles per locus ranged from 3 to 19. Mean observed and expected heterozygosity were 0.655 and 0.790, respectively. Thirteen loci conformed to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Polymorphic information content ranged from 0.478 to 0.919. These microsatellites are useful for exploring fine-scale genetic structure and connectivity among populations.

The study enrolled 266 patients who underwent major orthopedic surgery at four tertiary public hospitals in Jiangsu Province between January and December 2024. Attitudes of Multilingual Individuals toward Stuttering and Cluttering: Evidence from University Foreign Language Majors
The article “Attitudes of Multilingual Individuals toward Stuttering and Cluttering: Evidence from University Foreign Language Majors” appeared online in Folia phoniatrica et logopaedica : official organ of the International Association of Logopedics and Phoniatrics (IALP) on March 31, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with An R. The study included 222 foreign language majors from three northeastern Chinese universities. Each university's cohort was randomly assigned to complete the POSHA-S, POSHA-Cl, or a combined instrument. The questionnaires were validated in Simplified Chinese. Participants generally held less positive and less informed attitudes toward stuttering and cluttering than international averages. Their attitudes were similar to those reported for Chinese university students in general majors but less positive than those of Chinese speech-language pathology students in previous domestic studies. Separate versus combined survey formats had no effect on attitude scores.

The University of Utah (the U, U of U, or simply Utah) is a public research university in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. It was established in 1850 as the University of Deseret  by the General Assembly of the provisional State of Deseret, making it Utah's oldest institution of higher education. The university received its current name in 1892, four years before Utah attained statehood, and moved to its current location in 1900. It is the flagship university of the Utah System of Higher Education. As of fall 2024, there were 28,064 undergraduate students and 8,817 graduate students, for an enrollment total of 36,881, making it the second-largest public university in Utah.

Marco Barbieri and Matteo Rosati are also listed as authors. The work proposes and analyzes a private remote sensing protocol using continuous-variable states in the single-user setting. Only 13.8% of OXA-48-positive episodes received recommended first-line antibiotics. In-hospital mortality reached 56.8%.

The University of Prešov in Prešov (Slovak: Prešovská univerzita v Prešove) is the only public university in the Prešov Self-governing Region of Slovakia. It focuses on the areas of social, natural and theological sciences, sport, arts, management, and health care. It was established by law in December 1996 by splitting the University of Pavol Jozef Šafárik in Košice into the University of Pavol Jozef Šafárik in Košice and University of Prešov in Prešov. It was officially established on 1 January 1997. The outcomes of its active education and research programmes stretch significantly beyond the borders of Eastern Slovakia. Among its organizational units are three centres of excellence: Centre of Excellence in Lingual-Cultural Translation and Interpretation Centre of Excellence in Socio-Historical and Cultural-Historical Research Centre of Excellence in Animal and Human Ecology Through bilateral agreements, the university cooperates with 75 higher education institutions from more than 20 countries, while Prešov students and teachers can spend time at one of more than 300 universities across Europe under the framework of the Erasmus programme.

title: GESIS – Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences
text:
GESIS – Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences
The GESIS – Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences is the largest German infrastructure institute for the social sciences. It is headquartered in Mannheim, with a location in Cologne. With basic research-based services and consulting covering all levels of the scientific process, GESIS supports researchers in the social sciences. As of 2017, the president of GESIS is Christof Wolf. GESIS is part of the Leibniz Association and receives federal and state funding. GESIS was established in 1986 as German Social Science Infrastructure Services (Gesellschaft Sozialwissenschaftlicher Infrastruktureinrichtungen). It originally consisted of three independent institutes: the Social Science Information Centre in Bonn, the Central Archive for Empirical Social Research in Cologne, and the Centre for Survey Research and Methodology in Mannheim. The three institutes merged into one in 2007. In November 2008, GESIS added "Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences" to its name. In November 2011, its Bonn and Cologne locations were merged into one location in Cologne.

title: Decoding selective attention in cochlear implant users with ipsilateral residual hearing
text:
Decoding selective attention in cochlear implant users with ipsilateral residual hearing
The PubMed citation dates the online publication of “Decoding selective attention in cochlear implant users with ipsilateral residual hearing” in Hearing research to February 24, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Dolhopiatenko H. The study compared behavioral speech understanding, cortical auditory evoked potentials, and selective attention decoding under electric, acoustic, and combined electric-acoustic stimulation. Seven subjects participated in the study. The speech material consisted of target HSM sentences with a competing talker of opposite gender. Selective attention was measured through EEG using monaural presentation of two concurrent speech streams. Supra-additive electric-acoustic integration during the behavioral speech understanding task was observed in six of the seven participants. Integration efficiency significantly correlated with the amount of residual hearing. No significant effect of listening condition on N1 latency or N1P2 amplitude was observed.

title: Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide PCI

Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide PCI
“Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide PCI” was published electronically in The New England journal of medicine on March 29, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Fearon WF. The study was an international noninferiority trial comparing physiological assessment derived from angiographic images (FFRangio) with pressure-wire-based measurements in patients with at least one intermediate coronary stenosis. The primary end point combined death, myocardial infarction, or unplanned, clinically indicated coronary revascularization at 1 year. The noninferiority margin was 3.5 percentage points. The PubMed author list begins with Wode K. MISTRAL was an investigator-initiated, phase III, parallel-group, superiority, multicenter clinical trial with a nested biomarker study. At nine oncology centers, 290 participants were randomized to standard treatment plus subcutaneous mistletoe extract or placebo. Standard treatment consisted of palliative chemotherapy or best supportive care. Main inclusion criteria were advanced pancreatic cancer and performance status 0–2, while neuroendocrine pancreatic tumor was a main exclusion criterion. The New Hampshire Institute of Politics was founded in 2001. There are 60 buildings on the campus, which spans over 450 acres.

title: Dirac bilinears in condensed matter physics: Relativistic correction for observables and conjugate electromagnetic fields
text:

The institutional affiliation given for Hiroaki Ikeda is Ritsumeikan University. Dirac bilinears are expressions formed from a Dirac spinor, its Dirac adjoint, and a matrix acting on the spinor components. The sixteen independent matrices in the Dirac algebra can be grouped into scalar, pseudoscalar, vector, axial-vector, and antisymmetric tensor sectors according to their Lorentz transformation properties. The Dirac adjoint is defined by multiplying the Hermitian conjugate of the spinor by the time-like gamma matrix. The Foldy–Wouthuysen transformation is a standard method for obtaining nonrelativistic expansions of the Dirac Hamiltonian and associated observables.

Examining the relationship between speech rhythm, fluency measures and comprehensibility ratings in L2 English speech

The work was published on February 17, 2026 in Journal of Second Language Pronunciation. Joan C. Mora and Mireia Ortega are also listed as authors. The study involved eighty-two advanced Spanish–Catalan bilingual learners of English who completed a spontaneous speaking task. title: Sex Differences in Mathematics and Reading Across Italy: The Role of Socioeconomic Factors
text:
Sex Differences in Mathematics and Reading Across Italy: The Role of Socioeconomic Factors
The second listed author of “Sex Differences in Mathematics and Reading Across Italy: The Role of Socioeconomic Factors”, Enrico Toffalini, is affiliated with University of Padua. The work was published on February 4, 2026 in Intelligence & Cognitive Abilities. The meta-analysis examined over 26 million observations from Italy’s INVALSI surveys conducted between 2009 and 2023. It included students in second, fifth, eighth, tenth, and thirteenth grade across Italy. Preliminary analyses found that boys outperformed girls in mathematics, with d = .25. Girls outperformed boys in reading, with d = -.29. Meta-regression models identified the geographical gradient, employment rate ratio, university enrollment ratio, and mean achievement score as key moderators. In mathematics, higher women’s university enrollment was associated with smaller sex differences. In reading, higher women’s university enrollment and higher mean achievement were associated with larger girls’ advantages.

text:
Cardiac dysfunction after acute ischaemic stroke: Long-term outcomes from the SICFAIL cohort
On April 20, 2026, International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature published the article “Cardiac dysfunction after acute ischaemic stroke: Long-term outcomes from the SICFAIL cohort” online. The PubMed author list begins with Ungethüm K. Adults with acute ischaemic stroke were consecutively enrolled in the prospective SICFAIL cohort between January 2014 and February 2017. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline. Patients were followed annually by mail or telephone. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause readmission or death. Secondary analyses considered individual endpoints and cardiovascular readmissions. Associations were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Of 696 enrolled patients, 644 (92.5%) had interpretable echocardiographic data.

title: Brunel University of London
text:
Brunel University of London
Brunel University of London (BUL) is a public research university located in the Uxbridge area of London, England. It is named after Isambard Kingdom Brunel, a Victorian engineer and pioneer of the Industrial Revolution. It became a university in June 1966, when Brunel College of Advanced Technology was awarded a royal charter and became Brunel University; it is sometimes considered a plate glass university. In 2014 the university formally adopted the name Brunel University London, and in 2024 became the University of London's 17th member, adopting the trading name Brunel University of London. Since 2014 the university has been organised into three colleges: the College of Business, Arts and Social Sciences; the College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences; and the College of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences.

title: "The community's memory is timeless": exploring cultural and community context to inform the public health response to the overdose crisis in black communities
text:
"The community's memory is timeless": exploring cultural and community context to inform the public health response to the overdose crisis in black communities
On April 29, 2026, Harm reduction journal published the article “"The community's memory is timeless": exploring cultural and community context to inform the public health response to the overdose crisis in black communities” online. The PubMed author list begins with Barnes J. The study used one-on-one, semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of people living or working in West and Southwest Philadelphia. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using thematic analysis. The researchers completed 19 interviews. Participants had a mean age of 46. Women comprised 79% of the sample. Black/AA participants comprised 83% of the sample. Participants reported substantial community stigma toward people who use drugs. Participants emphasized the importance of community-driven initiatives, culturally appropriate services, and expanded outreach to address structural inequities.

title: Rotational Kinematics in the Globular Cluster System of M31: Insights from Bayesian Inference
text:
Rotational Kinematics in the Globular Cluster System of M31: Insights from Bayesian Inference
In “Rotational Kinematics in the Globular Cluster System of M31: Insights from Bayesian Inference”, published on January 12, 2026, Yuan (Cher) Li is the first listed author. The institutional affiliation given for Yuan (Cher) Li is University of Auckland. The article appeared in The Open Journal of Astrophysics. Its other authors are Brendon J. Brewer, Geraint F. Lewis, and Dougal Mackey. The study uses Bayesian modelling to investigate the combined inner and outer globular cluster populations of M31. It examines subpopulations defined by metallicity and associations with substructure. Lower-metallicity clusters and those linked to substructures exhibit a common, more rapid rotation with an alignment distinct from higher-metallicity and non-substructure clusters. Higher-metallicity clusters rotate in alignment with Andromeda’s stellar disc.

title: Characterization and Risk Analysis of Seaweed Farming Ventures in Sorsogon, Philippines
text: Characterization and Risk Analysis of Seaweed Farming Ventures in Sorsogon, Philippines Michelle M. Bongalonta is the first author listed for “Characterization and Risk Analysis of Seaweed Farming Ventures in Sorsogon, Philippines” (2026), with University of Santo Tomas–Legazpi as the institution named for that author. The publication appeared in International Journal of Multidisciplinary Applied Business and Education Research on March 24, 2026. The study analyzed seaweed farming operations and risks using Risk Management Theory. Its data included a survey of 115 farmers in Sorsogon City and Castilla, alongside interviews with stakeholders and experts. The sector was dominated by small-scale and medium-scale ventures, primarily cultivating Kappaphycus alvarezii through fixed-bottom long lines. All farmers accessed government propagules, but only 20% received direct financial support. Typhoons and “ice-ice” disease were environmental hazards driving yield volatility.

title: In situ degradability of king grass (Pennisetum purpureum) supplemented with banana (Musa spp.) varieties
text:
In situ degradability of king grass (Pennisetum purpureum) supplemented with banana (Musa spp.) varieties
“In situ degradability of king grass (Pennisetum purpureum) supplemented with banana (Musa spp.) varieties” was published electronically in Brazilian journal of biology = Revista brasleira de biologia on January 26, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Godoy V. The experiment was conducted at the Rumenology Laboratory of the Faculty of Animal Sciences. It used a completely randomized block design under a 3 × 3 factorial arrangement. The dried King Grass inclusion levels were 50, 65, and 75%. The banana varieties were Valery, Grand William, and Grand Nain. Nine treatments were tested with three replicates each. Data were analysed using ANOVA, with means compared using Tukey's test (P < 0.05). The highest dry matter degradability was observed with 50% King Grass and 50% Grand Nain.

title: Successful rescue of a patient with aortoesophageal fistula secondary to anastomotic leak after esophagectomy
text:
Successful rescue of a patient with aortoesophageal fistula secondary to anastomotic leak after esophagectomy
The article “Successful rescue of a patient with aortoesophageal fistula secondary to anastomotic leak after esophagectomy” appeared online in BMC surgery on January 31, 2026. The PubMed author list begins with Xue M. The case involved a 68-year-old man who underwent minimally invasive McKeown esophagectomy after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and immunotherapy for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Postoperatively, he experienced fever followed by hematochezia and hematemesis. Emergency endoscopy failed to control active arterial bleeding at the inflamed anastomotic site. A repeat enhanced CT scan revealed active contrast extravasation from the descending aorta into the gastric conduit. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed to stabilize his hemodynamics. Ten months after the onset of the fistula, the patient continued chemotherapy and led a normal daily life.
